## The Lords of Easy Money

Source: Christopher Leonard, Chinese edition of "The Lords of Easy Money: How the Federal Reserve Broke the American Economy".

Executive conclusion: This book argues that post-2008 Federal Reserve policy, especially zero interest rates and quantitative easing, did much more than stabilize markets. It changed the distribution of wealth, pushed capital away from safe assets into riskier debt, inflated asset prices, encouraged corporate leverage, and created a fragile financial system dependent on continued Fed support. The book follows former Kansas City Fed president Thomas Hoenig as the dissenter who warned that monetary policy was not just about inflation, but about resource allocation and financial stability.

Core thesis: Zero rates create winners and losers. In a normal interest-rate world, banks, insurers and pension funds can earn returns from safe assets such as Treasuries. In a zero-rate world, safe yields disappear, forcing institutions out the risk curve. The Fed intended this risk-taking to restart the economy, but Leonard argues it also transferred money toward asset owners and Wall Street while encouraging speculation rather than productive investment.

Key mechanisms explained by the book: First, QE lowers Treasury yields by creating huge demand for bonds, pushing investors into stocks, corporate bonds, leveraged loans and structured credit. Second, the system becomes unstable because asset prices depend on Fed purchases; when Bernanke suggested slowing purchases in 2013, the "taper tantrum" showed how fast capital could move back toward safety. Ten-year Treasury yields jumped from around 2.2% before the press conference to 2.73% within weeks, and the Dow fell almost immediately after the announcement. The book treats this not as a random shock but as evidence that QE embedded fragility.

Corporate debt and CLOs are a major case study. Credit Suisse issued 11 CLOs worth $6.7bn from 2010 to 1H14 and became a major dealer. CLOs transformed complex leveraged loans into standardized products that pension funds, insurers, mutual funds and banks could buy by tranche: AAA, mezzanine or equity. This created steady demand for leveraged loans and allowed private-equity-backed companies to refinance repeatedly. Floating-rate loans looked safe to investors in a zero-rate world, but shifted risk to borrowers if rates rose.

The book highlights covenant-lite loans as a direct consequence of yield hunger. Sponsors increasingly demanded looser terms, and buyers accepted them because there was too much cash chasing too few yields. A $1bn loan could attract $2bn in demand. By 2014-2015, junk-bond analysts observed that markets had become detached from economic reality; negative information no longer mattered as long as QE liquidity kept demand strong. Global investment banking fees reached $11.1bn per month in June 2014, above the $10.7bn record set before the 2007 crisis.

Investment implications: The book is a warning against treating low rates as free. Easy money can support asset prices for years, but it also builds hidden leverage, poor underwriting and fragile funding chains. Investors should watch credit quality, covenant protection, floating-rate debt exposure, CLO demand, private-credit leverage and Fed liquidity dependence. It is especially relevant in an AI-capex cycle financed partly by debt and private markets. The core lesson is timeless: when policy suppresses safe yields, returns migrate to assets whose risks may be underpriced until liquidity reverses.

## China Wind Tender Data April 2026

Source: Caixin Data, "Wind Power Watch: April 2026 wind tender data rose sharply month-on-month and year-on-year" (1 June 2026).

Executive conclusion: China's wind-power tender pipeline rebounded sharply in April 2026, suggesting stronger future installation momentum. The near-term demand signal is positive for wind turbine, tower, electrical equipment, EPC and grid-related suppliers, but the report also makes clear that the real constraint is no longer only generation capacity. As wind/solar penetration rises, grid flexibility, storage, transmission channels and market mechanisms become the bottlenecks that decide how much new renewable capacity can be absorbed.

Key data: Caixin/Jiefeng's China Wind Capacity Index registered 140 in April 2026. There were 59 new wind-turbine-related events involving 23,524.93MW of capacity, up 263% month-on-month and 154% year-on-year. For historical context, the April index values from 2018 to 2025 were 94, 113, 91, 119, 136, 125, 128 and 127, respectively, making April 2026 meaningfully stronger than recent Aprils. Four single projects exceeded 500MW, mainly located in Altay, Xinjiang; Zhenglan Banner, Inner Mongolia; and Zhuolu County, Zhangjiakou, Hebei. Purchasers included China Energy Engineering, SPIC, China Huaneng and Shenzhen Energy North.

Winning-bid data show listed-company participation. In April 2026, 20 listed-company/subsidiary wind-capacity winning-bid events were recorded. The top three by number of projects were China Power, MCC and Mingyang Smart Energy, with 4, 2 and 2 projects respectively. Among disclosed wind-related winning bids, PowerChina had the largest single bid at Rmb1.17bn.

National power data support the structural story. By end-April 2026, China's total installed power capacity was 3.99bn kW, up 14.2% year-on-year. Wind installed capacity reached 660mn kW, up 22.0%. From January to April, average utilization hours of power-generation equipment were 925 hours, down 84 hours year-on-year, highlighting the consumption/utilization challenge.

Project filing data: In April, China added 5,692 registered new-energy power projects excluding residential distributed PV. Wind projects numbered 37, totaling 5,565.98MW. Liaoning had 6 projects totaling 1,085.2MW; the largest single project was a 1,000MW wind project in Ar Horqin Banner, Chifeng, Inner Mongolia.

Policy and investment implications: Central policy is pushing non-fossil energy, new storage, green power direct connection, smart microgrids and higher renewable consumption. The 15th Five-Year Plan emphasizes building a new power system. The National Energy Administration says it will support rational consumption of more than 200mn kW of annual new-energy additions by integrating "new energy + storage + grid + market." Key work includes offshore wind, desert/Gobi/wasteland bases, distributed wind/PV, pumped hydro, new storage, gas peakers, virtual power plants, vehicle-grid interaction, ultra-high-voltage transmission and electricity market reform.

Advice: The bullish signal is strongest for companies tied to large-scale wind tenders, grid upgrades, flexible resources, storage and renewable integration, not just turbine volume. Watch whether tender growth converts into installed capacity and whether utilization pressure worsens. Prefer firms with exposure to offshore wind, UHV/transmission, storage dispatch, grid automation and high-quality EPC. Avoid simple extrapolation from tender volume if local curtailment and pricing mechanisms do not improve.

## Tao Law and Semiconductor Beneficiaries

Source: Caixin Data, "Which sectors benefit from Huawei's Tao (tau) law?" (1 June 2026).

Executive conclusion: Huawei's "Tao/tau law" reframes semiconductor progress from geometric scaling to time scaling. Instead of defining progress only by smaller transistor nodes, the new framework optimizes system time constant tau across devices, circuits, chips and systems. The investable implication is that China's semiconductor opportunities should broaden from advanced nodes alone to advanced packaging, testing, storage, interconnect, EDA/IP, equipment, materials and system-level architecture. The market initially chased the whole semiconductor sector, but institutions see the strongest consensus around advanced packaging, testing and memory.

Market reaction and background: Huawei released the tau law on May 25. The CSI Chip Industry Index rose 6% that day, but pulled back in the following days. Advanced packaging outperformed: the Shenwan integrated-circuit packaging/testing index rose for two consecutive days with a 17% cumulative gain across 14 packaging/testing stocks. The reason is that tau law directly points to lower latency, higher bandwidth and shorter data paths, where packaging, chiplets, hybrid bonding and memory proximity matter.

Technical logic: Moore's law was a spatial-scaling framework: shrink transistor dimensions, increase transistor density and improve performance/cost. But after 2005, power scaling from geometry began to fail, and China also faces EUV lithography constraints. CITIC Securities argues that transistor miniaturization ultimately shortened signal transmission paths, so the deeper goal is time reduction. Tau law therefore uses "time miniaturization" rather than "geometric miniaturization" as the target, compressing signal propagation delay through innovations such as logic folding.

Industry data: The broader semiconductor cycle is being reaccelerated by AI. SIA data show global semiconductor sales reached $791.7bn in 2025, up 25.6%. In 1Q26, global sales reached $298.5bn, and March sales rose 79.2% year-on-year; China's March market rose 74.8%. SEMI expects global 300mm wafer-fab equipment spending to rise 18% in 2026 to $133bn and further to $151bn in 2027.

Beneficiary layers: At the device layer, focus shifts to channel mobility, transistor structures, contact resistance and local interconnect RC. At the circuit layer, vertical active-layer stacking, ultra-fine pitch hybrid bonding and critical-path folding reduce wiring and RC delay. At the chip layer, AI's data-movement bottleneck pushes logic and memory closer together; HBM, 3D-stacked SRAM and hybrid bonding become key. At the system layer, Unified Bus, Hi-ONE and 3D Folding lower data-transfer time across chips, racks and systems.

Investment advice: Institutions highlight three layers. First, architecture and design: AI chips increasingly need specialized design and software-hardware co-optimization. Second, advanced packaging and testing: bottlenecks increasingly occur between chips, chiplets, memory and compute. Third, equipment/materials/storage: AI training drives HBM, inference drives data-center storage, and both support long-term equipment demand. GF Securities specifically sees demand for bonding, thinning, etching, deposition, CMP and packaging inspection equipment. CITIC emphasizes hybrid bonding, TSV, multi-layer logic stacking, domestic fabs, electroplating, cleaning, CMP, etching, thin-film deposition, co-packaged optics and domestic advanced packaging.

Risk controls: The article warns that valuation can run ahead of fundamentals. ## Energy: A Human History

Source file: 能源传：一部人类生存危机史.epub
Converted file: 能源传：一部人类生存危机史.pdf
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

This book is a long historical argument about energy as the foundation of civilization. Richard Rhodes does not present energy history as a simple sequence of technological triumphs. Instead, he shows that every energy system solves a previous bottleneck while creating new externalities, dependencies, and risks. Wood solved early heating and cooking needs but caused deforestation. Coal solved the wood shortage and enabled steam power but created mine disasters, urban pollution, and carbon emissions. Petroleum enabled mobility, aviation, mass logistics, and modern agriculture, but produced geopolitical dependency and climate damage. Electricity transformed industry and household life but required large centralized systems. Nuclear power offered extraordinary energy density but brought fear, waste, accidents, and proliferation concerns. Renewables reduce fuel pollution but need grids, storage, land, materials, and reliability management. The book's core conclusion is that the future energy challenge is not just discovering another fuel. It is designing an energy system that can support roughly ten billion people while reducing pollution, climate risk, and geopolitical fragility.

Main structure and arguments

1. Energy transitions begin with scarcity. Early societies depended heavily on wood for heat, cooking, metallurgy, building, and shipbuilding. As populations and urban needs grew, wood became insufficient. The book uses early modern Europe, including Elizabethan England, to show how wood scarcity pushed society toward coal. Coal was not adopted because it was pleasant; it was dirty and difficult. It was adopted because the alternative energy base could no longer support population and production needs.

2. Coal and steam changed the scale of civilization. Coal was first a heating fuel, but its deeper significance came when mining, steam engines, metallurgy, transport, and factories became connected. Mine flooding and ventilation problems created demand for mechanical pumping. Papin's pressure cooker and safety valve, Newcomen's atmospheric engine, and Watt's improvements were part of the same historical chain: energy scarcity created engineering problems, and those engineering problems produced the industrial revolution. Steam was not merely a machine; it was a new way to convert fossil energy into work independent of animal muscle, wind, or water location.

3. Lighting is treated as a major energy revolution. The book pays attention to whale oil, manufactured gas, kerosene, and electricity because the ability to light the night changed work, education, safety, commerce, and domestic life. This is one of the book's important insights: energy history is not only about factories and armies. It is also about daily life, hours of productivity, indoor air quality, and the expansion of human possibility.

4. Petroleum created modern mobility and geopolitical dependence. Oil's energy density made automobiles, trucks, ships, aircraft, and global logistics possible. It also transformed agriculture through mechanization and petrochemical inputs. But the same energy density made oil strategically sensitive. Control of production, refining, shipping lanes, and reserves became central to international politics. Petroleum gave societies unprecedented mobility while making them vulnerable to supply shocks and wars.

5. Electricity is a system, not simply a product. The book shows how electricity required generators, grids, motors, regulation, and large capital investment. Its value came from flexibility: the same network could power light, factories, appliances, communications, and later computing. This matters for the current era because AI, data centers, electric vehicles, and electrified industry are again making the power grid the center of economic strategy.

6. Nuclear power is portrayed as both a miracle of energy density and a social-political challenge. The technology can produce massive reliable power with low direct carbon emissions, but public fear, accidents, waste management, and weapons links have constrained deployment. The book does not treat nuclear as a simple answer, but it does make clear that excluding it entirely makes decarbonization harder.

7. Climate change is the final externality of the fossil-energy age. The book argues that the great benefits of coal, oil, and gas came with accumulated atmospheric costs. The problem is now global and time-delayed: past energy use creates current and future warming, and fast-growing societies still need affordable power.

Data and historical significance

The book's broad quantitative frame is that by 2100 the world may need to support around ten billion people, with much of the demand growth linked to large countries such as China and India. The essential question is not whether humanity can produce enough energy. Historically, humans have repeatedly found ways to unlock more energy. The harder question is whether the planet, atmosphere, cities, and political systems can absorb the waste and risk from how that energy is produced.

Investment and strategic implications

The best investment lesson from the book is to evaluate energy transitions through reliability, density, infrastructure, affordability, and externalities. Ideological narratives are insufficient. The winners in energy transitions are usually companies or systems that solve bottlenecks: mining pumps in the coal age, refining and engines in the oil age, grids and turbines in the electricity age, and today likely storage, transmission, advanced nuclear, gas flexibility, grid software, power equipment, critical minerals, carbon management, and industrial electrification. The book suggests that the next successful energy businesses will not simply produce cleaner energy; they will make clean energy reliable, financeable, scalable, and compatible with existing infrastructure.

## The World Cup and Economics

Source file: 4.The World Cup and Economics_ Big Business, Small Macro
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

Goldman Sachs argues that the 2026 FIFA World Cup will be a very large commercial event but is unlikely to create a statistically meaningful macroeconomic boost for host countries. The title captures the point: big business, small macro. The tournament can matter for selected companies, categories, advertising, travel, lodging, beer, sportswear, retail, airlines, and local activity around host cities. But historical evidence does not support the idea that hosting the World Cup reliably lifts national GDP in a durable way. Investors should therefore separate company-level beneficiaries from exaggerated macro claims.

Tournament scale and data

The 2026 World Cup runs from June 11 to July 19 and is larger than past tournaments. The number of teams expands to 48 from 32. Total games rise to 104 from 64. Stadium capacity rises to about 7.2 million from 3.4 million. The United States hosts 78 games, while Mexico and Canada host 13 games each. This structure creates a larger travel, hospitality, food-and-beverage, and advertising opportunity than a traditional 32-team tournament.

Global audience remains enormous. The 2022 World Cup had about 5 billion people watch at least part of the tournament, and around 1.5 billion watched the final. This explains why sponsors, media platforms, apparel companies, beverage companies, and travel-related businesses care deeply about the event even if the macro GDP impact is small.

Corporate beneficiaries

Goldman identifies several groups of potential beneficiaries. European and U.S. consumer staples are likely to benefit from beer and beverage consumption: ABI, TAP, STZ, HEIN, and CARL are mentioned. European consumer discretionary names such as ADSGn and PUMG may benefit from sportswear and football-related demand. U.S. retailers such as ASO and DKS may see sporting-goods and fan-merchandise demand. Nike is a global beneficiary because of football apparel, team sponsorships, and consumer attention.

Travel and lodging names can also benefit. Hyatt, Marriott, Hilton, Airbnb, and U.S. airlines may receive incremental demand from international tourists, domestic travel, and city-level event activity. These effects are most relevant around host cities and during the tournament window, so the trade is more likely to matter at the company or regional level than at the national GDP level.

Macro evidence

FIFA has suggested that the tournament could boost U.S. GDP by around USD17.2 billion, or about 0.2% of quarterly GDP. Goldman treats this estimate cautiously. Using historical difference-in-differences evidence since 1982, Goldman finds only a marginal positive impact on host-country GDP, and the result is not statistically significant. Long-run effects are essentially zero. This is because World Cup spending often substitutes for other spending, requires security and infrastructure costs, and is temporary. Tourism rises in some places but can crowd out normal visitors or local activity.

The report also notes that winning the World Cup has a more visible short-term sentiment effect. The winning nation's equity market has historically outperformed the global market by about 3.5% in the first month on average. However, this effect fades after about three months. This suggests that World Cup victory can create temporary national confidence and consumer sentiment, but it is not a durable investment thesis.

Probability and market interest

The report includes implied football probabilities. Spain is estimated at around 26% probability of winning, France 19%, Argentina 14%, Brazil 8%, and England 5%. These probabilities matter less for macro investing than for sentiment, sports betting, marketing exposure, and possible short-term equity-market reactions in the winning country.

Investment advice

The practical advice is to trade bottom-up beneficiaries, not host-country macro. Investors looking for World Cup exposure should focus on beverage companies, sportswear, lodging, airlines, advertising, broadcasters, retailers, and local service businesses with direct tournament leverage. The strongest names are not necessarily those in the host country; global brands with World Cup sponsorship and consumer demand may benefit more cleanly. For macro investors, the U.S., Mexico, and Canada GDP impact is likely too small to matter relative to monetary policy, oil, AI investment, employment, and broader consumption trends.

Risks

Risks include overestimating incremental demand, assuming tourist spending is additive when it may be substitutional, weak consumer confidence, weather/logistics disruptions, security costs, and short-lived sales boosts that do not change full-year earnings. The report's final message is disciplined: the World Cup is huge as an entertainment and commercial event, but it is not a reliable national macro catalyst.

Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

Goldman Sachs sees near-term strength in North American energy services as Middle East uncertainty persists, but the report is selective rather than broadly bullish. The strongest change is an upgrade of Expro (XPRO) to Buy from Neutral, with the stock viewed as underappreciated relative to its international exposure and valuation. Goldman also remains constructive on FTI, PTEN, SLB, and HAL, while maintaining a Sell on AESI because market expectations for deployable power appear too optimistic. The key thesis is that geopolitical uncertainty, the need to restore and maintain production, offshore/international activity, and North American demand/pricing resilience support selected oilfield-services names.

Sector backdrop

Middle East uncertainty creates two kinds of demand. First, near-term disruptions or threats of disruption can increase urgency around workover, maintenance, and production restoration. Second, the broader realization that energy security remains fragile supports medium-term investment in offshore, international, and North American capacity. Energy services companies benefit when producers need to keep fields operating, restart production, and develop resilient supply.

However, the report does not recommend buying the whole sector blindly. The best opportunities are where valuation, earnings visibility, international mix, and near-term demand align. Goldman differentiates between companies with improving fundamentals and those where the market may already be pricing too much optionality.

Key stock calls

Expro (XPRO) is upgraded to Buy from Neutral, with a target price of USD19 and upside of about 23.5%. Goldman argues that XPRO trades at about 4.0x 2027 EBITDA despite having an international mix similar to larger peers. The stock had lagged, falling about 15% while peers rose about 4% since the conflict began. Goldman views this underperformance as unjustified. The upgrade is based on valuation, international exposure, and the company's leverage to production restoration and well services.

TechnipFMC (FTI) remains Buy-rated with an USD80 target. At a price of USD69.45, the implied upside is about 15.2%. FTI was down about 8% over the prior month compared with coverage down about 3%, which Goldman views as unjustified. FTI is positioned for offshore and subsea investment, where long-cycle project activity remains supportive.

Patterson-UTI (PTEN) remains Buy-rated with a USD13 target and about 10.8% upside. The case is more North-America-specific. PTEN benefits from North American exposure, improved demand and pricing, and raised guidance. The report sees the company as a way to express near-term North American strength rather than only international offshore.

AESI remains Sell-rated, with a USD14 target versus a price of USD18.04, implying about 22.4% downside. Goldman models deployable power of about 2GW by 2031 but warns that the market may be pricing a much larger opportunity. This is an important caution against overpaying for energy-power adjacency stories without enough proof.

SLB remains Buy-rated with a USD63 target and about 11.4% upside. Goldman views SLB as well positioned for global oilfield activity because of its scale, technology, and international exposure. Halliburton (HAL) remains Buy-rated with a USD44 target and about 9.6% upside, supported by North American and international services demand.

Investment advice

The report's practical recommendation is selective ownership of energy-services names with clear exposure to international/offshore strength, North American pricing, or production restoration. XPRO is the most important upgrade and appears to offer the best valuation re-rating potential. FTI and SLB are higher-quality international/offshore plays. PTEN is the cleaner North American demand/pricing expression. HAL remains a large-cap oilfield-services choice. AESI should be avoided or underweighted because power-related expectations may be ahead of realistic deployment.

Risks

Risks include a faster-than-expected easing of Middle East tensions, lower oil prices, producer capex cuts, North American rig-count weakness, pricing pressure, project delays, and execution risk. For XPRO and smaller names, liquidity and valuation re-rating timing matter. For AESI, the main risk to Goldman's bearish view is if deployable power demand grows faster than modeled. The key monitoring variables are oil prices, offshore order activity, North American pricing, rig counts, workover demand, and evidence of real power deployment contracts.

## Japan Portfolio Strategy Shareholder Benefits

Source file: 7.JAPAN PORTFOLIO STRATEGY Unequal equities - How do stocks with shareholder benefits perform during major market corrections
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

This Goldman Sachs Japan strategy report studies yuutai, the shareholder-benefit programs common in Japan, and finds that companies offering such benefits tend to behave differently during market stress. The main conclusion is that yuutai stocks, especially those whose benefits are tied to the company's core business and those with minimum holding-period requirements, have historically shown better downside resilience during major TOPIX corrections. The report connects this effect to domestic retail investor loyalty, shareholder-base stability, NISA account growth, and the behavioral value of receiving tangible benefits. For investors, yuutai is not only a consumer perk; it may be a signal of sticky retail ownership and lower selling pressure in drawdowns.

What yuutai is

Yuutai refers to shareholder benefits offered by Japanese listed companies, often to domestic retail shareholders. Benefits can include the company's products, vouchers, discounts, meal coupons, travel benefits, retail gift certificates, or other perks. The benefits are often designed to connect shareholders emotionally to the company's products and services. Because many benefits are practical and familiar to households, yuutai can attract long-term retail holders who may be less sensitive to short-term market volatility than institutional investors.

Adoption data

About one-third of liquid listed Japanese companies, defined as those with more than USD5 million average daily trading value, have yuutai programs. The number has grown from about 170 companies to more than 240 between 2022 and 2026. Among companies with market capitalization above JPY100 billion, around 35-40% have such programs. This shows that yuutai is not limited to tiny illiquid companies; it is present across a meaningful part of the investable Japanese market.

Shareholder-base effects

Companies with yuutai programs tend to have nearly twice as many shareholders as comparable non-yuutai companies. The report's logic is that benefits broaden the shareholder base, especially among domestic individuals. A larger and more loyal retail base can reduce realized volatility and selling pressure during corrections. The exact volatility comparison in the report should be read carefully, but the qualitative conclusion is clear: yuutai companies are associated with a more stable shareholder structure and better downside behavior.

Correction performance

Goldman examines ten recent TOPIX corrections of more than 5% peak-to-trough. Across these drawdowns, yuutai companies outperformed by an average of nearly 3 percentage points per correction. This is the central empirical finding. The effect is not about yuutai companies always outperforming in all markets; it is specifically about market stress and downside resilience.

The structure of the benefit matters. During the February-March correction, when TOPIX fell about 11%, companies whose benefits were tied to their core business outperformed TOPIX by about 4.4 percentage points and outperformed other yuutai companies by about 1.9 percentage points. Core-business benefits may create stronger loyalty because shareholders understand and use the company's actual products. Programs with minimum holding-period requirements also tend to outperform because they discourage short-term trading and reward patient holders.

Factor and strategy evidence

A long yuutai-plus-dividend portfolio versus a short no-yuutai-no-dividend portfolio generated an average annual return of about 18% over the past five years. This is a strong result, though investors should not assume it is purely a yuutai effect; dividend policy, company quality, domestic ownership, and factor exposures may also contribute. Still, the finding suggests that shareholder-return policies aimed at households can matter in Japanese equity selection.

NISA and domestic retail backdrop

The report links yuutai to the growth of NISA accounts. NISA accounts exceeded 28 million by the end of 2025. Domestic stocks accounted for about 44% of NISA buying in January-March 2026. Japanese households still hold about 48.5% of assets in cash and deposits, indicating a large potential pool for further equity participation. Yuutai can be a bridge between cash-heavy households and equity ownership because it makes investing tangible.

Investment advice

For Japan equity investors, yuutai can be used as a defensive quality/ownership signal. Prefer companies with core-business-related benefits, minimum holding requirements, dividends, and broad domestic retail appeal. The strategy may be especially useful in corrections or volatile markets. It is not a replacement for fundamental analysis: valuation, earnings, governance, liquidity, and shareholder returns still matter. But in Japan, where household cash balances are large and corporate governance reform is ongoing, yuutai can help identify companies with a more stable shareholder base.

Risks

Risks include confusing correlation with causation, overpaying for low-growth defensive names, policy changes to benefit programs, illiquidity in smaller yuutai companies, and fading outperformance if too many investors crowd into the factor. Investors should monitor NISA flows, retail participation, dividend policy, and whether yuutai programs remain economically meaningful rather than symbolic.

## Meituan NDR Highlights

Source file: 12.Meituan (3690.HK)_ NDR highlights_ Food delivery profit recovery; stable in-store margins; Buy
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

Goldman Sachs reiterates Buy on Meituan with a target price of HKD116, implying about 44.3% upside from HKD80.40. The investment thesis is that Meituan's core food-delivery profitability can recover, in-store/hotel/travel margins can remain stable despite competition, and instant shopping can move toward profitability over time. Overseas expansion remains a near-term drag, especially Keeta's investments in Saudi Arabia and Brazil, but Goldman believes the market is undervaluing the long-term earnings power of the core local-services ecosystem. AI is also becoming more important, not as a generic buzzword but as a tool to improve search, matching, merchant operations, healthcare assistance, and closed-loop service fulfillment.

Valuation framework

Goldman's sum-of-the-parts target is HKD116. Food delivery is valued at about HKD46 per share. In-store, hotel, and travel are valued at about HKD26. Instant shopping contributes about HKD15. The remaining value comes from new initiatives and overseas operations such as Keeta. At HKD80.40, the stock offers about 44.3% implied upside, making it a clear Buy in Goldman's view.

Food delivery

Meituan's food-delivery GTV share remains above 60%, and its share in the RMB30-plus average-order-value segment is around 70%. This is important because higher-AOV orders support better unit economics and merchant quality. The long-term EBIT per order target is RMB1. Goldman forecasts food-delivery volume growth of +2% in 2Q26, +1% for FY26, and +6% for FY27. EBIT per order is expected to be around breakeven in 2Q26, -RMB0.2 in FY26, and +RMB0.6 in FY27.

The food-delivery conclusion is that profits are recovering but competition still matters. If subsidy intensity normalizes and order quality improves, the path back toward positive unit economics is credible. But if competition forces persistent subsidy spending, earnings recovery may be delayed.

In-store, hotel, and travel

For in-store/hotel/travel, Goldman forecasts revenue growth of 8% in 2026, 7% in 2027, and 8% in 2028. Adjusted EBIT margin is expected at 25%, 25%, and 24% across those years. Competition from Douyin and Doushengsheng is a real risk, but Goldman argues that subsidies are not sustainable indefinitely. Meituan's strength is merchant density, user intent, reviews, fulfillment integration, and transaction history. The report implies that while competition can pressure growth or marketing spend, Meituan's platform depth should protect long-term margins.

Instant shopping

Instant shopping remains a growth business moving toward profitability. Goldman forecasts volume growth of 20% in 2026, 21% in 2027, and 18% in 2028. EBIT per order is expected at -RMB0.8 in 2026, -RMB0.4 in 2027, and +RMB0.6 in 2028. The long-term GTV margin target is around 2%. This business is strategically important because it extends Meituan from meals into broader local retail and on-demand consumption.

Overseas and Keeta

Overseas expansion is the largest near-term loss driver. Goldman forecasts overseas losses of RMB2.4 billion in 2Q26, RMB8.8 billion for FY26, and RMB7.0 billion for FY27. Saudi Arabia could become profitable next year, but Brazil depends heavily on competitive intensity. The report recognizes that Keeta can create long-term optionality, but it will depress earnings in the near term.

AI strategy

Meituan's AI efforts include Xiao Tuan search, a health assistant, merchant tools, and LLMs trained on proprietary local-service data. Goldman highlights Meituan's real advantage: in-house local-service data, user reviews, merchant data, logistics, and closed-loop fulfillment. This means AI can improve conversion, merchant productivity, service quality, and user experience in ways that general models may not easily replicate.

Financial forecasts

Goldman forecasts revenue of RMB395.9 billion in 2026, RMB439.7 billion in 2027, and RMB484.0 billion in 2028. EPS is forecast at -RMB0.02 in 2026, RMB3.91 in 2027, and RMB6.74 in 2028. Free-cash-flow yield is expected at -0.4%, 6.6%, and 10.1% across those years.

Investment advice

Goldman's Buy thesis depends on core profitability recovery, stable IHT margins, instant-shopping operating leverage, and overseas losses becoming more controlled. The stock is attractive if investors can tolerate near-term earnings drag from Keeta. Key risks include renewed food-delivery subsidy wars, Douyin pressure in local services, Brazil losses, regulatory changes, weak consumption, and slower AI monetization. The most important monitoring points are EBIT per food-delivery order, IHT margin, instant-shopping loss narrowing, and overseas loss trajectory.

## DiDi Global 1Q26 Review

Source file: 11.DiDi Global Inc. (DIDIY)_ 1Q26 review_ Better-than-expected China Mobility profit; Continued investments in Brazil; Buy
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

Goldman Sachs reiterates Buy on DiDi Global with a target price of USD5.90, implying about 54.1% upside from USD3.83. The core thesis is that China's domestic mobility business is producing better-than-expected profitability, while international expansion, especially Brazil food delivery, is creating near-term losses but long-term optionality. The report is therefore a classic trade-off: domestic China mobility is increasingly cash-generative and margin-improving, but group-level earnings are depressed by aggressive international investment. Investors who believe Brazil and international mobility/food-delivery synergies will eventually scale can use the current loss period as an entry point; investors focused only on near-term consolidated EBITA may be frustrated.

1Q26 results

China Mobility adjusted EBITA was RMB4.0 billion, about 9% above Goldman's estimate and 10% above consensus. GTV margin reached 4.6%, up 0.6 percentage point year over year and a new high. This is the most important data point in the report because it shows that DiDi's core domestic business has strong operating leverage.

Domestic order volume and GTV rose 9% and 10%, respectively. Average order value was positive for a second consecutive quarter. Platform sales margin improved by about 2 percentage points to 23%. These metrics show that DiDi is not only growing orders; it is improving take rate, pricing, or operating efficiency. The domestic platform appears to be moving into a healthier profitability phase.

International investment

International Mobility GTV rose 59%, or 49% constant currency, driven partly by Brazil food-delivery ramp-up. However, adjusted EBITA was -RMB2.9 billion, compared with -RMB3.4 billion in 4Q25. The loss narrowed sequentially but remains large. At the group level, adjusted EBITA fell more than 90% because international investment consumed much of the domestic profit improvement.

This creates the main debate around the stock. Goldman is willing to tolerate near-term group profit pressure because it sees strategic value in international mobility, food delivery, fintech, and local-service synergies, especially in Latin America. But if international losses persist longer than expected, valuation upside could be delayed.

2026 and 2Q outlook

Goldman forecasts FY26 domestic mobility GTV margin of 4.2%, up from 3.7% in 2025. For 2Q, domestic profit is expected to rise about 14% year over year, with GTV margin at 4.6% versus 4.4% previously. International loss is expected at around -RMB3.1 billion. This means the near-term pattern continues: China improves, international remains a drag.

Brazil and strategic optionality

Brazil is a major focus. DiDi is investing in food delivery, and Goldman sees potential synergies with mobility and fintech in Latin America. The strategic logic is that ride-hailing, delivery, payments, drivers, merchants, and consumers can reinforce one another in dense urban markets. If successful, DiDi could build a local-services ecosystem outside China, not only a transportation app. The risk is that Brazil food delivery is competitive and capital-intensive, so losses may stay high before scale benefits become visible.

Financial forecasts and valuation

Goldman forecasts revenue of RMB252.6 billion in 2026, RMB276.5 billion in 2027, and RMB300.4 billion in 2028. EPS is forecast at RMB0.15 in 2026, RMB1.83 in 2027, and RMB3.22 in 2028. The implied P/E is 167.6x in 2026, 14.2x in 2027, and 8.0x in 2028. Free-cash-flow yield is expected at -1.2% in 2026, 4.8% in 2027, and 9.5% in 2028. This forecast profile shows why Goldman is bullish: if international losses moderate, earnings and FCF can inflect sharply.

Investment advice

The Buy case is based on improving domestic China mobility profits, margin expansion, strong platform economics, and optionality from Brazil/international investments. The stock looks inexpensive on 2027-2028 earnings if losses decline as forecast. However, investors should size the position with awareness that 2026 consolidated earnings are distorted by investment spending.

Key risks

Risks include renewed domestic competition, regulatory pressure, weaker Chinese consumer travel, driver incentive inflation, Brazil food-delivery losses, currency volatility, and difficulty achieving cross-business synergies in Latin America. The key metrics to watch are China GTV margin, domestic order growth, platform sales margin, international loss per quarter, Brazil order growth, and whether free cash flow turns positive as Goldman expects.

## Palo Alto Networks 3QFY

Source file: 13.Palo Alto Networks (PANW)_ 3QFY_ Early signs that demand can catch up to expectations
Batch: WeChat File Transfer documents received after 11:25 AM on 2026-06-04

Executive conclusion

Goldman Sachs reiterates Buy on Palo Alto Networks with a target price of USD330, implying about 11% upside from USD297.18. The report's main conclusion is that early signs suggest demand can catch up to expectations, especially as AI expands the security attack surface and drives demand for security operations, cloud, identity, runtime, and application/model protection. However, valuation is already demanding after a strong stock move, so execution must remain excellent. The stock fell about 6% intraday after results despite generally positive metrics, showing that investor expectations were extremely high.

Quarterly reaction and headline data

Palo Alto reported results that were mostly above expectations. RPO, revenue, and next-generation security ARR were 3%, 2%, and 2% above Street expectations, respectively. EBIT margin was 130 basis points above expectations, and EPS beat by about 6%. Fourth-quarter revenue and EPS guidance were 2% and 3% above Street. These are strong results in isolation.

The negative share-price reaction is explained by positioning and valuation rather than a weak quarter. The stock had risen about 100% since the 2QFY EPS report, so the market wanted overwhelming upside. When a high-multiple security stock has already rerated sharply, a merely strong beat can fail to satisfy traders.

AI security thesis

Goldman argues that AI can create new demand across several areas of cybersecurity. In security operations, AI increases both the need for automation and the complexity of threat detection. In observability and runtime security, enterprises need to monitor increasingly dynamic AI workloads. Palo Alto's Koi runtime agentic security offering and Protect AI application/model security capabilities are positioned to address new risks around AI applications, models, and autonomous agents. Agentic identity also becomes important as AI agents act on behalf of users or systems. AI infrastructure creates new network and cloud-security requirements beyond hyperscalers, especially as enterprises deploy hybrid on-premise and cloud AI environments.

Next-generation security metrics

Organic next-generation security ARR grew about 28% year over year, stable versus 2Q. SASE ARR grew about 40% to USD1.6 billion. XSIAM ARR grew about 100% to more than USD600 million. These metrics support Goldman's view that the company is successfully expanding beyond traditional firewalls into platformized cloud, SASE, and security operations.

Product revenue was about 5% above Street expectations. Next-generation firewall bookings rose nearly 40% year over year, driven by hybrid on-premise/cloud needs and enterprise AI infrastructure beyond hyperscalers. This is important because many investors worry legacy firewall products will slow. The report suggests firewall demand can remain relevant when AI infrastructure requires secure network architecture.

CyberArk and AgentiX

The report says CyberArk integration appears ahead of plan and AgentiX has launched. Synergy targets are being pulled forward by about three to six months. This is strategically important because identity security becomes more critical in AI-driven environments, where agents, services, and machine identities can create new privileged-access risks. If Palo Alto integrates identity, cloud, SASE, firewall, and SOC automation effectively, its platform thesis strengthens.

Financial forecasts and valuation

Goldman forecasts revenue of USD11.424 billion in FY26, USD13.790 billion in FY27, and USD15.648 billion in FY28. EPS is forecast at USD3.78, USD4.12, and USD4.68. P/E is therefore high: about 78.7x FY26, 72.1x FY27, and 63.5x FY28. Revenue growth is forecast at 23.9%, 20.7%, and 13.5%. EBIT margin is forecast at 29.1%, 29.3%, and 29.8%. These numbers make the valuation issue clear: Palo Alto is a high-quality compounder, but the market already prices in durable growth and margin strength.

Investment advice

The Buy thesis is that Palo Alto is one of the best-positioned cybersecurity platforms for AI-driven demand, SASE adoption, SOC automation, identity security, and hybrid AI infrastructure. Investors should own the stock if they believe platform consolidation and AI-security demand can support premium growth for several years. However, because valuation is high and the stock has already doubled since the prior EPS report, position sizing should reflect the risk of sharp corrections after merely good results.

Risks

Key risks include valuation compression, slower enterprise security spending, weaker AI-security monetization, integration risk around CyberArk, competition from Microsoft and cloud-native vendors, firewall deceleration, and platform fatigue among customers. The most important monitoring points are NGS ARR growth, SASE ARR, XSIAM ARR, firewall bookings, AI-product adoption, margin stability, and whether management can keep pulling forward synergies faster than investors expect.

> 本合集由 41 篇邮件研报解读合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。

## Asian Equity Perspectives: 台湾升至超配，KOSPI 目标 12,000

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-06-03

评级：台湾→超配；KOSPI 12个月目标上调至12,000；H股→标配；A股维持超配
核心结论：亚洲股市YTD +27%但极度集中——**剔除韩台后MXAPJ实际-4%**。IT板块1Q26 EPS +185%、YTD +93%。台湾：85%市值有AI收入敞口、39% EPS增速、PEG仅0.7。中国：MSCI China连续6年盈利不及预期，EPS预测下调至8%/12%，H股降标配（A股硬科技占比高故维持超配）。
- 韩台杠杆ETF规模数月翻倍——散户投机风险升温，建议零成本put spread collar对冲
可操作结论：买台湾、韩国维持超配（衍生品对冲回调）、中国偏好硬科技而非互联网。

---

## Global Memory: Higher for Longer — 三星/海力士/Kioxia 全面看多

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-05-31

评级：三星买入TP W480,000（+53%）；SK海力士买入TP W3.5mn（+60%）；Kioxia升级买入TP ¥93,000（+41%）
核心结论：**2027年DRAM/NAND/HBM供需比2026年更紧，紧张延续至2028**——市场完全未定价周期长度（存储股仍在中个位数P/E）。三大结构性差异：AI需求可见性空前（服务器/AI占比历史最高）、供给受限（HBM trade ratio吞噬传统DRAM产能）、LTA长约锁定需求。
- 三星2026E传统DRAM ASP +326%；HBM TAM：$56bn→$116bn→$168bn（2026-28E）
- 2027E HBM ASP"补涨"约+50%——最独特的看多观点
可操作结论：mid-single-digit → 9x P/E 重估 + 盈利上修双驱动；三只全买。

---

## Oil Analyst: 霍尔木兹推升成品油利润率

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-06-01

核心结论：霍尔木兹对成品油市场的冲击大于原油——柴油利润率3月底创历史新高，2026年余下时间成品油利润率将维持2013-19均值的2-3倍（柴油超战前预测$19-26/bbl）。全球成品油出口-4.0mb/d；OECD成品油库存趋向历史低点。
可操作结论：持有复杂炼厂与清洁油轮至年底；Q4美国柴油$50/汽油$22每桶利润率是炼化商暴利。

---

上行空间前列：**DoorDash $280 TP（+76%）**、LOAR（+55%）、CWST（+46%）、TPG（+43%）、TSN/GLNG（+33%）、NOW/CSL（+31%）、Celestica（+23%）。
可操作结论：近期催化最强：DASH（结构性盈利）、LOAR（国防航空）、CLS（AI服务器）；防御价值：JNJ/UNH/TSN/CWST。

---

## USA: 职位空缺大超预期；QCEW 暗示就业上修

核心结论：4月JOLTS 7,618k 大超预期（共识6,866k），专业与商业服务+669k为**该类别史上最大增幅**（或与AI相关岗位扩张有关）。QCEW数据暗示2025年12月前就业上修约+180k——**数年来首次方向性转变**（此前连年下修被视为宽松依据）。
可操作结论：劳动力市场比担忧的更有韧性，就业恶化驱动的看跌逻辑被削弱；盯周五非农确认。

---

## Asia Batteries: BTM 储能机遇 — LGES 升级买入

评级：LGES升级买入；三星SDI降级中性（TP仍上调70%）
核心结论：**美国数据中心表后（BTM）储能是韩国电池新结构性需求**：美国ESS TAM上调至2030年~170 GWh（从110）。LGES产能利用率42%（2026E）→67%（2028E），EBITDA翻倍；此前一年跑输同业87%提供入场点。SDI在YTD跑赢121%后估值已满。
可操作结论：买LGES卖SDI的轮动；NCM化学体系+合规+客户关系使韩厂占据BTM主要份额。

---

## China Property 专家会: 结构性分化持续

核心结论：80+城高频数据：上海小户型/低总价领涨（政府收储驱动）、深圳改善型领涨。高租金回报资产价格见底。**库存分化是广泛复苏的根本约束**：领先T1&T2城市9-32个月，其余T2城市14-479个月，T3更高——广泛复苏需以年计。消费者偏好从地段转向品质（物业/社区）。
可操作结论：只买领先城市高品质新盘/超跌中端/高租金回报资产；回避全国性地产beta。

---

## EM Macro Navigator: 科技与能源驱动 EM 分化

核心结论：2026年EM被两大力量撕裂：AI投资潮（利好科技出口国）vs 霍尔木兹能源冲击（重创石油进口国）。重度石油进口国的库存与补贴缓冲正在耗尽——若6月底不恢复将被迫紧缩。
- 推荐：股票超配中国（A>H）/韩国/巴西/南非；外汇做空EUR/HUF、SGD/MYR，做多TRY/NGN/KZT carry
可操作结论：科技型EM（韩台+A股）是明确超配；能源出口国战术多头；重度进口国低配。

---

## JPMorgan（转引）: 港股互联网盈利拐点未至；A股牛市中场

评级：MSCI China 12m目标100（牛市120）；CSI300目标5,200（牛市6,000）
核心结论：A股跑赢由"流动性+盈利预期"双共振驱动：换手率5%+、两融占成交10-11%、Q1新发基金+30%、**外资YTD净流入$13.1bn且正从互联网转向硬科技A股标的**。JPM预测CSI300 2026年EPS +25%。三主题：AI全产业链、能源安全、人形/工业机器人。
- 与高盛结论收敛：A股>H股、硬科技>互联网
可操作结论：两大投行同向验证A股硬科技超配。

entries.title: 投行研报摘要合集（2026-05-26 Selected 系列，35篇）
entries.excerpt: 本合集由 35 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。 FOMC Minutes English standalone summary Source file: 1.USA FOMC Minutes Note "Almost All" Participants See the Committee "Well Pos
entries.body:
> 本合集由 35 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。

## FOMC Minutes

English standalone summary
Source file: 1.USA_ FOMC Minutes Note "Almost All" Participants See the Committee "Well Positioned" at Current Policy Rate.pdf

Conclusion:
The March FOMC minutes show a Fed that is deliberately keeping policy two-sided. Almost all participants agreed that the 3.5%-3.75% funds-rate range leaves the Committee "well positioned" to respond as data evolve. The important change is not that the Fed is preparing to hike immediately, but that the easing bias is being diluted: many participants still think cuts will likely be appropriate in time if inflation cools, while some participants argued for language that explicitly recognizes the possibility of hikes if inflation remains above target.

Key data and arguments:
The minutes say a majority of participants judged the Middle East conflict had increased both upside risks to inflation and downside risks to employment. Most participants said further labor-market softening could warrant additional cuts, while many said higher oil-driven inflation could call for rate increases. The staff GDP forecast was weaker than at the January meeting, reflecting softer incoming data and tighter financial conditions, while the inflation forecast was slightly higher because of incoming price data and higher oil prices.

Labor-market commentary is important. Many participants described the labor market as a low-hire, low-fire environment that is vulnerable to adverse shocks. Several also noted firms may delay or reduce hiring in anticipation of AI adoption. This matters because it gives the Fed a reason to watch employment deterioration closely, but it does not override the inflation risk from energy.

Investment implications:
This note argues against assuming a simple cutting cycle. Front-end rates should remain sensitive to inflation surprises, oil prices, and labor-market data. Duration can rally if employment weakens or oil falls, but the Fed is not giving markets a clean dovish signal. Equity investors should treat the policy backdrop as supportive only if inflation data cooperate. High-duration growth stocks face a valuation headwind if the market prices out cuts or starts pricing hike risk.

Risks to the view:
A quick Middle East de-escalation and softer inflation could restore the case for cuts. Conversely, persistent oil-price pressure or higher inflation expectations could push the Fed toward an even more hawkish stance.

---

## China Industrials Middle East Tracker

English standalone summary
Source file: 10.China tracker_ Middle East crisis - What Chinese corporates are telling us about their operations_ Industrials sector(1).pdf

Conclusion:
The report surveys Chinese machinery, building materials, chemicals, and advanced-material companies on Middle East conflict exposure. The direct demand shock is still manageable, but cost, shipping, feedstock, and second-order stagflation risks are rising. The key conclusion is that the conflict is not yet causing widespread order cancellations, but it is already altering logistics costs, raw-material prices, and pricing behavior.

Key data and arguments:
In machinery, Middle East export exposure varies widely: concrete machinery has the highest exposure at about 35% of exports, while tractors are only around 3%. Companies reported no broad order cancellations so far, though one construction machinery company said regional conflict weighed on 1Q26 demand. The long-term demand story for Saudi Vision 2030 and UAE Centennial Plan remains intact, but prolonged conflict could delay customer decisions and project timelines. Shipping disruption and higher freight costs are the main operational problems. A construction machinery company said every 10% change in steel cost affects product gross margin by roughly 0.5 percentage point. Rubber and tire costs are also rising.

Building-material companies are more domestic China-oriented, so the issue is raw materials rather than end demand. Bitumen prices, tied to refinery byproducts, rose about 33% after the crisis, prompting waterproofing companies to raise ASPs by around 10%. TiO2 prices rose roughly 20% after the crisis, leading coating companies to raise prices by about 3%-15%. PE/PP/PVC prices rose 15%-45%, and pipe companies are passing through costs with a lag of about one month because of inventory coverage.

Chemical companies have Middle East export exposure of roughly 5%-18% in the covered products. The conflict has pushed up feedstock and raw-material costs. Some firms benefit in the near term because product prices rise before inventory costs fully reset, temporarily improving spreads. The main concern is olefins-chain feedstock availability, especially naphtha and LPG imports from the Middle East.

Investment implications:
The better-positioned companies are those with cost-plus mechanisms, FOB terms, overseas plants or assembly capacity, locked-in input prices, and the ability to raise ASPs. Electrification is a medium-term beneficiary because higher oil prices can accelerate adoption of electric machinery and LNG heavy-duty trucks. The worst exposure is commodity chemical companies reliant on Middle East feedstock without pass-through power.

Risks:
A prolonged war could shift the problem from costs to demand destruction. Shipping and insurance disruption could also widen margin dispersion between companies with local capacity and those dependent on China-to-Middle-East exports.

---

## Global Economic Indicators

English standalone summary
Source file: 10.Global_ GS Economic Indicators Update_ Higher Global Inflation in 2026(1).pdf

Conclusion:
Goldman's global indicator update shows a world economy still growing slightly above potential, but with inflation forecasts revised higher after the Middle East energy shock. The macro message is stagflation-lite rather than recession: activity indicators remain resilient, but headline inflation risk has returned and financial conditions have tightened modestly.

Key data and arguments:
Goldman's 2026 global headline inflation forecast has risen to 3.3% since the start of the war, while the global core inflation forecast has increased more moderately to 2.3%. The distinction matters: the immediate shock is energy-led, but the risk is that it leaks into core through transportation, goods, and expectations.

The global ex-Russia Financial Conditions Index tightened 2.2bp over the week, mainly through short rates. This is not a severe stress signal, but it shows monetary markets reacting to higher inflation risk. The Current Activity Indicator remains above potential: the global March CAI is +2.7% annualized versus Goldman's global potential estimate of 2.5%. Developed markets are at +1.9% versus potential of 1.6%, and emerging markets are at +3.8% versus potential of 4.2%. Within countries, the US CAI is +2.9%, China +4.4%, India +6.8%, Euro Area +0.6%, Germany -0.9%, Spain +2.8%, Japan +1.3%, and the UK +0.2%.

Forecast revisions show growth downgrades concentrated in economies exposed to the energy shock and trade channels, including Vietnam and the US in the near-term comparison. Inflation revisions are more widespread, with particularly large moves in countries exposed to food, fuel, or currency pressure.

Investment implications:
This report supports a cautious macro-risk stance. Risk assets can hold up because growth is not collapsing, but duration and rate-cut trades are vulnerable because inflation has moved in the wrong direction. Equities with pricing power, energy exposure, and AI-driven earnings are better positioned than rate-sensitive or low-margin sectors. EM countries with large energy-import exposure face more pressure.

Risks:
If energy flows normalize quickly, headline inflation forecasts could come down and financial conditions could ease. If the shock persists, the inflation revision could broaden into core and push central banks away from easing.

---

## US Consumer

English standalone summary
Source file: 11.Americas Consumer Cyclicals_ State of the US Consumer_ Lower pre-savings DCF for 2026 on higher energy prices.pdf

Conclusion:
Goldman lowers its 2026 discretionary cash flow outlook for US households because higher oil, energy, and food costs are absorbing income gains. The aggregate consumer is not breaking, but the low-income consumer is now much more pressured. The report's most important conclusion is that higher essential spending nearly offsets the benefit from tax cuts and lower interest rates.

Key data and arguments:
Goldman lowers 2026 discretionary cash inflow growth to +4.2%, down from +5.1% in January, and only slightly above +4.1% in 2025. Disposable personal income growth is trimmed to +5.0% from +5.2%, still above the 2009-2019 average of 4.0%. Total household cash inflow is expected to grow +4.6%, helped by expected mortgage equity withdrawal growth of +7.8% and borrowing growth of +10.6%. Financial obligations are expected to ease slightly to 14.3% of DPI from 14.5% in 2025.

The negative surprise is essential spending. Goldman now models essential expenditures growing +7.4% in 2026, versus +2.4% previously and +4.3% in 2025. Energy goods and services spending is expected to grow +12.3%, compared with -4.2% previously, and food spending +6.6%, compared with +3.9% previously. The savings-rate assumption is cut to 4.5% of DPI from 5.6%, which keeps adjusted DCF growth at +4.2%, but this means consumers are using lower savings to defend spending.

The distributional impact is severe. For the bottom income quintile, higher energy and food costs plus SNAP and Medicaid cuts reduce pre-savings DCF growth to just +0.8% in 2026, down from +2.4% in 2025 and much lower than the aggregate +4.2%. Goldman estimates a roughly 50bp aggregate discretionary-spending-power headwind from $100 oil, but about 135bp for the bottom quintile.

Investment implications:
Best-positioned stocks listed by Goldman include DKS, WMT, ULTA, PM, MNST, PEP, STZ, TPR, TJX, ROST, ATZ, ANF, GRGD, CCL, MAR, HLT, DPZ, MCD, YUM, HSY, KR, SFM, and TSN. The theme is quality consumer exposure, value retail, staples, restaurants with scale, and travel/leisure where demand remains resilient. The riskier areas are discretionary categories dependent on low-income spending.

Risks:
A lower oil price would restore spending power. A more persistent oil shock or labor weakness would pressure the bottom quintile further and could hit discretionary retail revisions.

---

## China Base Metals

English standalone summary
Source file: 11.China Commodities_ 2025A earnings review (base metals)_ aluminium, copper and gold; upgrade Chalco-H_A to Neutral(1).pdf

Conclusion:
The China base-metals earnings review is broadly constructive. Copper and gold delivered stronger earnings growth than aluminium, and Goldman expects most covered base-metal and gold companies to produce strong recurring profit growth in 2026. The rating action is also notable: Chalco-H and Chalco-A are upgraded to Neutral from Sell, while Goldman maintains Buy ratings on copper and gold names.

Key data and arguments:
The report covers 11 stocks across aluminium, copper, and gold. All companies reported higher recurring earnings year over year. Aluminium results were generally in line or below expectations. Most copper companies missed Goldman's expectations because of higher costs, while Zhaojin beat because of lower income tax.

Goldman revises aluminium earnings up by 1%-45% to reflect higher SHFE aluminium prices and spreads in 2026E. It raises CMOC earnings by 0%-4% for 2026-2027E because of mark-to-market prices for minor metals. It cuts Jiangxi Copper 2026-2027E earnings by 5%-9% because 2025 copper profitability was weaker, and lowers Zhaojin 2026-2027E earnings by 4%-5% because self-mined gold output was lower.

The 2025 earnings table shows Chalco recurring earnings of RMB14.9bn, up 11% yoy, and Hongqiao recurring earnings of RMB26.5bn, up 1% yoy. CMOC recurring earnings were RMB19.5bn, up 43%; Zijin recurring earnings RMB50.9bn, up 56%; Zhaojin recurring earnings RMB3.70bn, up 126%. Goldman expects 2026 recurring profit growth of 42%-114% across most base-metal and gold companies, driven by higher metal/gold prices and copper/gold output growth of 5%-12% for selected names such as Zijin and CMOC.

Investment implications:
Goldman maintains Buy on copper and gold names, remains Neutral on Hongqiao, and upgrades Chalco-H/A to Neutral. The most attractive exposure is companies with metal price leverage plus volume growth, especially Zijin and CMOC. Aluminium has improved but is more margin/spread sensitive. Gold exposure remains useful in the current geopolitical and inflation backdrop.

Risks:
The main risks are metal price reversal, cost inflation, weaker output, policy intervention, and valuation after strong commodity-stock performance.

---

## Valero Suncor MPC

English standalone summary

Source file: 12.Americas Energy_ Oil_ Takeaways from the Road_ Valero, Suncor and Marathon Petroleum(1).pdf

Conclusion: Goldman remains Buy on Valero, Suncor, and Marathon Petroleum. The report’s core message is that meetings with management teams point to unusually strong refining fundamentals, with US Gulf Coast refiners especially well positioned if Middle East disruption keeps product markets tight. The report distinguishes between paper Brent prices around $110/bbl and cash physical pricing closer to $140/bbl, suggesting that headline futures may understate real physical tightness.

Key data and arguments: Valero’s capital-return framework remains attractive, with management indicating minimum cash returns of 40-50% of CFO excluding working capital. Goldman believes Valero should hold closer to $5bn of cash rather than the $4bn minimum, given volatility. Suncor’s turnaround is also emphasized: the stock rose 99% over the prior year versus XLE +51%, S&P 500 +30%, and TSX +45%. Management’s 11bn incremental resource disclosure helps address inventory-life concerns, and Goldman sees 2028 volume growth of roughly +100 kbpd versus a prior model of +30 kbpd. Marathon Petroleum is framed around operational excellence, West Coast refining, and jet fuel exposure.

Investment advice: Goldman’s bias is to own advantaged refiners and integrated oils with strong assets, disciplined capital allocation, and exposure to tight product cracks. The report highlights Valero, Suncor, and Marathon Petroleum positively, while also noting Cenovus as having the most total return among integrated oils and ConocoPhillips as a Conviction List idea. Main risks are oil-price reversal after a ceasefire, demand destruction if products become too expensive, working-capital volatility, and margins normalizing faster than expected.

---

## China Bulk Commodities

English standalone summary

Source file: 12.China Commodities_ 2025A earnings review (bulk commodities)_ Cement and paper better; steel and coal still weak.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman reviews 20 China bulk commodity stocks across steel, coal, cement, and paper. The sector picture is mixed but more nuanced than a simple cyclical downturn. Cement recurring earnings were better than expected, though forward earnings were cut because construction demand and margins remain weak. Coal earnings were negative year-on-year and below expectations, but Goldman’s coal-price outlook improved enough to raise earnings estimates for some names. Steel remains depressed, but the low base creates selective earnings-revision upside. Paper and packaging were generally better than expected.

Key data and revisions: Coal earnings forecasts were revised up by roughly 3-15%, supported by higher coal and coal-chemical assumptions. Cement earnings forecasts were cut by 7-53% because construction activity is still weak and margin recovery is not secure. Steel estimate revisions were highly dispersed, ranging from -8% to +51%, largely because the starting point is very low. Goldman maintains Buy ratings on Chinacoal, Conch, and CNBM, and upgrades Maanshan-H to Neutral from Sell. In the table, Chinacoal-H has a target price of HK$16 and 18% upside; Conch-H has a HK$28 target and 33% upside; CNBM has a HK$6 target and 24% upside. Shenhua is Neutral, Angang is Sell, and Maanshan-H is Neutral.

Investment advice: The report favors leaders with stronger balance sheets, potential dividend support, and better pricing resilience, especially in coal and cement. It remains cautious on structurally weak steel, except where valuation and a low base justify upgrades. Risks include deeper property/construction weakness, commodity price reversal, policy disappointment, and margin pressure from weak demand.

---

## North America Pipelines

English standalone summary

Source file: 13.Americas Pipelines and MLPs_ Basin Infrastructure and Production Dynamics.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman expects only a moderate US production response despite the commodity rally. The report’s central conclusion is that North American energy infrastructure growth will be concentrated in gas and NGLs rather than crude oil, with the Permian, Canada, Marcellus/Utica, and Haynesville as the most important basins to monitor. Most basins appear unconstrained later in the decade, but Canada crude egress and Marcellus/Utica gas takeaway remain key pinch points. Permian gas also tightens because of higher gas-oil ratios.

Key data and infrastructure details: The report expects high gas growth, moderate NGL growth, and low oil growth. Major projects include Desert Southwest at 2.3 bcf/d by 4Q29; Eiger Express up to 3.7 bcf/d in 2H28; Tallgrass expansion of +1.5 bcf/d in 4Q29; GCX in 2Q26; Blackcomb in 3Q26; Hugh Brinson in 4Q26/1Q27; Haynesville NG3 in 4Q25; Cloud Connector +2 bcf/d in 2Q29; WBI Bakken East +1 bcf/d around late 2030; Speedway +500 kb/d Permian NGL in 3Q27; Bahia +400 kb/d in 4Q27; and multiple Canada-related projects including Mainline, TMX, Express Platte, and MLO2.

Investment advice: Goldman’s framework is constructive for pipeline and midstream companies tied to Permian gas, NGLs, and Canadian egress. TRGP and KGS are notable beneficiaries because rising Permian GOR supports NGL and gas infrastructure needs. The report also implies that producer discipline limits the risk of an uncontrolled oil-supply response. Key risks are faster-than-expected producer activity, project delays, regulatory friction, and demand changes from LNG, power, or industrial users.

---

## China Property Weekly

English standalone summary

Source file: 13.China Property Weekly Wrap_ High frequency data, policy updates, and developer valuation.pdf

Conclusion: China property activity showed a sequential pause during week 14 because of the Qingming holiday, but year-on-year comparisons improved on an easy base. The report does not argue for a structural recovery yet. Instead, it presents a market supported by policy easing and secondary-market resilience, while primary sales, new starts, and completions remain weak. Inventory is still high and developer valuations remain deeply discounted.

Key data: New home GFA was down 1% week-on-week but up 30% year-on-year. Secondary home GFA was down 11% week-on-week but up 31% year-on-year. Year-to-date primary transactions were down 22% year-on-year and down 19%/53% versus 2024/2023 levels. Secondary transactions were down 6% year-on-year but up 25%/2% versus 2024/2023. Inventory months stood at 29.7, slightly below the March average of 29.9. Developers’ offshore and onshore stocks traded at 33% and 22% discounts to 2026 NAV, and both at about 0.5x P/B.

Policy details: Shanghai completed the first secondary-housing trade-in transaction in Jing’an: a 40 sqm unit valued at RMB2.2mn, below the 70 sqm threshold and RMB4mn cap, with a voucher for new commodity housing. HPF easing remains widespread, with more than 50 initiatives year-to-date. Hangzhou raised loan limits to RMB0.9mn for individuals and RMB1.8mn for couples, with priority groups eligible for +70%. Shenzhen allows voluntary HPF contribution up to 12%, while Anhui and Hainan broadened withdrawal uses.

Investment advice: Policy easing supports tactical sentiment but does not yet prove a durable housing upcycle. Goldman’s implied stance is to prefer stronger SOEs and selective quality names while remaining cautious on weaker private developers. Risks include high inventory, weak income confidence, low new starts, and a delayed completion cycle.

---

## Apple App Store China Shipments

English standalone summary

Source file: 14.Apple Inc. (AAPL)_ App Store in C1Q26 and China smartphone shipment trends.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman’s Apple update is constructive but not euphoric. App Store growth modestly accelerated in C1Q26, and China improved, but March decelerated and the US/Japan softened. Goldman maintains Buy on Apple with a 12-month price target of $330, based on 34x NTM+1 EPS. The main positive is services ecosystem durability; the main concern is that App Store growth still sits below Apple’s broader Services guidance and remains exposed to regulation and geographic softness.

Key data: March App Store net revenue was $7.00bn, up 6.2% year-on-year versus +8.7% in February. C1Q26 net revenue was $20.52bn, up 7% year-on-year versus +6% in C4Q25. This is still below Services guidance of about +14%. Non-games revenue grew 14% in C1Q26 and represented roughly 56% of total App Store revenue. Games were down 0.5% year-on-year in C1Q26 and represented about 42% of March revenue, with March games down 1%. Entertainment rose 2%, while Photo & Video rose 15%. By region, the US represented about 35% of total App Store revenue and declined 2% in March; Japan was about 10% and declined 3%; China was about 20% and rose 7% in March and 3% in C1Q26, improving from -2% in C4Q25.

China shipment context: CAICT data showed February China phone shipments of 16.8mn units, down 15%. Chinese brands shipped 14.3mn units, down 16%, while foreign brands shipped 2.5mn units, down 7%, with foreign-brand share rising to 15% from 12% in January.

Investment advice: Goldman stays positive on Apple because services monetization, ecosystem lock-in, and shareholder returns remain powerful. Risks include consumer demand weakness, App Store commission regulation, China competition, supply-chain disruption, and slower Services growth.

---

## China Consumer Durables Middle East

English standalone summary

Source file: 16.China Tracker_ Middle East crisis - What Chinese corporates are telling us about their operations_ Consumer Durables(1).pdf

Conclusion: Goldman’s tracker suggests Chinese consumer durables companies have limited direct revenue exposure to the Middle East, but the conflict still matters through freight costs, shipment timing, petrochemical inputs, and margins. The direct demand impact is generally small because most surveyed companies report negligible to low-single-digit Middle East revenue exposure. However, companies with overseas sales above 30% of total revenue still face operational risk if logistics disruption and input inflation persist.

Key operational findings: The surveyed companies generally report normal production and no severe shortage of raw materials so far. Some appliance shipments have been disrupted, but management teams describe the total impact as controllable. The reason is that many exporters use long-term shipping contracts or FOB terms, which reduce direct exposure to volatile spot freight. Even so, companies warn that prolonged conflict could raise shipping costs and create margin pressure, especially if customers ask for delivery delays or renegotiation.

Cost structure and data: Petrochemical-linked inputs are the most important indirect channel. Companies repeatedly mention plastics, MDI/TDI, refrigerants, TDI, and PU as key raw materials exposed to energy and chemical-price inflation. Some companies have already raised prices, while others may adjust promotions or pricing if cost inflation continues. The report therefore treats the Middle East shock more as a margin and working-capital risk than a direct revenue shock.

Investment advice: Prefer consumer-durables exporters with diversified overseas markets, low Middle East dependence, FOB terms, pricing power, and lower petrochemical intensity. Companies with high plastic/chemical input exposure and weaker pricing power are more vulnerable. Main risks are longer conflict duration, client renegotiation, spot-freight spikes, petrochemical inflation, and demand weakness caused by higher energy prices.

---

## Microsoft M365 Azure

English standalone summary

Source file: 17.Microsoft Corp. (MSFT)_ 3QFY Preview and M365 SOTP analysis.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman keeps Microsoft at Buy with a $600 target price, implying about 60.7% upside from $373.46. The report acknowledges near-term investor concerns: Microsoft shares had fallen 23% since 2Q earnings versus Nasdaq -8%, mainly because of AI capex/ROI questions and fear that M365/Office could be disintermediated by AI. Goldman sees near-term risk/reward as balanced but 12-month risk/reward as favorable, especially if Azure supply normalizes and Copilot monetization improves.

Key estimates: Revenue is forecast at $281.7bn in FY25, $328.6bn in FY26E, $388.2bn in FY27E, and $462.6bn in FY28E. EPS is forecast at $13.83, $16.63, $19.75, and $24.08 across the same years. Azure 3Q growth is expected at 37.5-39.0% constant currency, versus guidance of 37-38%. Goldman expects 4Q Azure guidance around 38% constant currency, roughly in line or slightly below Street because of tougher comps and internal GPU commitments. Capex is a key debate: FY27 capex including leases is raised to $178bn, or $148bn excluding leases, versus prior $164bn and Street $167bn.

M365 argument: Goldman argues M365 disintermediation risk is more than priced in. M365 reacceleration will take time, but Copilot data are improving and E7 general availability in May could help over roughly nine months. The SOTP implies the market may be valuing M365 at only about 4x EV/2027 EBIT, far below broader application software at about 14x.

Investment advice: Own Microsoft for Azure, enterprise AI distribution, Copilot optionality, and underappreciated M365 resilience. Risks include capex ROI disappointment, Azure competition, AI disrupting Office workflows, and valuation pressure if AI revenue ramps too slowly.

---

## PayPay Initiation

English standalone summary

Source file: 18.PayPay Corp. (PAYP)_ Initiation of coverage.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman initiates PayPay at Buy with a $29 target price, implying 38% upside. The thesis is that PayPay is Japan’s leading QR-code payment platform, with category leadership, powerful user scale, expanding financial-services adjacencies, and significant operating leverage. The company is framed not merely as a payment app but as a broader consumer-finance platform that can expand into cards, banking, securities, and potentially overseas opportunities.

## AI Labor Market

English standalone summary

Source file: 4.US Daily_ Breaking Down the Impact of AI on the Labor Market.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman finds that AI is already producing a small but measurable net drag on employment through substitution, partially offset by augmentation. The report combines AI exposure with IMF complementarity scores. Occupations with high AI exposure but low human complementarity are classified as high-substitution; occupations with high AI exposure and high complementarity are classified as high-augmentation. Since ChatGPT launched, labor-market outcomes have diverged between these groups.

Key evidence: High-substitution industries and occupations saw payroll declines and higher unemployment after ChatGPT’s launch. High-augmentation areas saw employment gains and slightly lower unemployment. Goldman estimates the net impact over the past year at about 16k fewer payroll jobs per month and a 0.1 percentage point increase in unemployment. Occupations most at risk: Substitution-risk roles include telephone operators, insurance claims clerks, bill collectors, billing clerks, telemarketers, payroll clerks, legal assistants, procurement clerks, proofreaders, and word processors. These jobs combine routine information processing with lower requirements for human judgment, physical presence, or interpersonal complementarity.

Augmentation beneficiaries: Occupations with high AI exposure but high complementarity include industrial engineers, operations managers, lawyers, physicians, construction managers, and education administrators. In these roles, AI may increase productivity rather than replace the worker.

Distributional impact: Younger and less-experienced workers appear most affected, which matters because AI may hit entry-level white-collar pathways first. Investment implications include possible deflation in some labor costs, stronger productivity for AI adopters, and political/regulatory sensitivity around job displacement. Investors should monitor entry-level hiring, software/services demand, and companies that convert AI into measurable productivity rather than vague automation claims.
