Those positions totaled `KRW 88tn`, or `3.3%` of GDP, at end-2025.

However, Korean bonds have two supports: WGBI inclusion and the AI-driven super-surplus. Goldman tech analysts estimate that 2026 tax provisioning by Korea's two largest chipmakers could jump from `KRW 12tn` in 2025 to as much as `KRW 150tn`. Major semiconductor companies may pay about `KRW 60tn` of interim excess taxes by end-August. Including the `KRW 25tn` already incorporated in the supplementary budget, that would total `KRW 85tn`, more than enough to cover the planned consolidated general government deficit of `KRW 52.7tn` for 2026. WGBI-related flows could total around `KRW 55tn` cumulatively this year.

KRW weakness has been driven mainly by financial flows. Local retail outbound investment surged in Q4; foreign equity investors' hedging demand rose in January; and foreign investors sold Korean equities in March during Middle East risk aversion. In May, USD/KRW moved back above `1,500`, while foreign equity outflows reached a record of about `USD 30bn`. But local retail outbound flows slowed from `USD 10bn` outflows in Q1 to marginal inflows over the last two months. Goldman thinks the improving current account will become more important, helped by memory-company local expansion of `USD 80bn` and interim tax payments. More than `90%` of YTD foreign selling has been concentrated in the two major memory makers, likely due to portfolio rebalancing and diversification rules rather than fundamentals. Diversification-related cumulative selling since end-October is estimated at about `USD 69bn`, and foreign ownership in Korea semiconductors is at a 10-year low.

Policy forecast: Goldman expects two `25bp` BOK hikes in 2H26, in July and October, taking the policy rate to `3.00%` by end-2026. This remains below the previous post-pandemic peak of `3.5%` and far below market pricing near `4.25%` over the next 12 months. Goldman thinks market pricing is too aggressive because the recovery is narrow and underlying inflation is not broad-based. Risks are balanced: longer Middle East energy disruption or procyclical spending of excess tax revenues could force more hikes; energy stabilization and saving of excess tax revenues could limit hawkish repricing.

Investment takeaway: Korea is a mix of AI semiconductor super-surplus, weak non-tech activity, and energy-driven inflation. Bonds should not simply be shorted because tax revenue and WGBI flows can support fiscal and funding conditions. KRW has medium-term current-account and tax-payment support but remains exposed to foreign equity flows and global risk appetite. Korean semiconductors have strong fundamentals but near-term foreign selling and rebalancing remain important variables.

entries.title: 投行研报摘要合集（2026-05-26 Current 49 系列，21篇）
entries.excerpt: 本合集由 21 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。 April FOMC Recap English standalone summary Source file: 1.US Daily April FOMC Recap A “Vigorous Discussion” About the Policy Guid
entries.body:
> 本合集由 21 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。

## April FOMC Recap

English standalone summary

Source file: 1.US Daily_ April FOMC Recap_ A “Vigorous Discussion” About the Policy Guidance(1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman reads the April FOMC meeting as modestly hawkish. The Fed left the fed funds target range and policy guidance unchanged, but the internal balance of the Committee shifted: three participants dissented against the statement’s implicit easing bias, while one dissented in favor of a cut. Chair Powell said the Committee had a “vigorous discussion” about guidance and that more participants could now support moving toward balanced guidance. Goldman’s key conclusion is that the Fed is closer to neutral language, and the risk to the September/December cut forecast is now tilted toward a longer pause.

Key data and arguments: The dissents came from Presidents Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan against the easing bias, plus Governor Miran in favor of a 25bp cut. Powell repeated that the FOMC can “wait here and see.” The pressure to move away from easing bias is tied mainly to inflation upside risks from the war and higher energy prices. Goldman also notes that some policymakers may hesitate to cut even after the war if inflation remains nearer 3% than 2%, even if the overshoot comes mostly from tariffs and energy pass-through.

Investment and market implications: Short rates moved higher, partly because the meeting was taken hawkishly and partly because oil kept rising on fears of a longer Strait of Hormuz disruption. Goldman remains skeptical of hikes, but thinks cuts require labor-market softening. This is bearish for aggressive rate-cut trades and supports a longer higher-for-longer rates stance unless payroll and survey data weaken meaningfully.

---

## Amazon Q1 2026

English standalone summary

Source file: 2.Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN)_ Q1'26 Earnings First Take(2)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman expected Amazon shares to react only modestly at first despite a broadly strong Q1 2026 print. The report highlights reaccelerating AWS revenue, stronger AWS margins, and a Q2 operating-income guide whose high end exceeded expectations. However, Amazon’s stock had already risen 32% in the prior 30 days, so management commentary on the earnings call became unusually important, especially on AWS AI capacity, backlog, consumer health, Prime Day timing, robotics, automation, and fast delivery investments.

Key data: Q1 revenue was $181.5bn, up 17% year-on-year, ahead of Goldman’s $177.2bn, Street $177.3bn, and guidance of $173.5-178.5bn. Segment revenue: Online Stores $64.3bn +12%, Third-Party Seller Services $41.6bn +14%, Subscription Services $13.4bn +15%, Advertising $17.2bn +24%, AWS $37.6bn +28%, Other $1.7bn +25%, North America $104.1bn +12%, and International $39.8bn +19%. GAAP operating income was $23.9bn, 13.1% margin, above Goldman’s $20.5bn, Street $20.9bn, and guidance of $16.5-21.5bn. AWS operating income was $14.2bn, 37.7% margin.

Guidance and valuation: Q2 revenue guidance was $194-199bn versus Goldman $186.9bn and Street $188.9bn. Q2 GAAP operating income guidance was $20-24bn versus Goldman $24.4bn and Street $22.8bn. Goldman maintains Buy, with a $275 12-month target, 5.9% upside from $259.70. Risks include e-commerce/cloud competition, margin pressure from investments, regulatory changes, macro volatility, and failure to scale advertising/cloud/subscriptions.

---

## Microsoft 3QFY26

English standalone summary

Source file: 3.Microsoft Corp. (MSFT)_ 3QFY26 First Take(2)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Microsoft’s 3QFY26 results were fundamentally strong, but Goldman expected the stock to trade lower after hours because investors remained uncertain about 4Q Azure guidance, commercial bookings, and AI capacity allocation. The important debate is not whether Azure is growing, but whether Microsoft can allocate constrained compute across Azure customers, Copilot, and internal AI R&D while sustaining growth against tougher comparisons.

Key data: Total revenue was $82.886bn, 2% above Street and up 18% year-on-year / 15% constant currency. Azure grew 40% / 39% constant currency, ahead of guidance and Street. Productivity and Business Processes grew 17% / 13% cc; Intelligent Cloud grew 30% / 28% cc; More Personal Computing fell 1% / 3% cc, better than guidance. M365 Commercial Cloud accelerated to 15% cc from 14% in 2QFY and beat the top end of guidance by 1 point. M365 Consumer Cloud accelerated to 29% cc from 27%. Adjusted EPS was $4.27, 5% above Street at $4.07. Capex including finance leases was $31.9bn, up 49%, below Street’s expected 63% growth.

AI details: Microsoft disclosed total AI revenue above $37bn, up 123% year-on-year, including Azure AI customer workloads and first-party AI applications/services. M365 Copilot paid seats exceeded 20mn, up from 15mn in 2QFY.

Investment advice: Goldman maintains Buy and a $600 target, implying 41.4% upside from $424.46. Key positives are Azure growth, Copilot adoption, and possible AI infrastructure economics. Risks include slower internal silicon ramp, spending outside Azure, leadership changes, and AI/custom software disrupting Microsoft’s applications business.

---

## Oil Tracker Hormuz Low Flows

English standalone summary

Source file: 4.Oil Tracker_ Downside Risks to Supply and Demand as Hormuz Flows Remain Low(1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman’s oil tracker shows a market still dominated by extreme Strait of Hormuz disruption, but with emerging downside risks to both supply and demand. Prompt Brent and WTI were up 17% and 15% week-on-week to $118/$107, the highest levels since June 2022. The main physical stress remains low Persian Gulf flow, but visible inventories stopped drawing in late April, possibly indicating larger demand destruction or invisible non-OECD product-stock draws.

Key data: Estimated oil exports through the Strait fell to 4% of normal on a four-day moving average. Goldman estimates a net hit to global commercial oil stocks of 12.6 mb/d before demand and production response, and a total hit to Persian Gulf oil flows of 14 mb/d. US weekly crude exports rose to a record 6.4 mb/d, supporting Western crude and product benchmarks. Brent/WTI timespreads strengthened and East-West refined-product price differentials narrowed, showing tightness spreading from Asia toward Western markets.

Demand and supply risks: Goldman estimates April global oil demand was 3.6 mb/d weaker than February, concentrated in jet fuel and petrochemical feedstocks, though US gasoline remained robust. China state refiners reportedly saw retail product sales 10-20% lower year-on-year in April. On Iran, Kpler data suggest no loaded Iranian oil tanker exited the blockade, loadings were 1 mb/d below 2025 average, and Iran storage could last only 12-22 days, with production cuts possibly rising to 1.5 mb/d by mid-May.

Investment implications: Oil/product tightness remains supportive for crude prices, refiners, and product cracks, but visible demand destruction is now a serious risk. Longer blockade raises supply-scar and inflation risk; faster reopening would compress risk premium sharply.

---

## FOMC Statement Dissent

English standalone summary

Source file: 5.USA_ FOMC Leaves Fed Funds Rate Unchanged; Three Participants Dissent From “Easing Bias” in the Post-Meeting Statement and On...(1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: This shorter Goldman FOMC note records the immediate policy decision: the FOMC left the fed funds target range unchanged at 3.5-3.75% at the April meeting, kept the March policy guidance intact, but revealed a divided Committee. The headline is that three participants objected to the “easing bias” embedded in the statement, while one participant wanted an immediate 25bp cut.

Key facts: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan dissented from the easing bias in the statement. Governor Stephen Miran dissented from the decision itself because he preferred a 25bp cut. The guidance sentence remained unchanged and continued to say the Committee would base the “extent and timing of additional adjustments” on incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

Inflation/labor wording: The statement changed inflation language from “remains somewhat elevated” to inflation “is” elevated, partly because higher oil prices had become a clearer problem. It also changed the labor description to say job gains had “remained low, on average” rather than simply “remained low,” likely reflecting volatility in payroll growth.

Investment implications: The note points to a Fed that is not ready to cut and is becoming more uncomfortable with pre-committing to easing. The dissent mix matters: inflation hawks are growing more vocal, while dovish pressure still exists. Rates markets should treat near-term cuts as data-dependent and vulnerable to delay if oil and tariffs keep inflation elevated.

---

## China Private Tech Tour

English standalone summary

Source file: 6.Private-Tech Tour 2026 Review_ Founders' visits_ Top 10 takeaways in AI infra & software, Quantum computing, Satellite, BCI, ...(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman’s China Private Technology Tour points to broadening AI infrastructure and application demand in China. The tour covered foundation models, AI agents, HarmonyOS AI software, distributed AIGC computing, AI servers, AI chips, memory, optical chips, robotaxi, LEO satellites, quantum computing, and non-invasive BCI. The central message is that China’s AI opportunity is shifting from model launch headlines to physical infrastructure, enterprise agent adoption, localization, and specialized deep-tech commercialization.

Key takeaways: Optical-networking demand is growing strongly, with China 800G+ optical-module growth expected to be triple-digit from a low base in 2027, while global growth is mid-double-digit. AI superpods become a key 2026 China driver, expanding from 64 GPUs to 256/1,024 GPUs and creating opportunities in compute and networking. China AI server demand skews more toward inference than the US because many foundation models are open-source and less training-intensive. China’s 15th Five-Year Plan targets 90% GenAI penetration by 2030, supporting AI infrastructure spending.

Hardware and software details: Local AI chips focus on GPGPU, ASIC, general GPU, and new RPP architecture for inference, aiming at better power efficiency, flexibility, and memory. Enterprise AI agents are being used for manufacturing engineering know-how, yield ramp-up, factory duplication, marketing, and CRM. Consumer AI applications focus on multimodal content generation and personal assistants. Quantum computing remains less mature than GPUs but China has relatively high self-sufficiency across superconducting, NMR, cold atom, and photonic approaches. Robotaxi operators expect accelerated 2026/27 fleet growth with overseas expansion.

Investment implications: The strongest read-throughs are optical modules, AI servers, localized chips, memory controllers/AI SSDs, enterprise software, robotaxi, satellites, and BCI. Beneficiaries include local AI infrastructure supply chains and software vendors tied to real enterprise deployment.

---

## Private Credit Cracks

English standalone summary

Source file: 7.Top of Mind_ Cracks in private credit(3).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman’s Top of Mind issue asks whether private credit stress could become systemic. The answer from Howard Marks, Michael Arougheti, Bruce Richards, Amanda Lynam, and Goldman specialists is mostly “not systemic,” but with meaningful disagreement about the near-term default cycle. The stress is real: high-profile defaults, concerns over inflated valuations, retail redemption requests, and heavy software exposure have damaged confidence. But the structure of private credit, especially locked-up capital and limited fund leverage, reduces the risk of forced fire sales.

Systemic-risk argument: Arougheti and Lynam argue worries are concentrated in non-traded BDCs, which are only a modest part of private credit. Limited liquidity is a feature because it prevents a bank-run dynamic. Goldman also notes private credit funds have limited leverage, bank exposure is generally secured/protected, and even a sharp rise in default rates would only moderately affect new lending to the private sector. The comparison to the Global Financial Crisis is therefore viewed as exaggerated.

Software risk debate: Bruce Richards is the most bearish. He argues software loans are 3% of the high-yield bond market, 13% of broadly syndicated loans, but 23% of private credit, creating excessive concentration. He expects very high software-sector default rates in 2027-2029, peaking around 15%, with double-digit defaults in each year and loss rates of 70-100% on some software loans. Arougheti and Lynam are less worried because loans are senior secured and often backed by large cash-generative companies.

Investment advice: Private credit likely survives and keeps growing, but dispersion between managers should rise sharply. Institutional/opportunistic credit may benefit as retail-focused strategies slow. Favor high-quality alternative asset managers with disciplined underwriting and diversified credit platforms; avoid assuming private credit is risk-free simply because systemic risk appears limited.

---

## Energy Costs Inflation Outlook

English standalone summary

Source file: 8.US Economics Analyst_ Higher Energy Costs, International Spillovers, and the Inflation Outlook(1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman raises its US inflation forecasts because higher energy costs and international spillovers from the Middle East shock are now larger than previously expected. The baseline assumes oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz normalize only by end-June, with about 0.5 mb/d of lasting Gulf production damage. Brent is expected to average $100/bbl in April and May before falling to $90 by 4Q26, with risks skewed upward.

Scenario data: In a benign case, flows recover by mid-June with no lasting damage and Brent falls to $80 by 4Q26. In an adverse case, normalization is delayed until end-July, Brent reaches $125 in May and $100 by Q4. In a severely adverse case with 2.5 mb/d lasting capacity loss, Brent reaches $145 in May and $120 by Q4.

Inflation impact: Goldman’s commodity pass-through framework now implies a 0.35 percentage point boost to core PCE and a 1.25 percentage point boost to headline PCE this year, capturing energy, food via fertilizer, and other Gulf-related non-energy exports. Foreign energy cost spillovers through import prices are expected to add about 0.1 percentage point to US core inflation in the baseline. The effect is modest because Asia and Europe export many finished consumer goods whose prices are less energy-sensitive.

Forecast changes: Goldman raises December 2026 core PCE to 2.6% year-on-year from 2.5%, and headline PCE to 3.4% from 3.1%. In adverse/severely adverse cases, core PCE rises to 2.7%/2.9%, and headline PCE to 3.7%/4.3%. Investment implication: inflation risk limits Fed easing, especially if supply-chain disruptions move beyond air freight into diesel, fertilizer, chemicals, and intermediate goods.

---

## SK Hynix

English standalone summary

Source file: 9.SK Hynix Inc. (000660.KS)_ Key takeaways from the post-earnings virtual group meeting(2)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman reiterates Buy on SK Hynix after a post-earnings virtual group meeting. The key message is that memory supply remains tight, pricing is favorable, HBM4 timing is unchanged, SOCAMM2 mass production has begun, capex is increasing to meet demand, and long-term agreements are being discussed to stabilize demand. Goldman views Hynix as one of the best ways to own the 2026 memory upcycle.

Key takeaways: Hynix said PC and mobile customers are struggling to secure enough volume, while server customer inventories continue to decline even after meaningful capacity allocation toward server demand. All customer groups are trying to secure more volume, and management expects shortages and favorable pricing to persist. Goldman recently raised blended DRAM/NAND ASP assumptions, with both expected to grow close to 3x year-on-year this year.

HBM and SOCAMM: Hynix confirmed no change to the HBM4 schedule, targeting mass-scale shipment and ramp-up through 2H26 in line with customer schedules. It will allocate capacity with a long-term approach rather than short-term profit maximization. SOCAMM2 mass production has started: a 1cnm LPDDR5X-based 192GB SOCAMM2 for the Vera Rubin platform, with twice the bandwidth and over 75% better power efficiency than conventional server DRAM modules.

Capex and valuation: Goldman raises 2026/2027/2028 capex estimates to W44tn/W53tn/W55tn from W40tn/W43tn/W49tn, mainly for DRAM, Yong-in fab construction, and M15X ramp. The 12-month target price is W1,800,000, based on 2.9x average 2026/27E P/B, implying 38.5% upside from W1,300,000. Risks are memory S/D deterioration, weaker smartphones/PCs/servers, Samsung HBM progress, and lower AI capex.

---

## JPY Funding

English standalone summary

Source file: 10.FX in Focus_ Verbal Intervention Not Enough to Challenge JPY Funding(1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman argues that Japanese verbal intervention is not enough to undermine the yen’s role as a tactical funding currency. The trade-weighted yen is at its weakest level since the early 1990s and the Ministry of Finance has become more vocal about currency weakness, but the case for imminent direct FX intervention is weaker than in 2024 or even the January 2026 rate-check episode.

Intervention framework: Goldman says three usual prerequisites matter: a rapid move to very weak levels, dislocation from fundamentals, and forceful verbal intervention. Two of the first two conditions look less compelling now. On a real trade-weighted basis versus its 10-year rolling average, the yen is about 24% below average, still short of the 26-27% deviation before the 2024 interventions. The recent move has not been rapid, and volatility has been subdued. The condition would be more likely met if USD/JPY quickly rose to 163-164.

Model and positioning: USD/JPY has traded broadly in line with Goldman’s GSBEER model, unlike 2024 when it underperformed model-implied value by 4-6% before interventions. Positioning also does not show excessive speculative short yen. Futures positioning is not extremely short JPY, and options positioning suggests net long JPY versus USD, partly because investors already expect intervention risk. This makes immediate action less likely.

Investment implications: Goldman sees more depreciation pressure in an energy-led inflation shock if risk sentiment remains supported, making yen funding attractive tactically. However, recession risk would create asymmetric yen-strength risk. Direct intervention probability rises if USD/JPY breaks quickly toward 163-164 or if JGB/UST volatility spikes again.

---

## AI Project Pulse

English standalone summary

Source file: 11.Americas Technology_ Hardware_ AI Project Pulse_ April 2026 (1)(1).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman’s April 2026 AI Project Pulse shows that AI infrastructure demand is broadening from hyperscaler training clusters to agentic inference, neoclouds, sovereign AI, and enterprise on-premise deployments. The report is a project tracker, not a full market sizing report, but the message is clearly constructive for enterprise hardware vendors with AI servers, storage, networking, and financing capabilities.

Key themes: Agentic AI demand is driving elevated GPU rental pricing and strong demand for CPU-dense servers. Autonomous agents need persistent, high-performance inference, pushing enterprises to upgrade on-premise infrastructure. This is a tailwind for Buy-rated DELL, HPE, PENG, NTAP, and distributors such as SNX, with Neutral-rated INGM also exposed.

Important projects: Dell announced a $1.44bn agreement with Boost Run to scale AI infrastructure. Microsoft took over capacity originally intended for OpenAI at Stargate Norway, securing 30,000 Nvidia Rubin GPUs at a 1GW data center in Narvik, with additional compute in 2027. CoreWeave and Meta announced a $21bn multi-year AI infrastructure agreement through December 2032 using Nvidia Vera Rubin. OpenAI paused a UK data center project because of regulation and energy costs. Sovereign/enterprise examples include Naver Cloud/HanmiGlobal targeting overseas data centers, Bell/Celestica building Canadian sovereign AI infrastructure, Dell EMC’s $984mn US Air Force IDIQ contract, and LKS Attorneys using Dell AI Factory for a legal assistant that improves lawyer productivity by 40% and accelerates case preparation by 50%.

Investment advice: Goldman raises DELL target to $230 from $215, HPE to $32 from $30, and PENG to $33 from $25. Dell customer wins from February-April total at least $9bn by Goldman estimates. Risks include PC/IT demand weakness, white-box competition, input costs, AI server cyclicality, and weaker neocloud demand.

---

## DRAM Sentiment Indicator

English standalone summary

Source file: 12.GS DRAM Sentiment Indicator_ Apr. 2026_ DDR5 spot pricing recovers, while 2027 HBM pricing expectations rise(2).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman’s April 2026 DRAM Sentiment Indicator moved up to “moderately positive” from “slightly positive” in March. The improvement is driven by DDR5 spot-price recovery, extreme strength in Taiwan DRAM/server supply-chain revenues, all-time-high Korean DRAM exports, and higher investor expectations for 2027 Hynix HBM pricing. The only meaningful negative is weak China smartphone shipments.

Key data: DRAM spot pricing was flat sequentially but up 596% year-on-year. Server ODM revenue rose 37% month-on-month and 79% year-on-year in March, driven by rack-level AI server shipments and ASIC AI servers. Aspeed revenue rose 22% month-on-month and 64% year-on-year. Korea DRAM export revenue rose 32% month-on-month and 265% year-on-year, reaching an all-time high. Nanya revenue rose 16% month-on-month and 560% year-on-year, marking eight consecutive months of triple-digit growth. Supreme Electronics revenue rose 71% month-on-month and 192% year-on-year.

Pricing details: DDR4 pricing declined 4% from March 18 but still traded at a 103% premium to March contract pricing. DDR5 had declined until early April but recovered 4% afterward and traded at a 24% premium to March contract pricing. Goldman estimates 2Q26 DRAM blended ASP for Samsung/Hynix rises around 40% quarter-on-quarter, but the second derivative of ASP growth is negative at about -38 percentage points.

HBM view: Consensus for Hynix’s 2027 HBM pricing rose to +19% year-on-year from +2% in March, likely because strong conventional DRAM pricing may affect future HBM negotiations. Investment implication: sentiment supports memory leaders, especially Hynix and Samsung, but smartphone weakness and pricing second-derivative slowdown are risks.

---

## Qualcomm

English standalone summary

Source file: 13.Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM)_ First Take_ In-line quarter with weak guidance, driven by smartphone downside(2).pdf
Duplicate note: Three exact duplicate files were selected; this report is summarized once.

Conclusion: Goldman expects Qualcomm shares to trade lower after an in-line quarter but weak guidance. The problem is not the reported quarter, which was broadly in line with Street expectations, but the forward guide: handset revenue is pressured by memory pricing and smartphone demand weakness. Strength in Automotive and IoT only partly offsets the smartphone downside.

Quarterly results: Qualcomm reported FY2Q26 revenue of $10.599bn, slightly above Goldman’s $10.544bn and Street’s $10.576bn. Gross margin excluding SBC was 54.7%, slightly below Goldman’s 54.8% and Street’s 55.0%. Non-GAAP EBT was $3.246bn, 2.3% above Goldman and 1.5% above Street. EBT margin was 30.6%, above expectations. EPS excluding SBC was $2.65, 3.6-3.7% above Goldman and Street at $2.56. QCT revenue was $9.076bn, slightly below estimates. Within QCT, Handsets revenue was $6.024bn, in line; Automotive was $1.326bn, slightly below Goldman but above Street; IoT was $1.726bn, below both.

Guidance: FY3Q26 revenue guidance was $9.6bn, well below Goldman’s $10.522bn and Street’s $10.257bn. EPS excluding SBC guidance was $2.20, below Goldman’s $2.53 and Street’s $2.46. QCT guidance of $8.2bn was 10.7% below Goldman and 8.4% below Street.

Investment advice: Goldman is Neutral on Qualcomm with a $135 target, implying 10% downside from $150. Upside risks are datacenter CPU traction, smartphone share stabilization/gains, and ARM PC success. Downside risks are greater smartphone share loss and slower Automotive/IoT ramp.

---

## Barron's May 4 2026

English standalone summary

Source file: Barron's_0405.pdf

Conclusion: This Barron’s issue is organized around market adaptation to AI, war-driven energy volatility, and stock-specific opportunities after a turbulent macro period. The cover story argues that Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser’s turnaround is beginning to take hold, but investors still need proof that restructuring, capital discipline, and revenue improvement can translate into durable rerating. The issue also repeatedly returns to the question of which companies can turn instability into pricing power or strategic advantage.

Major articles and investment ideas: “4 Ways to Invest Alongside Bill Ackman” reviews Pershing Square USA and related vehicles under Bill Ackman’s umbrella. “Palo Alto Is Protected From the AI Threat” argues that global demand for advanced cybersecurity software can help Palo Alto stock rise about 30%. “Renewables Get Fresh Attention Due to War” says high fossil-fuel prices are reviving clean-energy interest and highlights three stocks to consider while warning investors to avoid weaker renewable plays. “Fertilizer-Inflation Fallout” says higher input costs create winners and losers in agriculture; Nutrien, Corteva, and AGCO look safer than CF Industries, Mosaic, and Tyson.

Macro and market themes: Rick Rieder is described as confident in Kevin Warsh’s Fed leadership and optimistic about AI spending’s broad benefits. Adam Parker of Trivariate Research is bullish on healthcare and bearish on software, with Labcorp cited as attractive. The Trader section argues earnings are fueling market gains, so “sell in May” may be premature. International coverage flags oversold German stocks. Retirement coverage discusses positioning for a Warsh-led Fed and inflation risk.

Investment implication: The issue favors selective stock picking over broad market calls. AI beneficiaries, cybersecurity, healthcare, energy-security/renewables, agriculture inputs, and financial turnaround stories are recurring areas of interest, while retail investors are warned about complex high-yield products such as autocallable ETFs and about unsustainable dividends such as Western Union.

---

## APAC Energy Security

English standalone summary

Source file: BofA Securities-Energy~Asia Pacific （HA）：APAC energy security~resilience，challenges and opportunities-260421.pdf

Conclusion: BofA argues that APAC energy security is now a central investment theme after the Strait of Hormuz shock. APAC relies on imports for about 81% of oil consumption and about 25% of fossil-fuel consumption. Middle East oil accounts for roughly 60% of APAC oil imports. Japan, Singapore, and Korea are most vulnerable because of 100% fossil-fuel dependence and high petrochemical naphtha reliance. China is best positioned because of high oil stocks, coal and coal-power capacity, high EV penetration, and complete chemical/solar value chains.

Short-term implications: Oil flows through Hormuz fell from about 20 mb/d pre-conflict to 2 mb/d in March, while global oil supply dropped 10 mb/d, about 10%. BofA’s commodity team raised 2026 Brent to $92.5/bbl from $60/bbl pre-conflict, assuming a 4.0 mb/d supply deficit in 2Q and 2.5 mb/d in 2H. Inventory outside the Persian Gulf fell 6.6 mb/d in March. BofA recommends Buy on PetroChina, ONGC, and PTTEP for oil exposure; China Shenhua, Coal India, and Whitehaven for coal; and warns that Korea/Japan naphtha users such as Lotte Chem are hurt, while coal/ethane feedstock users such as Yankuang and Wanhua benefit.

Long-term beneficiaries: Energy diversification should drive thermal power, nuclear, ESS, lithium, EVs, grid construction, power equipment, and tankers. BofA sees China non-fossil at 55% of power generation by 2030 versus 41% in 2025, global BESS CAGR of 29% in 2024-2030, China transformer exports +30% year-on-year in 2026, and EV penetration in Greater China/Korea/Japan at 62%/21%/24% by 2030.

Stock picks: Dongfang, Doosan, Goldwind, Zhongtian, NTPC; Sungrow, Ganfeng, Tianqi, LGES; CATL and Geely; Sieyuan, Nari, Huaming, Jinpan, LS Electric, HD Hyundai, Power Grid; COSCO Shipping Energy for tankers.

---

## China Medtech Surgical Robots

English standalone summary

Source file: Goldman Sachs-CHINA MEDTECH GOING GLOBAL：Assessing the opportunity for surgical robots~global expansion beyond ISRG’s core markets-260421_加水印.pdf

Conclusion: Goldman sees laparoscopic surgical robots as one of the most attractive global expansion opportunities for Chinese medtech companies. The market has a proven razor-and-blade model, long-duration growth, and meaningful underpenetration outside the US. Chinese firms are unlikely to challenge Intuitive Surgical’s US leadership near term, but they can scale as value-oriented challengers in price-sensitive ex-US markets where ISRG’s ecosystem advantages are less entrenched.

Market size and data: Goldman expects the global endoscopic surgical robot TAM to grow from about $11bn in 2025 to $42bn by 2035, a 14% CAGR. Around 45% of the 2035 TAM should come from outside-US markets. ISRG’s global installed base reached 11,106 systems in 2025, versus cumulative orders of 220+ for MicroPort MedBot and 120+ for Edge Medical as of March 2026. In 2025, ISRG recorded 734 overseas system sales, while MedBot secured 100+ overseas orders and Edge Medical 70+, showing early catch-up momentum.

Why Chinese players can win: Chinese systems typically price equipment and consumables at a 30-40% discount to da Vinci, creating earlier hospital break-even and higher IRR. They also offer remote surgery, modular designs, Edge Medical’s 3-in-1 solution, and lower-cost versions for emerging markets. Goldman’s stress tests show Chinese vendors can maintain positive cash margins even with 75-85% price cuts.

Competitive view: ISRG’s moat is less about patents and more about scale, data, digital ecosystem, installed base, and procedure experience. Earlier patent waves have largely expired or are circumventable, but ISRG’s system integration remains powerful.

Investment advice: Goldman favors MicroPort MedBot (Buy) for global commercial infrastructure and Edge Medical (Buy) for multi-port plus single-port strategy and distributor-led overseas execution. It expects MedBot and Edge to capture about 5.4% and 4.1% of global TAM by 2035E.

---

## Agentic AI Hardware Beneficiaries

English standalone summary

Source files: MS-Greater China Technology Hardware Agentic AI - Greater China Hardware Beneficiaries-_加水印.pdf; MS-Greater China Technology Hardware Agentic AI - Greater China Hardware Beneficiaries-)_加水印.pdf
Duplicate note: The two selected Morgan Stanley hardware reports appear to be the English original and a machine-translated/watermarked version of the same report, so they are merged into one draft.

Conclusion: Morgan Stanley argues that the rise of agentic AI will benefit Greater China hardware suppliers because CPU demand becomes more important as the coordination layer for AI agents. The report’s key beneficiaries are ABF substrates, PCBs, CPU sockets, peripheral connectors/cables, passive components, and server assemblers. Covered beneficiaries include Unimicron, NYPCB, Lotes, FIT Hon Teng, Yageo, Gold Circuit, Shennan Circuits, Shengyi, Wiwynn, Inspur, and Lenovo.

ABF thesis: Agentic AI expands server CPU TAM and widens the 2030 ABF substrate undersupply gap to about 15%, versus Morgan Stanley’s prior forecast of about 7%. This implies an incremental 8 percentage point widening. ABF substrate market demand is forecast to reach about $16bn by 2030, a 17.9% CAGR over 2025-2030 versus the prior 16.1%. Agentic AI alone could broaden server CPU ABF substrate TAM by about $1.2bn and drive 5-10% incremental ABF demand. Unimicron is the main beneficiary, while NYPCB benefits through networking-chip ABF exposure and Zhen Ding gains new-entry opportunities.

Other components: CPU socket demand rises with server CPU TAM. Lotes and FIT are the largest beneficiaries because Morgan Stanley estimates they hold 70-80% combined global supply share. Both also supply DRAM connectors and PCIe cables/connectors. Passive components also benefit: a 10-15mn increase in CPU TAM by 2030 could add 2-3% to global MLCC market value, supporting Yageo. More CPUs also require more servers, benefiting ODM/OEMs such as Wiwynn, Inspur, and Lenovo.

Investment actions: Morgan Stanley keeps Unimicron and NYPCB Overweight, raises Unimicron PT to NT$785 from NT$550 and NYPCB to NT$850 from NT$515. FIT remains Overweight with PT HK$9.60 from HK$7.40. Lotes remains Equal-weight but PT rises to NT$2,400 from NT$1,585.

---

## TIME May 11 TIME100 Companies

English standalone summary

Source file: Time_1105.pdf

Conclusion: TIME’s May 11, 2026 issue is built around the 2026 TIME100 Companies list and the role of narrative, leadership, AI, and geopolitical volatility in shaping corporate influence. The cover package highlights Alphabet/Sundar Pichai, Rhode/Hailey Bieber, Beast Industries/MrBeast, Nvidia, Anthropic, Novo Nordisk, Kalshi, SpaceX, Toyota, and many others. The issue argues that influential companies are not only those with scale, but those that tell a compelling story and organize products, users, and capital around it.

Alphabet/Pichai thesis: The central business profile is Sundar Pichai’s reinvention of Alphabet. TIME notes that Pichai declared Google an “AI-first company” in 2016, long before the market rewarded that positioning. Google later looked behind after OpenAI’s ChatGPT launch, but by January 2026 Alphabet reached $4tn market cap, only the fourth company in history to do so after Nvidia, Apple, and Microsoft. Gemini now accounts for about one-quarter of global AI traffic, up from nearly 6% at the start of 2025. TIME frames Pichai as a quiet product leader whose long-term bets in DeepMind, TPUs, Cloud, , Waymo, and AI-enabled search/products have started to converge.

Other major themes: The issue includes “Cuba Waits,” where leading Cuban writers describe being caught between the island’s communist regime and US aggression. “The Democrats’ Billionaire” profiles Illinois governor JB Pritzker as a potential national Democratic figure and Trump antagonist. The Brief section argues that the Iran war has created a new baseline of structural energy volatility because the Strait of Hormuz can no longer be assumed reliably open.

Business implications: TIME’s company framework emphasizes leadership narrative, AI adoption, consumer storytelling, and platform power. Alphabet’s AI comeback is treated as both a strategic success and a societal risk because AI-equipped Google may become even more powerful in data, search, defense, surveillance, and commercial infrastructure.

---

## Sanlian Factory Second Generation

English standalone summary

Source file: 三联生活周刊（2026年第15期）(1).pdf

Conclusion: This Sanlian Lifeweek issue centers on China’s “factory second generation” succession problem: the children of manufacturing family-business founders are entering leadership just as domestic and global conditions become more volatile. The issue treats succession not only as a family or business topic but as a social and employment issue, because China has more than 58mn private enterprises and over 80% are family businesses under the broad All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce definition.

Core cover-story argument: Most first-generation founders were born in the 1950s/60s and built companies after reform and opening. Many are now forced to consider succession, while their children, often born in the 1980s/90s/00s, return with overseas education, stronger individual identity, and different views of work-life boundaries. Unlike Europe or Japan, where many family firms have gone through five or six generations of succession, Chinese firms are often moving from first to second generation for the first time, without mature institutional templates.

Case studies: The magazine visits three family enterprises: the Hunan spicy-snack brand “Mala Prince,” a Putian shoe company, and a stainless-steel high-end cabinet / whole-house customization furniture company in Guangzhou-Foshan-Shunde. It also interviews Professor Fan Xinyu of CKGSB’s “Jieli Changjiang” succession program. Cases show that family ties gave founders resilience during crises, but can constrain second-generation leaders who want professionalism, clearer governance, branding, IP, digitalization, and personal autonomy.

Important business insights: Digital transformation is a recurring tool. One company pushed ERP, front/back-end order integration, imported automated stainless-steel bending equipment, and built an intelligent unmanned warehouse. AI is also appearing in design, marketing, and management. Gender roles matter: daughters often enter sales, branding, foreign trade, and media, while sons more often take production/technology roles.

Other issue topics: The issue also covers Ukraine/Russia war resilience, a missing law-firm director and fundraising case, overseas adoptee family search, stem-cell scams, falling pork prices, The Witcher 3, fermented foods, oil shortages and travel, AI-generated public speech, digital brain mapping, Italian football decline, blood sugar control, and lifestyle essays.

---

## Warsh Inflation Metric

English standalone summary

Source file: 分析美联储新主席沃什的通胀新算法会带来特朗普想要的降息吗.pdf
Duplicate note: Two exact duplicate files were selected; this article is summarized once.

Conclusion: This Caixin article analyzes whether incoming Fed chair Kevin Warsh’s proposed use of trimmed-mean inflation could provide a technocratic path toward the rate cuts Trump wants. The answer is cautious: trimmed-mean measures can show lower inflation than headline/core measures during high-inflation periods, but the article argues the metric should not be overinterpreted. Oil, public opinion, AI, labor supply, and Fed independence are more important than one statistical choice.

Political context: Warsh’s nomination passed the Senate Banking Committee 13-11 on April 29, with Republicans supporting and Democrats opposing. After the Justice Department canceled its investigation into Powell, Senator Tom Tillis withdrew opposition, making Warsh’s confirmation likely. Trump said before the hearing that he would be disappointed if Warsh did not cut rates.

Inflation metric details: Warsh argued core PCE is not a good inflation measure and that the Fed should use a more accurate trimmed-mean inflation measure. Dallas Fed trimmed-mean PCE removes 24% of lower-tail and 31% of upper-tail weights, effectively discarding 55% of PCE and using the remaining 45%. In February 2026, Dallas trimmed-mean PCE was 2.3% over 12 months, versus headline PCE 2.8% and core PCE 3.0%. Cleveland’s 16% trimmed-mean CPI removes 8% at each tail and in March 2026 was 2.64%, close to core CPI 2.6% but below headline CPI 3.26%.

Critical view: Economists cited by Caixin warn trimmed mean measures the inflation “center” and can understate high-inflation pressure. Energy shocks may have second-round effects that trimming can hide. Nomura’s Rob Subbaraman expects two Fed cuts in 2H26 partly due to politics and weaker growth. The article concludes that US inflation is still above 2%, labor supply is shrinking from immigration enforcement, white-collar jobs face AI pressure, and Fed independence remains contested.

---

## China Exports Geopolitical Disruption

English standalone summary

Source file: 地缘扰动下的出口三问.pdf

Conclusion: This Caixin/Huatai-style macro article asks how Middle East disruption affects China’s exports through three channels: external demand, China’s export share, and export prices. The framework is: exports = external demand volume × China share × export price. The conclusion is balanced: short-term external-demand impact may be mild, China’s share and export prices can offset part of the drag, but if the Strait of Hormuz reopening disappoints or leaves permanent supply scars, the negative impact could become much larger.

External demand: Historical oil shocks transmit through inflation first, then soft data/manufacturing PMI and consumer confidence after 1-3 months, then growth after 1-2 quarters, and employment after 3-4 quarters. This shock differs from the 1970s because energy structures, reserves, policy tools, and US/Europe direct dependence are more favorable. The article estimates every 10% oil-price rise drags global growth by about 0.15 percentage point. Scenario estimates: optimistic case with 2026 oil average $80/bbl drags global growth 0.2pp and China exports 0.5-1pp; neutral case with $100/bbl drags global growth 0.4-0.6pp and China exports 2-3pp; pessimistic case with blockade into 2H and oil at $150/bbl drags global growth 1.7pp and China exports close to 10pp.

Export share: China’s supply-chain resilience can lift export share and offset external demand weakness. During 2020-2021 China’s global export share rose from about 13% in 2019 to over 15.5%. The current episode is unlikely to repeat the pandemic magnitude. The article thinks a 0.3-0.5 percentage point short-term share gain is more reasonable. Key mechanisms are substitution effects, cost effects, and demand creation.

Prices and sectors: Export prices lag PPI; a roughly 3pp PPI uplift can support export value, but import-price pass-through can hurt trade surplus. Strong pricing-power areas include AI-chain exports: integrated circuits +64%, storage components +103%, diodes +62%, ADP equipment parts +178%, CPUs +38%, transformers +36%, wires/cables +27%. Resources/materials also benefit: urea export volume +2453% and price +79%, tungsten price +219%, rare earths +42%. Investment theme: AI, supply-chain competitiveness, materials, shipbuilding, and energy-transition demand are better lines through geopolitical volatility.

entries.title: PLTR 估值专题 + 市场每日报告十期精粹（2026-05-26）
entries.excerpt: ★ PLTR 估值专题 方法：DCF，WACC 15.93%。假设：政府部门202628增速56%/39%/30%；商业部门2026年~90%后放缓至4045%；运营利润率5359%。 三情景：悲观$130 / 基准$188 / 乐观$244（当时股价$136.88，处于悲观情景附近）。 核心逻辑：PLTR历来"超预期
entries.body:
## ★ PLTR 估值专题

- 方法：DCF，WACC 15.93%。假设：政府部门2026-28增速56%/39%/30%；商业部门2026年~90%后放缓至40-45%；运营利润率53-59%。
- **三情景：悲观$130 / 基准$188 / 乐观$244**（当时股价$136.88，处于悲观情景附近）。
- 核心逻辑：PLTR历来"超预期并上调指引"，若只能"符合预期"则高估值不可持续——持续超预期是维持溢价的必要条件。

## 每日报告十期要点

1. **微软Maia芯片破圈**：与Anthropic谈判供应自研芯片——AI算力供给格局多元化开端。英伟达Token推理成本年降70%+而售价稳定；Vera Rubin下半年量产；2025-27收入目标$1万亿；新增$1,185亿回购。沃尔玛指引不及预期（油价+退税消退压制消费）。大科技今年或发债超$2,000亿——建议配少量债市对冲。
2. **美联储转鹰**：纪要显示通胀高于2%将进一步收紧；SMH偏离200周均线150%、14周RSI破80（历史上RSI到80后平均还需21周才真正见顶——不必立即卖但建议买保护）。OpenAI推"Guaranteed Capacity"锁算力——产业链互相绑定，确定性增强但弹性下降。
3. **债市风险信号**：基金经理股票净超配50%（历史单月最大增幅）、现金3.9%；30年美债破5%。存储LTA改变周期特征（备货式→按单式），估值框架或从PB切换到PE——美光/三星重估空间。Gemini 3.5 Flash成默认模型、月活9亿。
4. **高盛推迟降息**：首次降息推至12月。亚马逊Trainium被低估（AWS+自研芯片差异化）。AI使劳动生产率从1.5%升至~2%。"学巴菲特留现金、学对冲基金买保险"。
5. **利率风暴**：美10年期突破长期下降趋势线、日债急升。闪迪FY27 EPS预期上调近2000%、美光+768%——分析师上调速度超股价。阿克曼建仓微软（前瞻PE 21倍历史低位）。伯克希尔：谷歌仓位加3倍、减仓雪佛龙35%。
6. **持仓公开**：大额买入英伟达/苹果/标普ETF，新增博通/甲骨文/德仪。亚马逊冲$3万亿：AWS +28%（三年最快）、Trainium承诺超$2,250亿、79位分析师全部买入。散户半导体拥挤度99.3% vs 软件22.8%。Cerebras IPO首日翻倍（WSE-3内存带宽是H100的7000倍、OpenAI $200亿订单、未盈利）。
7. **标普9400预测**（大摩）：基础是盈利强劲增长不依赖降息；84%成分股盈利超预期。AI网络安全威胁：AI生成攻击代码概率超70%，企业应对窗口仅3-5个月——CRWD/PANW/DDOG定价基础更扎实。
8. **通胀两年新高**：4月CPI +3.8%。甲骨文风险：过度依赖OpenAI单一客户（超50%未履约义务）。芝商所推全球首个算力期货（GPU租金指数结算）——GPU代际18个月一迭代，期货失真概率高，散户暂不参与。
9. **半导体泡沫警示**：高盛指市场呈2000年特征、看涨期权偏斜近垂直。边缘推理提升或使高端算力需求转向廉价边缘计算。CPO规模化2026H2启动、Scale-up场景需到2028；铜光并存而非替代。
10. **三大风险齐聚**：通胀（油价触顶前）、美联储换届（6月17日FOMC）、中期选举（5-10月历史偏弱）。不会崩盘的三理由：涨幅集中半导体单一板块、84%公司盈利超预期18.2%、2026/27标普盈利增速预期23%/15%。**机会：从AI基础设施层转向应用层（GOOGL、TEAM、DDOG）。**

## 核心主线（近2周）

| 主题 | 共识方向 | 主要风险 |
|---|---|---|
| 美联储/利率 | 鹰派转向、降息推迟 | 30年期破5%，股债背离 |
| 英伟达/半导体 | 财报验证、长期逻辑未破 | 技术面过热（SMH偏离150%） |
| 通胀 | CPI 3.8%两年新高、阶段峰值或至 | 油价+供应链推动核心通胀 |
| 亚马逊/AWS | AWS加速28%、Trainium低估 | 2027 capex $2,260亿 |
| PLTR | 基准$188（+40%） | 现价接近悲观情景$130 |
| 下一轮机会 | AI应用层接棒基础设施层 | 轮动时间窗口不确定 |

entries.title: 市场观察十篇摘要（2026-05-26）：加息风险 / SpaceX 招股书 / TSLA 估值 / 软件AI颠覆论
entries.excerpt: 1. 加息已成最大风险：沃什就任美联储主席；沃勒称加息与降息概率"五五开"。OpenAI/SpaceX/Anthropic 三巨头筹备IPO——超大规模IPO通过被动基金再平衡吸走流动性，或成牛市拐点。英伟达CPU收入$200亿有水分（独立CPU实际$5070亿，其余为捆绑内存打包计费）。 2. 英伟达三大催化剂：FY
entries.body:
1. **加息已成最大风险**：沃什就任美联储主席；沃勒称加息与降息概率"五五开"。OpenAI/SpaceX/Anthropic 三巨头筹备IPO——超大规模IPO通过被动基金再平衡吸走流动性，或成牛市拐点。英伟达CPU收入$200亿有水分（独立CPU实际$50-70亿，其余为捆绑内存打包计费）。
2. **英伟达三大催化剂**：FY27Q1收入$816亿（+85%）、EPS +95%、毛利率75%、供应承诺$1,190亿。担忧：Rubin或因海力士HBM4延迟、HBM成本从$37.4万飙至$200万/台、自研芯片蚕食。催化：收入结构重拆（大科技50%+ACIE50%）、Vera CPU $200亿、$800亿回购+股息提至$0.25/季。**前瞻PE 20倍出头是巨头中最低；8月底财报是"近一年最重要的一次"。**
3. **SpaceX 招股书（下·梦想）**：TAM $28.5万亿（火箭$3,700亿+星链$1.6万亿+AI $26.5万亿）。发射成本$2,700/kg（行业$18,500）占全球75%但发射业务亏损。星链是现金牛：收入$114亿、利润率39%、用户1,030万但ARPU降至$66。xAI烧钱：收入$32亿亏$64亿、与Anthropic签每月$12.5亿算力合同（总额~$450亿）。**FCF年缺口逾$140亿、长债$291亿、审计三大关注点**。募资$750亿；2026年8月初/11月初为解锁节点。
4. **SpaceX 招股书（上·控制）**：马斯克B类股掌控85.1%投票权且可单独选董事会过半；关联交易严重（Valor与xAI约$200亿设备租赁）；章程禁止集体诉讼。**买的是"经济权益"而非"话语权"，治理风险应体现为估值折扣。**
5. **PLTR估值**：DCF三情景 悲观$130/基准$188/乐观$244。
6. **特斯拉基本面**：全球EV渗透率12.8%（中国份额从10.8%跌至4.1%）；毛利率从近30%跌至17.8%。估值（股价$420时）：悲观$214/基准$333/乐观$450——**卖车业务仅贡献~$30，FSD+Robotaxi贡献~$262是估值绝对核心**。投资特斯拉本质是押注FSD和Robotaxi。
7. **软件板块AI颠覆论**（专家访谈，IGV年初以来-25%）：财税软件最大壁垒是"法律担责"（软件公司为报税错误兜底，AI不能）；SAP短期难被替代（大企业无验证案例不换系统）；HR软件相对悲观。三共识：AI短期扩大蛋糕；收费从按人头转按量；行业壁垒降低。**存活关键=有无AI触不到的硬壁垒（法律/合规/隐私）+ 窗口期内把AI武器化。**
8. **年度复盘方法论**："猎人模式"——牛市保留现金子弹等待高确定性机会集中出击；真正赚钱的投机全部来自已深度研究的股票；管理层评估核心是"逆境中断臂求生的魄力"；集中持有3-5只深研标的长期跑赢分散。
9. **台积电**：先进制程领先3-7年、3/5/7nm贡献70%+营收——"AI产业链中确定性最高的投资"；风险在地缘而非商业竞争。
10. **三大风险齐聚**：通胀/美联储换届/中期选举；机会从基础设施层转向应用层。

entries.title: 投行研报摘要合集（2026-05-24 批次，51篇）
entries.excerpt: 本合集由 52 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。 Japan Portfolio Strategy HALO, Good Buy 文件：6.Japan Portfolio Strategy HALO, Good Buy(1).pdf 结论：这份报告把欧洲和亚洲策略团队提出的 HALO 框架应用到日本股票市场。
entries.body:
> 本合集由 52 篇邮件草稿摘要合并而成，可用页内搜索定位。

## Japan Portfolio Strategy - HALO, Good Buy

文件：6.Japan Portfolio Strategy_ HALO, Good Buy(1).pdf

结论：这份报告把欧洲和亚洲策略团队提出的 HALO 框架应用到日本股票市场。HALO 指 Heavy Assets, Low Obsolescence，即重资产、低过时风险的公司。报告核心判断是：在 AI 冲击、供应链重构、地缘政治重新排列和能源安全压力上升的环境下，市场会重新评估那些拥有难以复制的实体资产、生产能力、基础设施和长期经济价值的公司。相对而言，轻资产、高过时风险的 LAHO 公司，尤其是部分软件、专业服务和依赖外包供应链的商业模式，可能面临估值折价。

关键数据：日本成长股相对价值股的 12 个月前瞻 PE 溢价在 2022 年初超过 140%，目前已回落至约 60%。日本高资本密集度行业包括公用事业 90%、运输 84%、电信服务 80%、材料 73%、汽车及零部件 68%、能源 67%。软件与服务、商业与专业服务的资本密集度最低。报告构建了日本 HALO 篮子 GSJPHALO 和 LAHO 篮子 GSJPLAHO，并指出从 2025 年四季度以来，做多 HALO、做空 LAHO 在日本已经开始产生正收益。

投资含义：报告建议投资者关注日本市场中具备重资产、供应链韧性、生产能力、能源/运输/材料等现实瓶颈暴露的公司。AI 时代不仅提升了算力资产价值，也降低了某些低资本投入、高人力密集业务的终值确定性。对日本而言，政策、地缘政治和制造业回流均有利于 HALO 风格继续跑赢。

风险和跟踪点：该策略并非单纯买入所有重资产公司，部分公用事业、运输和食品等防御性板块在强牛市中可能跑输。若 AI 对软件和服务的冲击被证伪，LAHO 估值可能修复。投资者应重点跟踪 HALO/LAHO 估值折价是否继续收窄、日本资本开支周期、能源成本、供应链本土化和日股价值风格持续性。

## US Weekly Kickstart - AI, Momentum, and the One Big Trade

文件：2.US Weekly Kickstart_ AI, Momentum, and the One Big Trade(2).pdf

结论：这份报告认为，美股当前越来越像“一笔大交易”，即 AI 与 Momentum 高度绑定后共同推动指数创新高。市场不是全面上涨，而是由科技、半导体、AI 基础设施和少数龙头贡献绝大部分收益。报告并不简单看空，而是强调：当前动量背后有真实盈利上修支撑，但历史上如此剧烈的 Momentum 拉升通常意味着短期仍可能延续、随后几个月回报趋弱。

关键数据：截至报告时，S&P 500 年初至今上涨 10%，其中科技贡献了 85% 的指数回报；剔除科技后，S&P 500 仅上涨 3%。过去一个月指数创下 14 次新高，但市场广度收窄。Momentum 因子过去三个月上涨 25%，属于历史上最剧烈的上行之一。NVDA 权重约占 S&P 500 的 9%，但贡献约 20% 的年初至今指数回报。前十大贡献股票占指数年初至今回报约 84%。

投资含义：报告建议投资者继续持有有盈利增长和盈利上修支撑的股票，但不要只押注纯 AI beta。投资机会可以分成两类：一类是 AI 直接受益者，如 AI 基础设施和能源；另一类是对 AI/Momentum 敏感度较低但盈利预期在改善的“Insensitive Portfolio”。对已经参与 AI 交易的投资者，报告建议加入部分低 Momentum、但盈利修正为正的股票作为对冲，因为过去 Momentum 反转时，低 Momentum 股票不仅相对跑赢，绝对收益也可能为正。

风险和跟踪点：主要风险是市场宽度继续收窄、AI 资本开支预期下修、长端利率无序上行或宏观增长走弱。投资者应跟踪 EPS revision breadth、NVDA/AI 供应链业绩、10 年期美债收益率、Momentum 因子强度以及科技板块以外行业的盈利修复情况。

## US Economics Analyst - Concentration, Profits, and AI Disruption

文件：1.US Economics Analyst_ Concentration, Profits, and the Competitive Landscape Ahead of AI Disruption(1)(1).pdf

结论：这份报告从宏观和产业组织角度分析 AI 对企业集中度和利润率的影响。核心观点是双向的：AI 可能通过降低工具门槛、削弱既有软件和服务流程，增加竞争；但从历史经验看，重大技术冲击更常见的结果是领先企业通过规模、数据、分发、资本和无形资产投资进一步扩大优势。因此，AI 未必天然利空大公司，反而可能让最会部署 AI 的龙头进一步集中市场份额。

关键数据：报告引用接近一个世纪的税务和行政数据，显示美国及其他发达经济体的企业集中度长期上升。美国集中度自 1930 年代以来持续提升，早期由金融和制造业大企业扩张驱动，后期由信息、零售和批发贸易驱动。利润率和 markup 在过去几十年上升，报告估计自 2000 年以来，集中度上升解释了美国企业利润率提升的大约三分之一。

投资含义：报告对 AI 投资的启示是：不要机械地认为 AI 会摧毁所有 incumbents。真正关键的问题是，某行业的现有龙头是否拥有 AI 部署所需的数据、客户分发、流程嵌入、算力预算和组织执行力。如果具备这些条件，AI 可能强化护城河；如果现有利润来自低效率、信息不透明或服务人力套利，则 AI 可能削弱其竞争力。

风险和跟踪点：高利润、高集中度且 AI 暴露高的行业最值得关注，因为它们既可能被 AI 原生公司攻击，也可能成为集中度进一步提升的赢家。投资者应跟踪行业毛利率、市场份额变化、AI 产品的客户留存、价格压力、监管反垄断态度，以及龙头公司是否能把 AI 转化为真实收入和成本节约。

## Global Market Views - Shortages

文件：3.Global Market Views_ Shortages(1)(1).pdf

结论：这份宏观市场报告认为，市场近期上涨来自深度尾部风险下降后的风险溢价压缩，但“短缺”仍是主线。短缺包括能源和大宗商品短缺，也包括 AI 供应链短缺。伊朗停火或冲突降温让市场暂时敢于向前看，推动美股、高息/商品货币和新兴市场反弹；但油价和收益率仍高，说明风险并未完全消失。报告认为，市场目前风险分布更平衡，但最重要的下行尾部仍是中东局势再升级或 Hormuz 长时间关闭。

关键数据和逻辑：报告指出，即使油价和债券收益率保持高位，广泛风险资产仍已强劲恢复，AI 乐观情绪使相关资产创出新周期高点。共同机制是：能源短缺带来通胀和能源盈利支撑，AI 供应链短缺带来资本流向半导体、数据中心、电力和相关瓶颈资产。报告也提醒，短缺和韧性增长的另一面是债券收益率上行，市场在收益率突破关键位时通常会更紧张。

投资含义：报告建议保留对中东再升级的保护。跨资产比较中，欧洲股票、信用和外汇的价外下行保护仍具有吸引力；做多石油也能在冲突升级时提供保护，但若危机完全解决，油多头会受损。若能源流动逐步恢复，油价和利率市场可能缓和，正向价格行动会从 AI 和能源扩散到更多地区和板块。

风险和跟踪点：核心风险不是市场没有反映风险，而是深度尾部可能仍被低估。投资者应跟踪 Hormuz 航运、伊朗/美国谈判、油品库存、长端美债收益率、AI 供应链交付周期以及风险资产广度是否改善。

## Oil Comment - Solving for Diesel and Gasoline Shortages

文件：4.Oil Comment_ Solving for Diesel and Gasoline Shortages(1).pdf

结论：这份油品报告讨论在 Hormuz 长期受阻的极端情景下，柴油和汽油是否会出现真正短缺。报告核心结论是：如果至少两个“解决器”启动，OECD 柴油库存有机会维持在临界水平以上；但柴油产出比例上升会挤压汽油产出，因此汽油市场可能更脆弱。要同时避免柴油和汽油库存跌破临界水平，需要更高价格驱动需求破坏，并配合炼厂利用率上升或 SPR 成品油释放。

关键数据：报告估计，美国柴油收率上升 1 个百分点，通常会使成品汽油收率下降 0.8 个百分点。炼厂会在柴油相对汽油利润更高时切换产出。3-2-1 refining margin 每上升 10 美元，全球炼厂利用率通常提高 1.3 个百分点。但当前美国炼厂利用率已高，夏季行车季又通常减少检修，进一步提升空间可能低于历史规律。报告把 20 天需求覆盖作为柴油和汽油商业库存的临界阈值。

投资含义：在 Hormuz 持续关闭且没有额外应对措施的灰色情景下，OECD 柴油和汽油库存可能分别在 8 月和 10 月触及临界线。若柴油收率上升 1 个百分点并发生需求破坏，柴油可维持到年底，但汽油可能在 12 月触及临界线。要让二者均安全，需要柴油额外 3%、汽油额外 4% 的需求破坏，并且要么全球炼厂利用率再升 1 个百分点，要么释放 0.6mb/d 的柴油 SPR。

风险和跟踪点：主要风险是炼厂物理瓶颈、原油可得性、价格上限导致成本转嫁困难，以及汽油库存被柴油切换挤压。投资者应跟踪汽柴油裂解价差、OECD 成品油库存、SPR 政策、美国驾驶季需求和炼厂开工率。

## Global Rates Trader - Rates Running Out of Patience

文件：5.Global Rates Trader_ Rates Running Out of Patience(1).pdf

结论：这份利率策略报告认为，全球债券市场正在失去耐心。能源供给冲击和中东冲突增加了通胀风险，使名义久期在短期内很难发挥传统组合对冲功能。美国、英国、日本和德国长端收益率同步上升，说明这不是单一国家问题，而是全球期限溢价、通胀风险和政策路径重新定价的结果。报告认为美债中期对冲价值在改善，但短期仍应通过限制下行风险的结构来表达。

关键数据：美国 10 年期收益率突破 4.5%，30 年期突破 5.0%。与上次 30 年期美债超过 5% 的 2025 年三季度相比，英国、日本和德国 30 年期平均收益率又上升约 50bp。报告指出，年初至今美债抛售很大程度反映英国和日本的外溢冲击。10 年期美债收益率变化与股票收益的一月滚动相关性达到数十年来最负水平，说明债券不再能有效抵消股票波动。

投资含义：报告并非否认美债价值，而是认为需要谨慎表达。随着市场定价了增长乐观和更明显的通胀风险溢价，美债作为中期对冲工具的吸引力提高；但在冲突和能源冲击没有解决前，直接做多久期容易继续承受收益率上行。策略上更偏向使用期权、限损结构或相对价值表达，例如长欧洲政府债相对 OIS，同时收紧止损。

风险和跟踪点：若能源价格继续上升、Fed 降息预期继续消失、英国/日本长端继续抛售，全球久期仍会承压。需要跟踪 Hormuz、油价、美国通胀预期、Fed 官员措辞、BoJ 政策路径和英国财政风险溢价。

投资含义：报告认为美元最清晰的上行风险来自能源冲击进一步压制其他发达经济体的增长、政策和预期回报。英镑下行相对 AUD 或 USD 更有价值，因为它同时暴露于国内政治、财政空间、能源价格和全球风险偏好的压力。商品出口国货币和高 carry 货币在能源/短缺环境中有相对支撑，但若风险情绪恶化，也会出现拥挤交易调整。

## US Week Ahead - May 18 to May 24

## GOAL Kickstart - Rising Bond Yields Weigh on Portfolios

文件：1.GOAL Kickstart_ The name is bond (again) - rising bond yields weigh on portfolios.pdf

结论：这份资产配置报告强调，债券收益率再次成为组合的核心压力源。过去一周美国通胀数据超预期，同时经济活动仍然稳健，全球债券因再通胀背景、英国和日本收益率外溢而抛售。关键不是收益率单纯上升，而是市场认为收益率上升更多来自通胀和政策风险，而不是健康增长。因此股票与债券收益率的相关性变得异常负面，传统股债分散效果下降。

关键数据：报告指出，美国股票与美国 10 年期收益率的两个月相关性降至 1990 年代末以来最负水平。自中东战争和能源价格冲击以来，市场把宏观冲击更多解读为通胀而非增长。美国 10 年期收益率单周上涨超过 2 个标准差，提醒投资者不要过早 fade 利率右尾风险。历史上，当美国 10 年期收益率高于 5%、实际收益率高于 2-2.5%，或 10 年实际利率高于长期实际 GDP 增长预期时，股票/债券收益率相关性更容易转负。

投资含义：Goldman 在 3 个月和 12 个月资产配置上维持债券 Neutral。虽然从风险溢价角度看债券更有吸引力，但负相关 regime 可能持续更久。报告认为，equity down/rates up 的双重二元期权适合作为平衡组合的 overlay，用于对冲因收益率进一步上升引发的股票下跌。

风险和跟踪点：若通胀继续高企、能源价格未回落、Fed 官员更鹰、英国/日本长端收益率继续上行，股债可能继续同跌。投资者应跟踪 10 年期和 30 年期美债、实际利率、油价、通胀预期、Fed 讲话以及股票对收益率变化的敏感度。

## Global Markets Daily - Yield-Based Bid in Corporate Credit

文件：2.Global Markets Daily_ Quantifying the ‘Yield-Based’ Bid in Corporate Credit.pdf

结论：这份信用市场报告解释了为什么 corporate credit spreads 虽然从历史角度看偏紧，但仍保持韧性。核心原因是 all-in yields 具有吸引力，吸引养老金和保险公司等 yield-based buyers。报告认为，只要收益率上行不是 disorderly，美元投资级信用的需求可能继续增强，从而帮助 spreads 维持较紧水平。

关键数据：报告指出，1-10 年美元投资级公司债平均 all-in yield 接近 5%，10 年以上美元投资级公司债接近 6%，相对历史具有吸引力。美国企业养老金 funded status 连续两年改善，目前 funded ratio 达到 2007 年以来最强；美国公共养老金 funded ratio 也改善。美国保险行业 invested assets 在 2025 年增长近 7%，是 2021 年以来最大年度增幅。同时，保险公司平均债券配置比例比 2010 年低 10 个百分点，而其账面收益率低于当前公司债市场收益率。

投资含义：报告认为，养老金和保险公司可能沿 de-risking glide path 增加固定收益和高质量公司债配置。即便投资者担心增长-通胀-货币政策组合恶化导致 spreads 扩大，绝对收益率仍能吸引长期资金入场。这支持 USD corporate credit spreads 的韧性，尤其是高质量、久期适中、能够满足 liability matching 的信用资产。

风险和跟踪点：最大的风险是收益率上升变得无序，导致总回报亏损和信用 spread 同步扩大。若经济增长恶化、违约预期上升或资金流从信用撤出，yield-based bid 可能不足以稳定市场。跟踪点包括养老金 funded ratio、保险公司资产配置、IG 新发行、10 年期美债收益率、credit spread 和资金流。

关键数据：报告指出，应用软件覆盖股票的中位数年初至今跌幅约38%，反映市场对AI替代、增长放缓、销售周期拉长、座席制收入受压等问题的担忧。板块已经经历两次反弹：一次是2月23日至3月6日上涨约14%，另一次是4月10日至5月中旬上涨约22%。这些反弹说明低位资金愿意参与，但尚未证明盈利预期已经系统性上修。报告提到一些“green shoots”：Klaviyo、Workday、Adobe等公司出现管理层或组织调整，ServiceNow ITSM Level 1自动化已有约50个试点客户，Salesforce也在推进headless CRM等新形态产品。但这些更多是产品和组织层面的早期信号，还没有转化为行业层面清晰的收入加速。

投资建议：报告建议投资者不要把软件板块简单看成“AI落后补涨”。AI确实可能在2027年之后推动部分软件公司重新加速，但市场需要看到AI收入对WholeCo总收入、订单、账单、剩余履约义务或毛利的实质贡献。换言之，软件公司如果只是讲AI故事、提升产品包装，估值很难持续修复；只有AI产品能够带来新增付费、降低流失、提高客单价或扩大使用量，股票才可能从bounce进入rally。报告更偏好能够证明AI是增量收入而非防御工具的公司，同时强调个股差异会非常大。

风险与跟踪点：主要风险来自续约定价压力、合同期限缩短、座席制商业模式中未充分使用的shelfware被客户削减、AI能力被大模型平台或竞争对手商品化，以及销售周期继续拉长。报告还提到RepVue数据中销售周期延长约1%-4%，虽然幅度不大，但方向值得重视。后续应重点跟踪软件公司AI产品的真实ARR、客户续约率、净收入留存率、RPO变化、销售人员生产率，以及管理层是否能把AI功能从演示转化为预算。总体看，报告不是否定软件AI机会，而是提醒投资者：现在买软件必须更像买“可验证经营改善”，而不是买“估值跌多后的反弹”。

## Hon Hai - AI Server and CPO Switch Demand

文件：12.Hon Hai (2317.TW)_ Asia Communacopia + Technology — Key Takeaways_ AI Server QoQ growth; 800G+_ CPO Switch in strong demand.pdf

结论：报告维持对鸿海（Hon Hai，2317.TW）的积极看法，认为公司正从传统EMS龙头升级为AI服务器机柜、交换机和关键组件的系统级供应商。报告给予Buy CL评级，目标价NT$400，报告时点价格NT$245，上行空间约63.3%。核心投资逻辑是AI服务器出货在2026年逐季增长，800G以上交换机需求强劲，下一代CPO交换机将在2026年下半年出货，而鸿海不仅组装整机，还逐步掌握液冷、连接器、busbar等更多价值量组件。

关键数据：公司预计2026年AI服务器出货将逐季增长，二季度出货环比增长可达高双位数。800G+交换机出货预计今年增长两倍，下一代CPO交换机预计在2026年下半年开始出货。这说明AI数据中心网络带宽升级与算力服务器扩张同步推进，不是单一GPU服务器需求。报告特别强调，鸿海自有产品已经覆盖AI服务器机架中除芯片和内存外约50%的组件，包括BP连接器、液冷模块、busbars等。这意味着公司有机会提升毛利率和客户粘性，而不是只承接低毛利组装。

投资建议：报告建议把鸿海放在“AI服务器平台化供应链”中评估。传统EMS估值通常较低，因为收入规模大但利润率薄；但如果公司在AI服务器机柜中承担更多设计、组件、热管理、电源和网络价值量，其盈利弹性和估值中枢都有上修空间。另一个重要点是ASIC AI服务器项目采用consignment模式，芯片和内存不计入鸿海收入，但毛利率比例更高，同时降低营运资金占用。这可能使表观收入不如完整BOM模式亮眼，但利润质量更好。

风险与跟踪点：主要风险包括AI服务器项目爬坡慢于预期、EV total solution业务低于预期、全球产能扩张进度较慢、EMS行业竞争加剧导致议价能力下降，以及CPO交换机平台时间表延后。投资者应跟踪AI服务器季度收入增速、800G/CPO交换机量产节点、自有组件收入占比、毛利率趋势、营运资金变化，以及客户集中度。报告整体观点是，鸿海的AI机会不只是“代工英伟达服务器”这么简单，而是从整机组装向机柜级系统解决方案和关键零组件扩展，若执行顺利，市场可能继续重估其AI链地位。

## Alibaba - AI Cloud and MaaS Scaling

文件：8.Alibaba Group (BABA)_ Asia Communacopia + Technology — Key Takeaways_ AI driving accelerating cloud growth as MaaS scales.pdf

结论：报告对阿里巴巴维持Buy CL评级，认为AI正在推动阿里云重新进入加速增长阶段，MaaS（Model-as-a-Service）规模化是最关键的边际变化。报告目标价为美股US$186、港股HK$180，对应报告时点价格US$133.26/HK$133.30，上行空间约39.6%/35%。核心判断是，阿里云不再只是传统IaaS/PaaS云服务商，而是在中国AI模型、算力、API和企业智能体生态中占据基础设施入口，未来五年外部云加AI收入目标可达1000亿美元。

关键数据：报告指出，上一季度AI相关产品收入已经占外部云收入约30%，公司目标是在未来一年提升到50%。百炼（Bailian）MaaS ARR近期达到约人民币80亿元，目标是在6月季度达到人民币100亿元，并在财年末达到人民币300亿元。增长主要来自MaaS API，且随着新模型智能水平更高，API价格存在上调空间。算力供给方面，阿里通过自建基础设施、租赁算力以及T-Head芯片支持推理需求；自研芯片有助于改善成本和利润率。报告还提出一个重要角度：agentic AI对CPU/GPU比例要求可能更高，因此CPU需求也可能受益。

投资建议：报告看好阿里云加AI收入成为集团估值重估的主线之一。国内需求正在从互联网、金融、EV扩展到制造业等更广泛行业，海外增长则来自中国企业出海和本地客户。电商方面，报告提到Quick Commerce业务改善以及淘宝天猫协同，这些因素有助于市场重新评估核心商业利润和云投入之间的平衡。报告预计FY27E/FY28E EPS同比恢复增长约32%/54%，显示盈利修复和云AI成长可以同时发生。对长期投资者而言，阿里更像是中国AI基础设施、模型分发和智能体应用生态的综合平台，而不只是消费互联网公司。

风险与跟踪点：需要跟踪百炼ARR是否按人民币100亿、300亿路径兑现，AI收入占外部云收入比例是否继续提升，API价格是否真的能随模型升级上行，以及自研芯片是否改善推理成本。风险包括国内云价格竞争重新加剧、模型API降价快于用量增长、资本开支过高压制自由现金流、监管或地缘政治限制海外拓展，以及电商竞争导致利润被再投入消耗。总体看，报告的投资建议明确偏多：阿里云的AI收入已经从概念进入规模化阶段，若MaaS ARR持续高增，阿里估值体系可能从传统互联网折价逐步转向AI平台溢价。

## USA FOMC Minutes - Hawkish Inflation Bias

文件：8.USA_ FOMC Minutes Note That “a Majority” of Participants Would Support “Some Policy Firming” If Inflation Stays “Persistently...(1).pdf

结论：这份FOMC会议纪要解读明显偏鹰，核心信息是美联储内部对通胀回到2%的信心不足，若通胀持续高于目标，多数与会者愿意支持进一步政策收紧。报告的宏观含义是：市场不能过早押注快速降息，尤其在能源价格、服务价格、软件价格和AI相关结构变化仍可能支撑通胀的情况下，美债前端和美元利率曲线需要继续消化“higher for longer”甚至重新加息的尾部风险。

关键数据：会议纪要显示，与会者普遍认为，如果通胀维持高位，可能需要更长时间保持联邦基金利率不变。更重要的是，“多数”与会者认为，如果通胀继续持续高于2%，某种程度的政策收紧可能是合适的。许多委员希望从政策声明中移除隐含宽松倾向，绝大多数委员认为通胀回到2%所需时间长于预期的风险已经上升。投票方面，几乎所有委员支持将利率维持在3.5%-3.75%；Governor Miran反对，主张降息25bp；Hammack、Logan、Kashkari则反对声明中存在宽松倾向。劳动力市场方面，多数委员认为就业数据仍显示稳定，但就业下行风险偏高。

投资建议：这份报告对资产配置的直接含义是，利率敏感资产不宜过度依赖降息交易。长久期成长股、房地产、信用利差和高杠杆资产若估值已经隐含明显降息，短期存在调整风险。对股票市场而言，AI和高质量盈利仍可支撑部分成长股，但指数层面需要警惕利率上行对估值倍数的压制。对债券而言，前端利率下行空间受到通胀风险限制，曲线定价需要同时反映增长放缓和通胀粘性。

风险与跟踪点：报告提到会议纪要公布后，市场隐含的2026年底联邦基金利率大体不变，但此前因油价下行曾下降，这说明能源价格仍是重要变量。后续关键数据包括核心PCE、工资增速、就业人数、失业率、服务通胀、能源价格以及中东局势对油价的传导。还需关注AI采用是否通过软件价格、劳动市场集中度或生产率变化影响通胀路径。总体结论是：FOMC内部尚未准备确认通胀战役结束，投资组合需要保留对利率上行或降息延后情景的防御。

投资建议：报告认为阿里具备中国AI agent生态的多重入口：企业端有阿里云和百炼，开发者端有Qwen Cloud和Qoder，消费者端有通义千问应用，商业场景端又能连接淘宝天猫。若AI agent成为下一代流量和任务执行入口，阿里不仅能赚云资源和API费用，也可能强化电商、广告、企业服务和国际业务。自研T-Head芯片路线和出货规模则有助于降低推理成本，提高MaaS毛利率。投资上，这支持阿里从“电商竞争压力下的低估值互联网公司”向“中国AI基础设施与agent平台公司”重估。

风险与跟踪点：关键风险包括模型能力无法持续领先、MaaS价格竞争过快、GPU或自研芯片供给不足、企业AI预算落地慢，以及消费者端AI入口难以形成高频使用。后续要跟踪百炼ARR、API调用量、模型价格、企业客户数量、Qwen应用活跃度、Taobao/Tmall与Qwen整合后的转化效果，以及云资本开支对利润的影响。总体看，报告结论积极：阿里的AI布局已经进入产品密集发布和商业化加速阶段，最重要的是证明百炼和Qwen生态能否从开发者热度转化为可持续收入。

## Nvidia First Take - Strong Quarter and Buyback

文件：1.Nvidia Corp. (NVDA)_ First Take_ Strong quarter, with guidance well above expectations and improved capital allocation(1)(1).pdf

结论：这份英伟达First Take报告结论非常明确：季度业绩强于预期，下一季度指引显著高于市场预期，同时资本回报力度提升，短期股价反应应偏正面。报告给予Buy评级，目标价US$250，报告时点价格US$220.61，上行空间约13.3%。核心判断是，AI基础设施需求仍然强劲，Data Center业务继续超预期，而公司通过大幅增加回购授权和提高股息，向市场传递现金流与长期信心。

投资建议：报告继续看好英伟达作为AI算力主链龙头的盈利能见度。业绩超预期不仅来自短期出货，也反映Blackwell/Rubin平台周期、数据中心CapEx、网络和边缘计算需求的综合拉动。报告还指出，英伟达结果对Broadcom、AMD、Marvell、ARM等AI半导体链条具有正面读数，因为强指引说明AI基础设施投资尚未进入明显消化期。对投资组合而言，NVDA仍是AI主题中确定性最高的核心资产之一，但报告时点目标价上行空间较前期收窄，意味着仓位管理应关注预期是否已经充分反映。

风险与跟踪点：主要风险包括AI基础设施投资放缓、客户资本开支进入消化期、ASIC和其他加速器竞争、毛利率因产品组合或供应链成本承压，以及供应约束影响交付。后续需要跟踪Data Center连续增长、Blackwell/Rubin供给爬坡、云厂商CapEx修订、网络产品增长、毛利率稳定性和回购执行节奏。整体看，这份报告并不是寻找新故事，而是确认AI算力龙头的增长仍然强劲，且现金流质量足以支持更积极的资本回报。

## Mutual Fundamentals - Semis over Software

文件：7.Mutual Fundamentals_ Funds widen tilt to Semis over Software(2).pdf

结论：这份报告通过主动型共同基金持仓分析，揭示机构资金在AI主题内部继续从软件转向半导体。核心结论是，尽管AI叙事同时覆盖软件和硬件，但大型主动基金实际行为更偏向买入AI数据中心和半导体链条，同时降低软件暴露。报告对市场风格的意义很强：AI交易并没有结束，而是从“宽泛AI概念”进一步集中到能够直接受益CapEx和硬件瓶颈的公司。

关键数据：报告分析了509只大型主动共同基金，合计权益资产约US$3.9tn。年初至今只有29%的基金跑赢基准，低于历史平均37%，说明主动管理者在集中度高、风格切换快的市场中面临压力。资金流方面，美国股票共同基金和ETF年初至今流入加速，总额约US$166bn。基金虽然年内提高了现金仓位，但现金比例相对历史仍处低位。AI主题持仓变化最重要：一季度共同基金减持软件、增持半导体；剔除大型科技巨头后，平均基金将半导体超配幅度提高25bp至+49bp。20个最受欢迎的增持标的中，有6个属于GS AI Data Centers basket成分股。相反，剔除微软后的软件低配扩大12bp至-36bp，达到至少2012年以来最低暴露。

投资建议：这份报告对投资策略的启示是，当前机构最愿意为AI中的“可见收入和订单”付费，而不是为软件公司未来可能出现的AI货币化提前买单。半导体、网络、服务器、数据中心电力与材料链更容易拿到真实订单和盈利上修，因此获得资金增配。软件板块则需要证明AI功能可以转化为ARR、价格提升或客户留存改善，否则可能持续被资金低配。报告还显示Mag 7仍被共同基金大幅低配723bp，较上一季度710bp进一步扩大，基金减持了每一只Mag 7，其中GOOGL减持最大，这说明很多主动基金仍在努力控制巨头集中风险。

风险与跟踪点：行业层面，基金最超配工业+197bp和金融+190bp，最低配信息技术-478bp，这反映传统板块与AI硬件链之间的复杂再平衡。报告还讨论IPO影响，认为历史上没有证据显示大型IPO前主动基金会显著提前卖出持仓，但若大型IPO快速纳入指数，被动基金可能机械性卖出现有持仓以腾出权重。后续应跟踪共同基金13F/持仓更新、AI数据中心篮子资金流、软件公司AI收入证据，以及大型科技股低配是否被迫回补。总体结论：机构资金已经用仓位表达了偏好，现阶段AI链条中半导体和数据中心基础设施仍强于软件。

## Global Strategy Views - Momentum Risks Duplicate

文件：10.Global Strategy Views_ Momentum risks yielding to bonds(3)(1).pdf

结论：这份报告与第29份Global Strategy Views主题重复，核心判断是过去表现强劲的Momentum交易正在面临债券收益率上行和宏观不确定性的压力。报告并不简单否定动量股或AI成长股，而是提醒投资者：当长端利率上行、债券重新具备估值吸引力、宏观增长开始变软时，过去由AI和盈利上修支撑的Momentum组合可能出现相对收益回落，资金可能重新评估股票与债券之间的风险补偿。

关键数据：报告背景是全球长端债券收益率上行，美债、英债、日债等市场均出现压力，投资者重新定价财政赤字、通胀粘性和央行路径。Momentum策略此前显著受益于AI相关股票和盈利预期上修，但当债券收益率抬升时，高估值成长股的久期属性会被重新审视。报告认为，当前Momentum并不完全等同于1999年或2021年的泡沫，因为本轮AI龙头确实有强劲盈利和现金流支持；但如果AI投资预期出现下降，或者债券收益率继续上行，Momentum仍可能出现“catch-down”式调整。

投资建议：报告建议投资者在保留AI核心资产的同时，逐步提高对债券和更均衡股票风格的关注。债券不一定马上带来大牛市，但在长端收益率升至较高水平后，其组合对冲价值和中期回报吸引力提升。股票内部，报告倾向寻找“Growth中的Value”和“Value中的Growth”：前者指盈利质量高但估值相对合理的成长股，后者指传统行业中具备结构性增长或资本回报改善的公司。对组合而言，单纯追逐过去涨幅最大的动量篮子风险上升，更合理的做法是降低拥挤度，保留AI主线但加入现金流、估值和分红约束。

风险与跟踪点：如果AI资本开支持续超预期、英伟达等核心公司继续大幅上修盈利，Momentum可能继续强势，债券吸引力被延后兑现。相反，如果油价和通胀上行推高利率、企业盈利下修或风险资产波动上升，动量股可能快速回撤。后续应跟踪美债10年和30年收益率、实际利率、AI CapEx指引、盈利修正广度、资金流向，以及Momentum组合与债券收益率的相关性。总体看，这份重复报告的价值在于强化同一结论：AI动量仍有基本面支撑，但组合管理需要从单一进攻转向更平衡的风险回报。

## Top of Mind Macro - Bond Selloff and Growth

文件：3.What's Top of Mind in Macro Research_ Sharp global bond selloff, Momentum rally, softer growth ahead(1).pdf

结论：这份宏观研究以访谈/问答形式讨论三条主线：全球债券急跌、Momentum股票强势反弹，以及未来增长可能放缓。报告的综合判断是，债券收益率上行背后既有再通胀背景，也有英国和日本长端利率压力向全球扩散的因素；Momentum上涨主要由AI交易和盈利预期推动，质量高于典型泡沫期；但全球增长动能在下半年可能走弱，投资者需要在AI结构性机会和宏观周期降温之间取得平衡。

关键数据：债券方面，报告认为如果没有明显宏观变化，全球债券收益率很难持续大幅逆转。美国和欧洲短期通胀仍偏高，除非霍尔木兹海峡能源流动改善、伊朗冲突缓和或通胀数据明显走低，否则利率下行空间有限。报告还指出，债券作为股票组合分散器的功能近期被削弱，股债收益率相关性达到1990年代以来最负的水平附近，说明传统60/40组合的对冲关系正在经历压力。与此同时，报告仍认为中期美债可以作为风险市场的对冲，因为风险资产中已经定价较多增长乐观预期，而通胀风险溢价也较高。

投资建议：Momentum方面，报告认为本轮反弹主要来自AI交易和盈利估计上修，与1999年或2021年单纯估值扩张不同。英伟达一季度结果说明AI投资繁荣尚无放缓迹象，但如果AI投资展望出现下修，Momentum可能发生快速catch-down。增长方面，报告预计美国下半年GDP年化增速约1.9%，低于上半年的2.1%；欧元区受能源影响会放缓，但德国财政扩张降低衰退风险；英国增长也预计转弱；中国二季度环比增长预计降至4.0%，低于一季度5.3%。因此资产配置上不能只押注AI成长，也要准备增长放缓和利率波动。

风险与跟踪点：报告建议寻找“Growth中的Value”和“Value中的Growth”，也就是避免拥挤动量，同时寻找估值尚未完全反映质量改善的资产。后续应跟踪全球长端收益率、油价和能源运输、AI资本开支、英伟达及云厂商订单、美国就业和消费、欧洲能源冲击、中国工业和消费数据。总体结论是：AI仍是最强结构性主题，但宏观环境并非无风险，债券急跌和增长降温可能让过去最拥挤的Momentum交易进入更挑剔阶段。

## Global Rates Notes - Treasury Yield Reversal Conditions

文件：4.Global Rates Notes_ US Treasury Valuations and Requirements for a Yield Reversal(1).pdf

结论：这份全球利率报告聚焦美国国债估值和收益率反转条件。核心判断是，30年期美债收益率持续突破5%后，长端利率虽然已经不便宜，但仅靠估值不足以触发持续性反弹；要让收益率真正下行，需要能源冲击缓和、增长和通胀数据转弱，或者风险资产压力显著上升。报告整体对未来收益率逐步下行持一定基准判断，但强调路径会取决于宏观催化，而不是因为债券“看起来便宜”就自动上涨。

关键数据：背景是全球长端收益率继续上行，美国、英国、日本等市场都在重新定价财政、通胀和央行路径。30年期美债收益率持续高于5%，利率市场也重新评估美联储政策路径。能源供给冲击带来通胀上行和增长下行的复杂组合，使得前端收益率相对GS的美联储基准路径偏高，但仍受到通胀定价和增长乐观支撑。报告指出，长期远期收益率相对公允价值略高，但并未达到极端便宜水平。市场对2027年3月FOMC前的定价比GS基准多出超过一次加息，而GS基准是假设到该会议仍有两次25bp降息。通胀定价方面，市场对2026年12月CPI的预期比GS高约20bp，对2027年12月高约50-60bp。

投资建议：报告提出三条收益率下行路径：第一，冲突缓和和石油流动恢复，降低能源通胀风险；第二，增长、劳动力市场或通胀数据更加鸽派，使市场重新定价降息；第三，估值便宜叠加风险资产压力，引发避险买盘。报告基准更看好前两条路径逐步发挥作用，并认为收益率回落可能由2-5年期引领，因为前端和中端对货币政策重新定价更敏感。对投资者而言，当前可以逐步关注美债配置价值，但不宜把长端债券当作无催化的确定性反弹交易。

风险与跟踪点：如果油价维持高位、通胀数据继续粘性、就业仍稳健，市场对美联储转鸽的定价会被推迟，长端收益率可能继续高位震荡甚至上行。另一个风险是财政赤字和期限溢价继续上升，使长端即便在增长放缓中也难以大幅下行。后续应跟踪能源运输、油价、核心PCE、就业、工资、ISM、财政供给和拍卖需求。总体看，报告建议从“等待催化”的角度做多债券，而不是单纯因为收益率突破5%就急于押注大幅反转。

---

## Oil Tracker - Stock Draws and China Weakness

文件：5.Oil Tracker_ Visible Stock Draws Accelerate on Lower Exports; Weakening China Imports and Demand(1).pdf

结论：这份Oil Tracker报告描绘了一个供需信号分化的油市：一方面，地缘冲突导致出口下降，全球可见库存大幅去化，物理市场明显偏紧；另一方面，中国进口和需求明显走弱，加上OECD战略储备释放，限制了Brent价格向上突破。报告的核心结论是，短期油品和原油现货基本面偏紧，但价格并未完全跟随库存收紧上涨，因为市场担心中国需求和潜在外交缓和削弱供给风险溢价。

关键数据：周度看，Brent和WTI近月价格基本横盘，原油一度回吐涨幅，原因是市场传出美国与伊朗谈判进入最后阶段。供给端非常紧张：霍尔木兹海峡相关石油出口按4日均值仅为正常水平的5%，伊朗石油装载按4日均值降至零，Kharg Island库存利用率超过80%。需求端，美国出行季开始，汽油、柴油和航煤需求有季节性支撑。全球可见库存去化加速，5月至今可见库存去化达到创纪录的870万桶/日；战争以来全球可见库存平均去化460万桶/日。不过由于战前库存缓冲较高，库存同比仍大致持平。5月库存去化约三分之二来自海上油库存下降，因为出口下降快于进口下降。欧洲航煤进口较2025年平均水平下降60%。

投资建议：报告对油价方向并非单边看多，而是强调“物理市场紧、宏观需求弱”的矛盾。若霍尔木兹和伊朗出口持续受限，柴油、汽油和航煤短缺风险会支持炼油利润和近月价差；但中国需求是主要拖累。中国原油和凝析油进口自2月27日以来下降430万桶/日，降幅38%，其中波斯湾来源贡献250万桶/日下降。上月中国进口下降还受到俄罗斯原油进口减少80万桶/日影响。官方中国炼厂加工量同比下降80万桶/日、降幅5.8%，达到疫情低位；GS经济学家数据显示，中国4月汽油及其他零售油品销售量同比下降22%。因此能源投资应更关注炼油产品短缺、区域价差和库存，而不是只看Brent绝对价格。

风险与跟踪点：上行风险来自冲突升级、海峡运输继续受阻、伊朗出口长期中断、美国夏季需求超预期；下行风险来自美伊谈判缓和、中国需求继续恶化、OECD释放SPR和全球增长放缓。后续应跟踪霍尔木兹出口、伊朗装船、Kharg库存、全球可见库存、海上油、欧洲航煤进口、中国炼厂开工和零售油品销售。总体看，报告提示油市短期不能被表面价格横盘误导，底层库存和物流数据已经非常紧，但中国需求疲弱让价格上行更依赖地缘风险持续。

---

## Japan Components - Nvidia Read-across Winners

文件：9.Japan Electronic Components_Semiconductors_ NVDA results read-across_ bullish on Ibiden, Murata, Yuden, Renesas, MARUWA(1)(1).pdf

结论：这份报告将英伟达强劲业绩和指引映射到日本电子零部件与半导体供应链，结论偏积极，重点看好Ibiden、Murata、Taiyo Yuden、Renesas和MARUWA。报告逻辑是，英伟达Data Center持续超预期、Vera Rubin平台下半年开始生产出货、Blackwell/Rubin 2025-2027年销售目标仍具可信度，将继续拉动ABF载板、MLCC、电源管理IC、陶瓷散热/绝缘材料等日本供应链需求。

关键数据：英伟达本季度收入US$81.6bn，环比增长20%，高于GS预测US$80.0bn、市场一致预期US$78.9bn以及公司指引中值US$78.0bn。下一季度收入指引US$91.0bn，高于GS预测US$87.7bn和市场预期US$86.3bn。这将是英伟达连续第15个季度收入增长，主要由Data Center驱动。Vera Rubin预计从三季度开始在下半年生产出货，报告对2025-2027年Blackwell/Rubin累计US$1tn销售保持信心。此外，英伟达对standalone CPU销售至少US$20bn有可见度，Vera CPU打开约US$200bn市场。

投资建议：具体公司方面，Ibiden被列为Buy，报告强调其电子业务计划到FY3/27、FY3/28、FY3/31销售分别达到JPY330bn、JPY460bn、JPY800bn，营业利润率分别为23%、29%、35%，相比FY3/26销售JPY243.3bn、OPM 19%显著提升，且需要进一步扩产。Murata为Buy CL，Taiyo Yuden为Buy，受益AI服务器MLCC需求；Murata将AI服务器MLCC需求CAGR从+30%上调至+80%，并增加JPY80bn产能，到FY3/28产能提升20%-25%；Taiyo Yuden预计FY3/27 AI服务器销售同比增长80%。Renesas为Buy，英伟达相关PMIC份额约三分之一至二分之一，ASIC PMIC也在扩展，AI相关收入同比翻倍且供给受限，正在提升内部产能。MARUWA为Buy，新工厂下半年贡献，AI销售预计同比翻倍以上。

风险与跟踪点：该报告的投资含义是，英伟达强劲并不只利好美国半导体，还会沿着先进封装、被动元件、电源管理和散热材料传导到日本上游。风险包括AI服务器需求波动、Blackwell/Rubin平台时点延后、供应瓶颈无法按计划扩产、客户议价压缩利润率，以及ASIC替代改变零组件规格。后续应跟踪英伟达平台出货、Ibiden扩产、Murata和Taiyo Yuden AI MLCC订单、Renesas PMIC供给、MARUWA新厂爬坡。总体结论：日本电子零部件链仍是AI硬件扩张的高质量二阶受益方向，尤其适合寻找英伟达之外的AI供应链弹性。

## 2026-05-24 51份PDF投行式系统总结

Piao，

我已整理今天 2026-05-24 23:24-23:26 通过“文件传输助手”收到的 51 份 PDF，并按顶级投行分析师口径生成系统总结。完整逐篇报告已作为附件放在本草稿中。

核心结论：

1. 这批 PDF 的主线非常清晰：AI 基础设施仍是最强 alpha 来源，但宏观环境正在变差，主要压力来自油价、通胀和长端利率。
2. 最值得跟踪的不是泛 AI 概念，而是 AI 的物理瓶颈层：GPU/CPU、XPU、网络、PCB/CCL、铜箔、光纤、数据中心电力、冷却、发电机、SOFC、特种晶圆厂、云和 MaaS 变现。
3. 报告中最积极的方向集中在 NVDA、AVGO、BABA、Tencent、Hon Hai、Elite Material、Co-Tech、Hua Hong、Biren、Meitu、MiniMax、Weichai、Fujikura，以及日本 AI 服务器供应链相关公司。
4. Kioxia 基本面很强，但原报告维持 Neutral，因为 NAND 周期高点和估值扩张空间仍有争议。
5. 软件板块不是全面买入，而是强调选股：优先有架构型护城河、数据平台、安全、垂直流程、基础设施控制能力的公司。
6. 宏观层面，多个报告都提示：美股创新高主要靠 AI 和盈利上修，但如果长端利率继续无序上行，AI/momentum 交易会面临回撤风险。
7. 油品短缺风险仍未完全消除。若 Hormuz 问题持续，柴油/汽油需要需求破坏、SPR 释放和炼厂利用率提升才能避免库存降到临界水平。
8. 51 份中有 49 份成功抽取正文；2 份 Beijing summit 相关 PDF 加密，无法读取正文，报告中已单独标注。
