entries.body:
# Detailed Summary of PDFs Sent to WeChat 文件传输助手

Date reviewed: 2026-05-23 
Source folder: `G:\gs\wechat\xwechat_files\piao433402_6a39\msg\file\2026-05` 
Scope: 16 PDFs with timestamps on 2026-05-23. 
Note: “Advice” below means the recommendation, trade idea, or investment implication in the PDF. It is not personalized investment advice.

## Executive Synthesis

The day’s PDFs cluster around five major themes.

First, the AI infrastructure cycle remains the dominant equity and credit theme. Nvidia’s report reinforces the view that hyperscaler capex remains strong and economically sustainable. Samsung’s note argues memory supply remains tight, with HBM4 and long-term agreements supporting margins. The Caixin storage article shows the same theme arriving in China’s A-share market through CXMT/长鑫科技 and YMTC/长江存储, but also warns that peak-cycle memory profits can be dangerous to extrapolate. Alphabet, Spotify, NetEase, and the EM AI adoption note all frame AI as moving from infrastructure into applications, content, productivity, and operating leverage.

Second, energy shock risk is increasingly macro-relevant. The natural gas note sees China LNG demand rising into winter because inventories have moved down year-on-year. The Asia macro note says oil near US$100-110/bbl, weak Asian currencies, and rising inflation are forcing central banks to tighten or at least price tighter policy. China Matters also attributes part of China’s April industrial miss to the Iran/Middle East energy shock.

Third, rates are driving credit and macro strategy. The Global Credit Trader note says higher government bond yields mechanically reduce 2026 corporate credit total return forecasts, especially USD investment grade. The Fed balance sheet note argues that despite political pressure to shrink the balance sheet, the Fed is likely to keep an ample-reserves framework and only allow limited balance sheet erosion.

Fourth, China’s domestic economy remains bifurcated. China exports and high-tech/new energy manufacturing remain resilient, while consumption, property, infrastructure, and credit demand remain weak. The Caixin loan article and China Matters both describe this split from different angles: weak loan demand and weak domestic investment do not necessarily mean a sudden macro collapse, but they do show structural demand problems.

Fifth, the equity-specific recommendations are mostly constructive but increasingly hedged. Goldman reiterates Buy on GOOGL, Samsung, SPOT, NTES, and NVDA. At the same time, the GOAL Risk Keeper note says bullish sentiment is already very elevated, so investors should protect gains with put-spread collars in selected equity markets.

## 1. Caixin: 国产存储巨头闯关A股，超级周期下估值存争议

### Conclusion

The article argues that CXMT/长鑫科技 and YMTC/长江存储 are becoming the most important “pure-play” domestic memory semiconductor assets in China. Their IPO paths could reshape A-share market leadership, but valuation is deeply contested because memory remains a cyclical, capital-intensive industry. AI demand may extend the cycle, but it does not eliminate cyclicality.

### Key Data

- 长鑫科技 disclosed explosive 1H26 guidance: revenue of RMB110-120bn, up more than 600% year-on-year, and attributable net profit of RMB50-57bn.
- In 1Q26, 长鑫科技 revenue grew 719% year-on-year to RMB50.8bn, with net profit of RMB33.0bn versus a RMB2.8bn loss in the prior-year period.
- The company’s 1Q net profit is far above many existing 科创板 leaders and would place it among the top profit generators in the A-share market.
- Financial pressure remains material: accumulated uncovered losses of RMB36.6bn and long-term borrowings of RMB118.8bn.
- Planned IPO fundraising is RMB29.5bn, the largest planned 科创板 fundraising to date. Use of proceeds: RMB13.0bn for DRAM technology upgrade, RMB7.5bn for production-line technology upgrades, and RMB9.0bn for advanced memory research.
- 长鑫科技’s DRAM share was estimated at 7.67% in 4Q25, ranking No. 1 in China and No. 4 globally.
- 长江存储 reportedly exceeded RMB20bn revenue in 1Q26 and surpassed 10% global NAND share.
- Valuation views are extremely wide: optimistic investors discuss RMB3-4tn market value for 长鑫科技 and RMB2-3tn for 长江存储; a more cautious private-fund estimate puts 长鑫科技 fair value at RMB0.8-1.2tn; another framework gives RMB1.5-3.0tn using 15-25x forward P/E and 6-12x forward P/S.

### Investment Implications

The bullish case is scarcity plus policy support plus AI-driven memory demand plus国产替代. Domestic investors may price the companies as strategic hard-tech platforms rather than as ordinary cyclical memory stocks. If the IPOs are priced conservatively, early secondary-market performance could be very strong.

The cautious case is that 2026 may represent a “super-profit peak.” DRAM/NAND profits are historically cyclical, and current numbers may be inflated by DDR4 tightness, AI demand, and global supply discipline. A 2027-28 downturn could expose debt and capex pressure.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- HBM gap: overseas leaders already ship HBM2/HBM3 at scale; 长鑫科技’s ability to progress to HBM3 and more advanced HBM products is central to sustaining a premium valuation.
- Equipment dependence: lithography and high-end metrology equipment remain import-dependent.
- Liquidity drain: giant IPOs may pull capital away from existing AI, optical module, CPO, and semiconductor equipment names. One quoted estimate suggests 5-10% valuation compression in popular concept sectors around listing windows.
- A-share market cycle: concentrated mega-IPOs have historically sometimes appeared near bull-market peaks, though not necessarily as the direct cause.

## 2. Science, 21 May 2026

### Conclusion

This is a general science magazine issue, not an investment research report. The most relevant themes are infectious disease response, AI in education, biological defense systems, climate/ecology, and frontier technology.

### Key Content

- Ebola outbreak: Science reports a significant Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with spread into Uganda. Early figures in the article include more than 500 suspected cases and more than 130 deaths. The response is complicated because Bundibugyo is rare and lacks widely available diagnostics, treatments, and vaccines compared with the Zaire Ebola species.
- AI and higher education: A policy article argues that generative AI use and misuse require assessment reform in universities. The problem is not only cheating, but unequal access and a mismatch between old assessment methods and AI-enabled work.
- Shared pathogen defenses: A feature highlights that some human antiviral and immune defense mechanisms have deep evolutionary roots in ancient microbial battles with viruses.
- Wildlife and human mobility: Research/commentary emphasizes that human mobility data can improve ecological analysis of how people affect animal movement.
- Other research themes: exoplanet atmosphere asymmetry, sleep biology and dementia, plant heat sensing, carbon removal through enhanced alkalinity, and organic qubits for quantum computing.

### Data and Advice

No investment advice. The closest market-relevant read-through is that infectious disease diagnostics, outbreak surveillance, AI governance, and biotech/immunology remain active scientific frontiers.

## 3. New Scientist, 23 May 2026

### Conclusion

This is also a general science issue. It is useful for scientific awareness rather than investable recommendations.

### Key Content

- Seasonal immune rhythms: A pooled analysis of 96 randomized trials involving about 48,000 children suggests vaccine immune response may vary seasonally. The article cautions that this does not yet mean people should delay vaccination.
- Thwaites glacier: The issue warns that the Thwaites Eastern Ice Shelf is destabilizing. The shelf’s flow reportedly tripled between January 2020 and January 2026 to just over 2,000 meters per year, with further acceleration in recent months.
- Neanderthal dentistry: A 59,000-year-old molar from Siberia shows signs of deliberate drilling, potentially pushing evidence of dentistry far earlier than previously known.
- Mindset and resilience: The feature argues that reframing uncontrollable challenges can improve coping, with the practical point that a mindset need not be “more true” to be useful.
- Other themes: an Earth-like exoplanet, The Selfish Gene at 50, early containers as tools, wolf-dog hybrids, air pollution and ocean currents, and scientific naming.

### Data and Advice

No investment advice. Possible thematic relevance includes climate risk, healthcare timing, and science communication.

## 4. Caixin: 一年内新增贷款两度负增长，事出何因？

### Conclusion

China’s negative monthly new RMB loan growth is not just a one-month anomaly. It reflects weak household and corporate loan demand, a structural shift from loan financing to bond/equity financing, regulatory pressure on low-quality consumer/assist loans, and weaker heavy-industry capex needs. However, loans alone now understate total financing because direct financing is becoming more important.

### Key Data

- Monthly new RMB loans were negative twice in the past year: -RMB50bn in July 2025 and -RMB10bn in April 2026. Before that, a similar case had not occurred since July 2005.
- April 2026 household loans and enterprise loans excluding bill financing both posted their largest single-month contraction since data began in 2007.
- 2026 first four months social financing was RMB15.45tn, RMB893bn lower year-on-year.
- RMB loans to the real economy rose RMB8.5tn in the first four months, RMB1.29tn less than the prior year.
- Enterprise bond net financing was RMB1.5tn, up RMB739.3bn year-on-year; government bond financing was RMB4.45tn, down RMB399bn year-on-year; equity financing was RMB200.8bn, up RMB65.5bn.
- Since April 2025, direct financing share in new social financing rose from 5.5% to 11%, while indirect financing fell from 63.3% to 55.1%.
- April 2026 enterprise loans: corporate loans increased RMB390bn, but short-term loans fell RMB460bn, medium/long-term loans fell RMB410bn, and bill financing rose RMB1.24tn.
- Resident loans fell RMB786.9bn in April; medium/long-term loans, including mortgages, fell RMB340.8bn; short-term resident loans fell RMB446.2bn.
- Resident leverage ratio fell from 62.3% in 1Q24 to 59.0% in 1Q26; resident debt growth turned negative for the first time since 1995 according to cited data.

### Investment Implications

The article is cautious for banks’ traditional loan-growth model. Banks face asset scarcity, weak project demand, mortgage run-off, and rising consumer-loan risk. The more attractive financing demand is in technology, semiconductors, storage, and advanced manufacturing, but many of those firms either have strong cash flow or can access direct financing.

The read-through is more constructive for capital markets and bond/equity financing platforms than for old loan-volume growth. It also suggests that headline loan weakness should be interpreted alongside bond issuance, equity financing, and government bond timing.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- Ticket/bill financing may be used to “fill quotas,” masking weak real loan demand.
- Consumer loan tightening could push long-tail borrowers toward informal or high-cost funding if not phased carefully.
- Mortgage loans remain under pressure because early repayments and weak new-home sales offset new lending.
- Banks may compete aggressively for scarce high-quality tech and government-backed projects, pressuring loan yields.

## 5. Goldman Sachs Global Credit Trader: Rates Still in the Driver’s Seat

### Conclusion

Higher government bond yields have become the main headwind for 2026 credit total returns, especially in investment grade credit because duration is longer and spread cushion is thinner. Credit investors should distinguish between “good” yield increases caused by growth optimism and “bad” yield increases caused by inflation/policy risk.

### Key Data

- Hypothetical scenario assuming rates stay near current levels and spreads widen modestly:
 - USD IG 2026 total return forecast falls to about 1.3% versus 6.0% in the early-April forecast.
 - USD HY falls to about 3.5% versus 6.4%.
 - EUR IG falls to about 1.0% versus 1.8%.
 - EUR HY falls to about 1.3% versus 2.2%.
- USD HY May supply reached about US$21bn and EUR HY about EUR9bn, above the 2021 high watermark.
- USD IG May supply has been muted, especially when duration-adjusted: roughly one-third of the 2020 high and nearly 30% below the median since 2015.
- USD leveraged loan net supply is negative year-to-date, while EUR leveraged loan net supply is about EUR11bn.
- Current/forecast spread dashboard:
 - USD IG current 74bp, forecast 95bp in 2Q26, 92bp in 3Q26, 90bp in 4Q26.
 - USD HY current 268bp, forecast 335bp in 2Q26, 325bp in 3Q26, 315bp in 4Q26.
 - EUR IG current 90bp, forecast 120bp in 2Q26, 117bp in 3Q26, 114bp in 4Q26.
 - EUR HY current 270bp, forecast 375bp in 2Q26, 368bp in 3Q26, 360bp in 4Q26.
- 2026 issuance forecasts:
 - USD IG gross issuance US$2.1tn, net US$850bn.
 - USD HY gross issuance US$400bn, net US$160bn.
 - EUR IG gross issuance EUR850bn, net EUR265bn.
 - EUR HY gross issuance EUR125bn, net EUR60bn.

### Investment Advice and Relative Value

- Overweight USD credit versus EUR credit.
- In USD: slight preference for IG over HY due to valuation and below-potential growth forecasts.
- In EUR: prefer IG over HY because growth/inflation/monetary policy mix is more challenging.
- Prefer BBBs over higher-rated USD IG to capture additional spread.
- In EUR IG, prefer As over BBBs because of weaker growth.
- In HY, prefer BBs; underweight Bs in USD and underweight CCCs in EUR.
- Prefer HY bonds over leveraged loans because loans have software-sector exposure and sentiment risk from AI disruption.
- Prefer CLO mezzanine tranches versus leveraged loans; neutral senior CLOs versus USD IG; use CLO spread widening to add.
- Prefer Agency MBS versus IG corporates as a diversification benefit.
- Underweight AT1s versus EUR HY because downside tail risks and valuation cushion are unattractive.

### Risks and Watchpoints

If yields rise for inflation or policy-risk reasons, spreads could widen and total returns could deteriorate. If yields rise for growth reasons, spreads may remain range-bound and credit appetite can hold up. Supply risk remains relevant because AI and M&A financings are less seasonal and may arrive outside normal issuance windows.

## 6. Goldman Sachs Natural Gas Comment: China Destocking Suggests Higher LNG Imports Ahead of Winter

### Conclusion

China’s gas demand is weak, but inventories are still falling relative to last year. That means China may need to import more LNG over the summer and ahead of winter, supporting upside risks to both European TTF and Asian JKM gas prices, especially if Hormuz flow disruption normalizes later than expected.

### Key Data

- China April apparent gas demand was 379 Bcm/year, marginally down year-on-year and 8 Bcm/year below Goldman’s expectation.
- Weak industrial production, especially chemicals, contributed to weak gas demand. The chemicals sector is cited as about 40 Bcm/year or 29 mtpa of gas demand in 2023.
- Despite weak demand, April LNG imports remained far below last year, while domestic gas production and pipeline imports also missed expectations.
- Inventories moved down year-on-year for the first time in several years.
- Base TTF price forecasts: EUR44/MWh for 3Q26 and EUR40/MWh for 4Q26, equivalent to about US$14.90 and US$13.65/mmBtu.
- Upside scenario if Hormuz normalization is delayed to late July rather than late June: TTF could rise to EUR65/MWh in 3Q26 and EUR53/MWh in 4Q26.

### Investment Advice

Goldman recommends that natural gas consumers in Europe and Asia hedge 2026-27 winter gas price exposure. The note is not simply bullish because demand is strong; it is bullish because inventory rebuilding and LNG routing pressure could tighten the marginal market.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- Faster Hormuz normalization would reduce upside price pressure.
- LNG suppliers have postponed/skipped some maintenance, temporarily lifting global loadings, but the note argues this is not sustainable and has only slowed the decline in Northwest European LNG imports.
- Watch JKM-TTF spread: a strong premium incentivizes rerouting US LNG from the Atlantic to the Pacific.

## 7. Goldman Sachs Global Markets Analyst: Fed Balance Sheet Outlook

### Conclusion

The selection of Kevin Warsh as next Fed Chair increased market attention on balance sheet shrinkage, but Goldman thinks a meaningful reduction is unlikely. The Fed is expected to maintain the ample-reserves framework, allow reserves to drift modestly lower as a share of bank assets, and later resume trend-like growth to keep reserves stable.

### Key Data

- Since mid-2008, the Fed balance sheet grew by US$5.8tn, from 6.4% of GDP to about 21% today; the peak was near 36% in 2022.
- Fed UST holdings are about 14% of Treasuries outstanding, below the pre-GFC average of about 17%.
- Fed agency MBS holdings are about 22% of the agency MBS market.
- Goldman estimates equilibrium balance-sheet expansion need at about US$25bn/month: US$9bn/month for currency growth, US$11bn/month to keep pace with bank asset growth, and US$5bn/month for TGA growth.
- Goldman expects reserve management purchases to average US$5bn/month through 1Q27, taking reserves to about 11% of bank assets.
- After early 2027, Goldman expects RMPs to return to a trend-like US$25bn/month.
- Baseline implies UST purchases of US$20-25bn/month near term and US$35-40bn/month steady state after including MBS runoff reinvestment into USTs.

### Investment Implications

The note argues against expecting a large QT shock. Keeping the balance sheet stable would still allow reserves to decline as a share of bank assets. A return to aggressive runoff would be more disruptive, but Goldman thinks the hurdle is high because overshooting reserve scarcity can cause funding stress.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- Warsh and other officials may tolerate somewhat higher short-term funding-rate volatility to encourage banks to economize on reserves.
- Bank liquidity rule changes could reduce regulatory-induced reserve demand.
- Temporary non-reserve liabilities such as the TGA can create reserve volatility; better mitigation tools could allow a smaller buffer.
- Downside risk to Goldman’s balance-sheet path exists, but the note still sees meaningful shrinkage as unlikely.

## 8. Goldman Sachs Global Economics Comment: EM Technology Adoption and AI

### Conclusion

Emerging markets may adopt AI faster than Goldman previously assumed because low-cost and open-source models reduce barriers. AI may also allow EM economies to leapfrog in digital sectors and healthcare, producing upside risk to EM productivity and GDP growth.

### Key Data

- Goldman’s standing forecast assumes AI boosts annual EM productivity by 4% over the next decade on a gross basis, less than half the forecast uplift for developed markets.
- Microsoft data cited in the report shows EM AI adoption around 22% on average versus 37% in DMs.
- Global AI adoption is rising by roughly 5 percentage points per year, implying a current DM-EM lag of about 3 years, shorter than the 5-year lag in Goldman’s baseline.
- China adoption is expected to exceed 30% by 2030 and become fully adopted within 15 years.
- If EM adoption lags DM adoption by only 3 years, Goldman estimates a 6% boost to EM GDP over the next decade versus 4% in the current baseline.
- Cloud adoption gap is relatively small: 41% of EM businesses purchase cloud services, only slightly below DMs.
- If AI-enabled healthcare improvements reduce EM-DM healthcare gaps proportionally, Goldman illustrates a possible 5% cumulative uplift to EM labor supply.

### Investment Implications

No direct trade recommendation. The macro implication is positive for EM growth, especially countries with digital services, healthcare gaps, cloud adoption, and low-cost AI access. It also supports the idea that AI upside is not only a US mega-cap equity story.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- EM labor forces are more production-heavy and less exposed to white-collar automation than DM labor forces.
- Adoption surveys may be noisy and may underestimate major EM progress.
- The healthcare uplift is illustrative, not a base-case forecast.

## 9. Goldman Sachs Equity Research: Alphabet / GOOGL

### Conclusion

Goldman sees Alphabet’s recent events as confirming an “agentic AI” future across Search, , Gmail, Maps, Workspace, Cloud, Android, Pixel, and Gemini. The firm argues Alphabet’s distribution scale and compute scale remain underappreciated as AI monetization moves from infrastructure to platform and application layers.

### Key Data

- Rating: Buy.
- Price: US$388.91.
- 12-month price target: US$450.
- Upside: 15.7%.
- Market cap: US$4.8tn.
- 2026E revenue: US$422.5bn; 2027E revenue US$520.0bn; 2028E revenue US$623.4bn.
- 2026E EPS: US$13.73; 2028E EPS US$17.04.
- Gemini has over 900m MAUs.
- AI Overviews have more than 2.5bn MAUs; AI Mode more than 1bn MAUs.
- Search queries reached an all-time high in Q1.
- : 91% reach of US adults; No. 1 US TV streaming watch-time platform; 2bn+ Shorts views on TVs monthly.
- ad performance disclosed: 2.2x higher long-term ROAS versus linear TV, paid social, and streaming; 86% higher long-term ROAS versus paid social alone.
- Demand Gen campaigns are said to drive a 30% average increase in conversions.

### Product and Strategy Takeaways

- Gemini 3.5 Flash is positioned as lower-cost, high-efficiency, and 4x faster in output tokens per second than other leading frontier models.
- Gemini Spark is a personal AI agent for planning and executing tasks across Google first-party properties and later third-party integrations.
- Gemini Omni adds multimodal video generation.
- Android 17, Android XR glasses, Googlebook, and deeper Gemini integration point to a potential AI intelligence layer across devices.
- Universal Commerce Protocol and Universal Cart position Google for agentic commerce and lower shopping friction.
- is positioned as a creator-led commerce platform, not only a video platform.

### Investment Advice

Goldman reiterates Buy and a US$450 target. The investment thesis is that Alphabet can navigate the shift in Search while monetizing AI through distribution, compute scale, consumer applications, enterprise products, advertising tools, and commerce.

### Risks

Key risks include Search disruption, competition for ad dollars and product utility, changing media consumption, heavy AI investments depressing margins longer than expected, low shareholder returns, regulatory scrutiny, macro volatility, and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.

## 10. Goldman Sachs Equity Research: Samsung Electronics

### Conclusion

Samsung reiterated a positive outlook for memory supply/demand and pricing. Goldman remains constructive because memory shortages could intensify, HBM4 confidence is improving, long-term agreements could stabilize margins, and capacity allocation to HBM may worsen conventional memory scarcity.

### Key Data

- Rating: Buy on both common and preference shares.
- Common price: W299,500; 12-month PT W320,000; upside 6.8%.
- Preference price: W187,800; 12-month PT W245,000; upside 30.5%.
- 2026E revenue: W693.1tn.
- 2026E EBITDA: W405.5tn.
- 2026E EPS: W42,395.
- 2026E P/E: 7.1x; 2027E P/E 5.7x.
- 2026E FCF yield: 7.6%; 2027E 14.3%; 2028E 15.2%.
- Goldman expects 2026 industry DRAM bit demand growth of 25%.
- Conventional DRAM pricing expected to rise low-teens quarter-on-quarter in 3Q26 and mid-to-high single digits in 4Q26.
- Samsung memory capex expected to rise 28% year-on-year to W52tn.
- Samsung foundry capex expected to rise 129% year-on-year to W16tn.

### Investment Advice

Goldman reiterates Buy. Preference shares appear to have larger upside in the report. The note sees memory as the earnings driver, supported by LTAs, elevated pricing, HBM progress, and shareholder-return potential.

### Catalysts

- HBM4 crossover in 3Q26.
- Around half of HBM sales expected to be HBM4.
- Potential premium positioning in the most advanced HBM4 SKU.
- P4 cleanroom allocation toward 1c-based HBM4/HBM4E could reinforce conventional memory shortage.
- Taylor fab 2nm mass production expected in 2027.

### Risks

Downside risks include deterioration in memory supply/demand, sharp smartphone margin contraction, and mobile OLED market share loss.

## 11. Goldman Sachs GOAL Risk Keeper: Hedging Bullish Sentiment

### Conclusion

Market sentiment and call-option positioning have risen sharply. Goldman does not say to turn bearish outright, but argues that high sentiment reduces the odds of large further rallies and increases the usefulness of put-spread collars to protect gains.

### Key Data

- Goldman’s Risk Appetite Indicator rose to 1.1, the 99th percentile since 1991 and the highest since 2021.
- Historically, when RAI starts above 0.9, very positive and very negative returns become less likely, while small corrections become more frequent.
- Bullish option positioning has risen since March, led by US TMT, US Financials, and China equities.
- Attractive put-spread collar screens:
 - Taiwan/EWT: call positioning 92%, put strikes -2%/-17%, call strike +15%, price 1.3% of spot, max payout 12.1x.
 - US Materials/XLB: price 0.8%, max payout 12.8x.
 - US Technology/XLK: price 1.3%, max payout 10.0x.
 - China Internet/KWEB: price 1.4%, max payout 8.8x.
 - S&P 500/SPY: price 0.6%, max payout 15.7x.
 - US Energy/XLE: price 1.1%, max payout 9.6x.
- For markets with large 3-month rallies, put-spread collars screen attractively on KOSPI, Taiwan, MSCI EM, and Nikkei.

### Investment Advice

Use put-spread collars, especially where bullish call positioning is high and hedges are cheap relative to history. Asia strategists specifically recommend put-spread collars on KOSPI200 and TWSE.

### Risks

Collars cap upside. If strong macro and earnings conditions persist, markets can continue rising even from elevated sentiment levels. The note’s message is hedge, not sell everything.

## 12. Goldman Sachs Global Markets Daily: Asia Finding It Harder to Look Through the Energy Shock

### Conclusion

Asian growth has been more resilient than feared, partly because of inventories and AI-related exports, but inflation and FX pressure are rising. Central banks and rates markets can no longer simply assume the energy shock will fade quickly.

### Key Data

- Brent is cited in the US$100-110/bbl range.
- Philippines BSP hiked 25bp to 4.50% in April.
- Bank Indonesia surprised with a 50bp hike to 5.25%.
- Goldman expects:
 - BoK: two 25bp hikes in Q3 and Q4.
 - RBI: two 25bp hikes, both in Q4.
 - Taiwan CBC: two 12.5bp hikes in Q2 and Q4.
 - Thailand and Malaysia: on hold.
- Markets are pricing around five hikes for BoK and RBI, which Goldman sees as too aggressive.
- Korea current-account surplus forecast: 12.4% of GDP versus 6.6% in 2025.
- KOSPI is up 80% year-to-date, yet KRW has underperformed because foreigners sold about US$60bn of local equities year-to-date.
- Goldman forecasts USD/CNY at 6.50 on a 12-month view.

### Investment Advice

- Bearish near-term Asian rates markets, especially high yielders such as IDR, PHP, and INR, because markets can overshoot even if all priced hikes are not delivered.
- Expect THB curve steepening on stagflation concerns.
- Prefer tech-related currencies KRW, TWD, MYR, and SGD over energy-exposed PHP, INR, IDR, and THB.
- Best trade ideas listed include:
 - Stay short SGD/MYR, target 2.90, stop 3.30.
 - Stay long TRY/NGN/KZT equally weighted versus USD, total return target 7.5%.
 - Buy 3-month EUR/NOK call spreads.
 - Stay long USD/SEK, target 9.65.
 - Stay long 3y France/Spain/Italy vs OIS.
 - Stay long MSCI Korea and Taiwan versus short MSCI India/Philippines/Thailand, target 135, stop 115.
 - Stay short EUR/HUF, target 350, stop 372.
 - Stay long 3y SOFR swap spread.
 - 2s5s CAD steepener.
 - Stay short USD/EGP.
 - Stay long 5y5y EUR OIS-HICP.
 - Stay long 5y receivers on 3m 2s5s10s receiver fly.

### Risks and Watchpoints

- A rapid de-escalation in the Middle East could relieve oil and FX pressure.
- But even with normalization, Goldman’s commodity team expects Brent near US$90/bbl by year-end due to inventory rebuilding.
- KRW recovery depends on portfolio-flow improvement, not just export strength.

## 13. Goldman Sachs China Matters: Not Too Worried About the April Data Miss

### Conclusion

Goldman argues that China’s April data miss looks worse than the underlying economy. The economy remains bifurcated: strong exports and high-tech/new energy activity versus weak domestic demand, property, and traditional investment. The Iran/Middle East energy shock did hurt activity, but some of the April miss may be seasonal/statistical.

### Key Data

- Retail sales rose only 0.2% year-on-year in April.
- Fixed asset investment declined about 8% year-on-year in April.
- Industrial production slowed to 4.1% year-on-year versus 5.7% in March and 6.0% Bloomberg consensus.
- Goldman estimates about half of the 2pp IP miss came from the Middle East/Iran energy shock, especially chemicals and processed petroleum products.
- Exports rose 14.1% year-on-year in April.
- April activity showed continued strength in industrial robots, wind power, semiconductors, NEVs, smartphones, and mobile handsets.
- Consumer-goods trade-in policy pulled forward demand; home-appliance sales growth fell from +53% year-on-year last May to -15% in April.
- EV purchase tax rose from 0% to 5%, weighing on auto sales.
- Domestic auto sales volume growth fell from +16% year-on-year in 2Q25 to -18% in 1Q26.
- In April, EV sales rose 8% month-on-month seasonally adjusted, while ICE car sales fell 23%.
- Goldman expects sequential real GDP growth to slow from 5.3% qoq annualized in 1Q26 to 4.0% in 2Q26.

### Investment Implications

No direct trade. The report argues against overreacting to April data. Policy has room to support investment because local government special bond issuance slowed after a strong Q1, and much of the annual government bond quota remains unused.

### Watchpoints

- Exports: a material weakening, especially to low-income oil-importing EM destinations, would likely change policy thinking.
- Property: stabilization in tier-1 cities could improve confidence and capital markets. April existing-home prices in tier-1 cities increased month-on-month, but prior improvements faded.
- Energy adaptation: China is shifting from oil-sensitive consumption to EVs and high-speed rail. Electricity consumption rose 6.0% year-on-year in April, while petroleum product consumption reportedly fell 20% from March to April.

## 14. Goldman Sachs Equity Research: Spotify / SPOT

### Conclusion

Goldman came away positive from Spotify’s first Investor Day in four years. The core thesis is that Spotify can increase user lifetime value through personalization, product tiering, AI-driven creation/organization, ad scaling, and steady pricing power.

### Key Data

- Rating: Buy.
- Price: US$489.93.
- 12-month price target: US$600.
- Upside: 22.5%.
- 2026E revenue: EUR19.31bn; 2028E revenue EUR24.23bn.
- 2026E EBITDA: EUR2.84bn; 2028E EUR4.28bn.
- 2026E EPS: EUR13.11; 2028E EUR19.74.
- 2026E FCF yield: 4.1%; 2028E 5.5%.
- 2030 targets:
 - Mid-teens revenue CAGR from 2025-2030.
 - Gross margin 35-40%.
 - Operating margin above 20%.
 - Strong FCF growth.
 - 1bn MAUs.
- Long-term ambition remains 1bn subscribers, EUR100bn revenue, and gross margin above 40%.
- Temporary operating expense step-up: about EUR200m for marketing around new launches and R&D tied to strategic AI initiatives.
- Active advertisers grew 68% year-on-year in 1Q26.
- Sponsorship is the fastest-growing ad format, up 100% year-on-year.
- Spotify Ad Manager AI tools generated more than 20,000 ads for over 7,000 advertisers globally.

### Investment Advice

Goldman reiterates Buy and US$600 target. No immediate estimate changes, but management’s medium/long-term targets could support upward revisions if execution improves.

### Catalysts

- Premium price increases with careful churn management.
- New tiers and add-ons.
- Universal Music agreement for AI remixes/covers.
- Live Nation ticket benefits for Premium subscribers.
- Prompted Playlist expansion into podcasts and audiobooks.
- Ad business acceleration in 2H26 and double-digit growth beyond.

### Risks

Competition affecting MAUs, subscribers, engagement, and retention; price increases causing churn; failure to execute advertising opportunity; gross margin reversal from content costs or mix; increased investment weighing on operating margins.

## 15. Goldman Sachs Equity Research: NetEase / NTES

### Conclusion

Goldman views the post-result share-price weakness as overdone. The main surprise was record-high margin expansion, much of which Goldman thinks is structural due to payment-channel shift, lower iOS/Android channel fees, higher PC contribution, and early AI cost benefits.

### Key Data

- Rating: Buy.
- ADR price: US$116.82; 12-month PT US$166; upside 42.1%.
- HK price: HK$171.70; 12-month PT HK$260; upside 51.4%.
- 2026E revenue: RMB120.25bn.
- 2026E EBITDA: RMB50.0bn.
- 2026E EPS: US$9.54, raised from US$8.68.
- 2026E P/E: 12.1x; 2027E 11.0x; 2028E 10.2x.
- 2026E FCF yield: 8.7%; 2028E 10.1%.
- Net profit estimates for 2026-28 raised about 6%.
- Deferred revenue excluding Youdao rose 24% year-on-year in 1Q26.
- Group and Games & VAS gross margin reached record highs; Games & VAS gross margin around 75%.
- FWJ PC reached a record 3.9m concurrent users in March.
- Sea of Remnants expected to launch in 3Q26, with Goldman estimating RMB5.8bn+ first-12-month grossing.

### Investment Advice

Reiterate Buy. Goldman raises target prices to US$166/HK$260 from US$160/HK$250. At current prices, Goldman says the stock trades at about 11-12x 2026E P/E with high-teens operating profit growth and buyback/dividend support.

### Catalysts

- Sea of Remnants launch in 3Q26.
- Continued high-teens to 20% operating profit growth through the rest of the year.
- HK primary listing conversion and potential Southbound inclusion after migration.
- Strong legacy-game lifecycle management: FWJ, WWM, Tianxia.
- AI integration into game development workflow.

### Risks

Weak legacy-game performance; slower monetization ramp for new games; intense competition in games, e-commerce, education, and other business areas; rising content costs; near-term 2Q26 grossing pressure because 2026 confirmed pipeline is light and Ananta timeline remains unconfirmed.

## 16. Goldman Sachs Equity Research: Nvidia / NVDA

### Conclusion

Goldman sees Nvidia’s quarter, guidance, and capital returns as strengthening the case for stock outperformance. The key argument is that hyperscaler capex is increasingly sustainable because Nvidia is driving more than 70% annual token cost reductions while token prices stabilize or increase, improving customer unit economics.

### Key Data

- Rating: Buy.
- Price: US$223.47.
- 12-month PT raised to US$285 from US$250.
- Upside: 27.5%; total return including dividend about 28.0%.
- Revenue: US$81.6bn versus Goldman US$80.0bn and Street US$78.8bn.
- Data Center revenue: US$75.2bn versus Street US$73.1bn.
- Edge Computing revenue: US$6.4bn versus Street US$5.6bn.
- Gross margin: 75.0%.
- Operating margin: 65.9%.
- Non-GAAP EPS: US$1.87 versus Goldman US$1.79 and Street US$1.75/1.76.
- 2Q revenue guide: US$91.0bn midpoint versus Goldman US$87.7bn and Street US$86.1bn.
- 2Q implied non-GAAP EPS: US$2.06 versus Goldman US$1.97 and Street about US$1.92-1.94.
- Buyback authorization increased by US$80bn, in addition to US$39bn remaining; dividends/buybacks in quarter were US$20bn.
- Quarterly dividend raised to US$0.25 from US$0.01.
- Supply-chain purchase authorization increased to US$145bn.
- Management sees at least US$20bn standalone CPU revenue this year.
- Goldman raised EPS estimates by about 6%.
- 2026E revenue now US$410.9bn; 2027E US$635.1bn; 2028E US$790.0bn.
- 2026E EPS now US$9.50; 2027E US$15.25; 2028E US$19.50.
- PT methodology: 30x P/E on normalized EPS of US$9.50.

### Investment Advice

Goldman reiterates Buy and raises PT to US$285. The note expects the stock to trade modestly higher after the report and sees clearer outperformance potential over coming months.

### Read-Through

Nvidia’s guide is constructive for the broader digital semiconductor group, especially Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, and ARM. It supports the view that AI infrastructure spending remains strong.

### Catalysts

- Upside to hyperscaler capex forecasts.
- Rubin platform ramp in 2H, with initial Rubin revenue recognized in FY3Q.
- Potential upside to prior US$1tn Rubin/Blackwell revenue forecast.
- Standalone Vera CPU racks, LPX/Groq, and Rubin-CPX.
- Improved capital allocation may broaden investor confidence.

### Risks

AI infrastructure spending slowdown; share loss from competition; margin erosion from competition; supply constraints.

## Cross-Document Investment Map

### Most Direct Buy Calls

- NVDA: Buy, PT US$285, 27.5% upside.
- NTES/9999.HK: Buy, PT US$166/HK$260, 42.1%/51.4% upside.
- SPOT: Buy, PT US$600, 22.5% upside.
- GOOGL: Buy, PT US$450, 15.7% upside.
- Samsung common/pref: Buy, PT W320,000/W245,000, 6.8%/30.5% upside.

### Main Macro/Strategy Trades

- Hedge bullish equity sentiment with put-spread collars, especially US Materials, US Tech, US Energy, China equities, KOSPI200, and TWSE.
- In credit, prefer USD over EUR, IG over HY, HY bonds over leveraged loans, CLO mezz versus loans, and Agency MBS versus IG corporates.
- In Asia macro, remain bearish near-term Asian rates, especially IDR/PHP/INR; prefer tech-related currencies over energy-exposed currencies.
- Gas consumers in Europe and Asia should hedge 2026-27 winter gas price exposure.

### Highest-Risk Areas

- A-share memory IPO valuation risk: strong short-term scarcity, but significant cycle and HBM execution risk.
- Asian energy-importer FX/rates: oil shock and currency weakness can force policy tightening.
- Equity market sentiment: elevated risk appetite makes hedging more attractive.
- Traditional China credit demand: loan contraction, weak household leverage, and direct-financing substitution challenge banks.

## Global Oil Analyst: 库存与供应更新

entries.title: 《世俗哲学家》（海尔布罗纳）深度总结 — 从亚当·斯密到凯恩斯
entries.excerpt: 海尔布罗纳经济思想史经典（第7版），全球销量数百万册。 核心主张 伟大经济学家是"世俗哲学家"——将人类最世俗的活动（对财富的追求）纳入哲学框架，通过思想改变世界。凯恩斯："经济学家和政治哲学家的思想，无论对错，都比常人所了解的更具威力。统治了这个世界的正是它们，鲜有别的。" 群像 斯密（看不见的手）→ 马尔萨斯/李嘉
entries.body:
> 海尔布罗纳经济思想史经典（第7版），全球销量数百万册。

## 核心主张

伟大经济学家是"世俗哲学家"——将人类最世俗的活动（对财富的追求）纳入哲学框架，通过思想改变世界。凯恩斯：**"经济学家和政治哲学家的思想，无论对错，都比常人所了解的更具威力。统治了这个世界的正是它们，鲜有别的。"**

## 群像

斯密（看不见的手）→ 马尔萨斯/李嘉图（人口与地租的悲观科学）→ 马克思（资本主义的内在矛盾）→ 韦伯伦（有闲阶级与炫耀性消费）→ 凯恩斯（有效需求与政府干预）→ 熊彼特（创造性破坏）。

## 第7版主线：熊彼特的"社会愿景"

每位伟大经济学家在构建正式模型之前，都有一个**预分析性的社会认知框架（愿景）**。理解愿景才能解码经济思想为何在特定历史时期出现——这也是解读当前政策辩论（产业政策回归、AI 与劳动、财政主导）的钥匙。

## 最终章："经济学的终结？"

现代挑战（环境极限、不平等、全球化，如今再加上 AI）正在将经济学推向传统框架的边界——在 AI 驱动的经济变革背景下尤具现实意义。

entries.title: 《技术革命与金融资本》（卡洛塔·佩雷斯）深度总结 — AI周期的历史透镜
entries.excerpt: 卡洛塔·佩雷斯 2002 年经典（2025 湛庐再版），技术革命与金融资本互动的四阶段周期模型。 核心框架：四阶段周期 1. 爆发阶段——新技术集群涌现，获得初期资金 2. 狂热阶段——金融资本主导、与生产资本脱离，泡沫形成 3. 协调阶段——新范式主导，金融与生产资本重新结合，"黄金时代" 4. 成熟阶段——范式饱和
entries.body:
> 卡洛塔·佩雷斯 2002 年经典（2025 湛庐再版），技术革命与金融资本互动的四阶段周期模型。

## 核心框架：四阶段周期

1. **爆发阶段**——新技术集群涌现，获得初期资金
2. **狂热阶段**——金融资本主导、与生产资本脱离，泡沫形成
3. **协调阶段**——新范式主导，金融与生产资本重新结合，"黄金时代"
4. **成熟阶段**——范式饱和，回报下降

依据：工业革命以来 200 年经济史（运河、铁路、钢铁、汽车、信息技术五次革命）。

## AI 革命对框架的五大挑战（朱嘉明中文版序）

1. **周期大幅压缩**——智能手机→云计算→深度学习→ChatGPT，时间轴戏剧性缩短
2. **开源颠覆**——开源 AI 生态挑战以风险资本为核心的集中化创新假设
3. **资产轻型平台**——打破"生产资本地域扎根且缺乏流动性"的假设
4. **金融与生产资本边界模糊**——科技公司通过数据资产化扮演金融资本角色
5. **多元并行融资生态**——企业自我融资、开源基金会、国家 AI 战略投资共存

## 投资启示

关键问题：当前 AI 投资热潮处于**"狂热阶段"（泡沫风险）还是"协调阶段"前期（生产率收益真实落地）**？
周期压缩效应可能加速从投机到生产率扩散的转变——支持中期谨慎乐观。
可与本站宏观栏目的 AI capex 分析对照阅读：若 2027 年云厂 capex 出现"协调式"再定价，正是佩雷斯模型从狂热转协调的信号。

## Oil Tracker: 霍尔木兹流量仍低，供需双向风险

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-29

核心结论：布伦特$118/桶（周+17%，2022年6月以来最高）。霍尔木兹流量仅为正常4%，伊朗剩余储量仅12-22天，产量削减5月中旬将达150万桶/天。需求破坏显现：4月全球需求比2月弱360万桶/天。**阿联酋退出欧佩克**（2027年产能目标500万桶/天）。
- 情景：乐观Q4 $80；基准Q4 $90；不利5月$125/Q4 $100；严重不利5月$145/Q4 $120
可操作结论：买入非霍尔木兹地区敞口的深水/上游E&P；阿联酋扩产中期利好油服；维持能源股多头。

---

## USA: FOMC 维持利率不变；三票反对"宽松偏向"

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-29

核心结论：联邦基金利率维持3.5-3.75%。三位地区联储主席反对隐性宽松偏向；声明措辞转强硬（通胀"is"偏高）。高盛下次降息预测9月但概率下降。
可操作结论：债市应定价更长时间偏高的政策利率；2年期或维持4.0-4.2%区间。

---

## Private-Tech Tour 2026: 中国AI基础设施/量子/卫星/BCI/Robotaxi 十大要点

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-29

核心结论：4月20-28日走访6城18家私募科技公司。要点：(1)**超级节点（64→256/1,024 GPU）驱动中国800G+光模块2026年三位数增长**；(2)中国AI服务器以推理为主（开源模型主导）；(3)本地AI芯片三架构并进（GPGPU/ASIC/RPP），2H26推多模态训练芯片；(4)"十五五"目标2030年生成式AI渗透率90%；(5)Robotaxi 2026-27加速扩张并出海；(6)量子计算四条技术路线国产化率均高。
- TFLN（薄膜铌酸锂）芯片：400G/lane性能优于SiPh且成本更低（180nm成熟制程可造）——潜在颠覆技术
可操作结论：最可操作的近期主题是中国光学联网元器件（800G光模块、TFLN）；中期关注RPP芯片、Robotaxi、量子商业化。

---

## Top of Mind Issue 148: 私募信贷的裂缝

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-27

核心结论：私募信贷（~2万亿美元市场）因违约、NAV虚高与软件敞口担忧承压。四位专家（橡树马克斯、Ares阿鲁格提、马拉松理查兹、高盛莱南）一致认为无系统性风险，但分歧大：理查兹预计2027-29软件违约率峰值15%、损失率70-100%。
- 核心结构性担忧：**私募信贷23%是软件贷款**（vs 高收益债3%）——最易受AI颠覆的行业
- 部分非上市BDC赎回请求已超5%季度上限
可操作结论：偏向机构性策略（CLO/机会性信贷）而非非上市BDC；避免软件密集型直接借贷基金；另类资管巨头（Ares/Apollo/Blackstone）是长期受益者。

---

## US Economics Analyst: 能源成本、国际溢出与通胀前景

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-28

核心结论：再次上调美国通胀预测：2026年12月核心PCE 2.6%（两度上调）、headline PCE 3.4%。新增"外国能源成本溢出"渠道（贸易伙伴能源成本+65% vs 美国+40%，经进口价格传导核心PCE额外+0.1pp）。
- 油价情景：基准4-5月$100/Q4 $90；严重不利5月$145/Q4 $120（对应headline PCE 4.3%）
可操作结论：不支持近期降息；10年期4.0-4.3%区间；高收益利差有走阔风险需精选；继续持有石油生产商作为尾部对冲。

---

## SK Hynix: 财报后虚拟路演五大要点

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-29

评级：买入；目标价₩1,800,000（+38.5%）
核心结论：(1)供给紧张与有利定价将持续（PC/移动客户抢货、服务器库存下降）；(2)**HBM4量产 2H26 进度不变**；(3)**SOCAMM2已量产**——1cnm LPDDR5X 192GB，带宽2倍、功耗效率+75%，专为 Vera Rubin 设计；(4)capex 大幅增加（₩44/53/55万亿，2026-28E）但强度占比下降；(5)LTA长约谈判进行中。
- FY26E 市盈率仅 4.3 倍，CROCI 78%——"全球半导体最引人注目的价值/成长组合之一"
可操作结论：高信心买入。

---

## 三联生活周刊 2026年第15期：厂二代接班（杂志摘要）

Publisher: 三联生活周刊 | Date: 2026-04-28

核心内容：封面专题聚焦中国制造业家族企业代际交接：约5,800万户民营企业中80%+为家族企业，50/60后创始人集中进入传承期。三组案例（辣条品牌、莆田鞋企、顺德定制家具）+ 长江商学院"接力长江"项目专访。
投资视角：传承浪潮既是私募股权机会（现代化转型企业）也是风险（传承失败快速衰退）；受影响最大的是轻工制造。

---

## Weichai Power 潍柴动力 (000338.SZ): 1Q26 First Take

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-05-04

评级：买入（维持）
核心结论：1Q26净利33亿元（+14%，历史一季度新高），剔除汇率（-3亿）后核心利润超预期（费用管控：运营费用-15%）。毛利率环比+1.2ppt至21.4%，缓解折扣担忧。**LNG重卡份额升至55-57%**（行业+10%背景下量价齐升）。
- 最重要中期催化剂：**AIDC 电源业务**（大缸径柴油/燃气发电机组+SOFC）——若获中国云厂订单将显著拓宽收入（Generac/Bloom Energy 提供正面旁证）
可操作结论：维持买入；汇率担忧引发的回调均为买入机会。

entries.body:
> 本合集由 22 篇邮件研报解读合并而成（中文版），可用页内搜索定位。

## US Strategy Views: Higher Highs

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-20

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
评级：超配美股
目标价：标普500年底目标7,600点（当前约7,100点，上行空间约+7%）
核心结论：高盛维持美股看多立场，以人工智能驱动的每股盈利增长为核心依据，将标普500年底目标上调至7,600点。伊朗战争后的宽松情绪已将市场情绪指标推回正区间，企业回购授权创历史新高，财报季开局强劲。高盛预测2026年EPS增长12%、2027年10%，AI贡献2026年标普500约40%的EPS增长，是重塑指数盈利结构的战略性顺风因素。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- 标普500年底2026年目标：7,600点（当前约+7%）
- 2026年EPS增速：+12%；2027年：+10%
- 远期市盈率：21倍（与5年均值持平）
- AI对标普500 EPS增长贡献：约40%（2026年）
- 年初至今回购授权：4,220亿美元（创纪录步伐）
- 高盛情绪指标：+0.8（从3月底-0.9低点大幅回升）
- Q1 2026 EPS增速市场一致预期：+12%（2021年以来最强）

▶ 【详细分析】
核心逻辑是AI已成为足够大的企业盈利驱动因素，使指数能够抵御典型的宏观逆风。AI贡献2026年标普500约40%的EPS增长，即便更广泛的经济有所放缓，AI资本支出持续高涨也足以支撑指数。高盛测算远期市盈率为21倍，与5年均值相当。创纪录的4,220亿美元YTD回购授权为EPS增长提供机械性底部支撑。Q1财报季预计EPS增速+12%（2021年以来最强）。
- 基准情景：年底标普500达7,600点（EPS约$270，前向P/E约21倍）
- 乐观情景：油价进一步回落 + Q1财报超预期 → 7,900+
- 悲观情景：伊朗冲突重新升级或美联储鹰派意外 → 回调至6,500-6,800

▶ 【可操作结论】
维持美股多头仓位，优先配置AI/科技方向。目标7,600点。鉴于宽松行情速度较快且油价仍偏高，建议叠加3-5%下行保护（近期认沽期权）。

---

## China: Three Things in China

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-19

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
核心结论：中国Q1 GDP同比增长5.0%，超过市场4.8%的一致预期，3月工业生产+5.7%（超预期），但零售销售不及预期。Q1美元计价出口同比激增+14.7%，不过伊朗战争预计将拖累2026年全年中国出口量约-2个百分点。银行间流动性极为充裕，7天回购利率跌破央行政策利率1.40%，为潜在宽松或降准创造条件。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- Q1 2026年GDP：+5.0% YoY（市场预期4.8%）
- 3月工业生产：+5.7% YoY；3月零售销售：不及预期
- Q1美元计价出口：+14.7% YoY（3月+2.5%，受春节日历效应扭曲：1-2月+10pp、3月-8pp）
- 伊朗战争对出口量拖累：约-2pp（2026年全年）
- 3月PPI自2022年底以来首次转正

▶ 【详细分析】
伊朗冲突预计通过能源进口型新兴市场需求减弱（占中国出口约40%）和运费上涨拖累出口。货币政策方面流动性极度充裕，为央行降准或降息创造空间。PPI转正是温和再通胀的初步信号。
- 基准情景：2026年全年GDP增长约5%；若Q2数据不及预期，央行可能降准或降息

▶ 【可操作结论】
Q1 GDP超预期对中国风险资产有正面支撑。MXCN估值仍便宜（12个月远期市盈率11.3倍），盈利上调、PPI转正、流动性充裕。聚焦出口多元化且受益于政策宽松的内需消费标的，关注5-6月出口数据及央行宽松信号。

---

## Japan Automobiles: Lowering GSe/TPs

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-20

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
评级：丰田（买入）、本田（买入）、斯巴鲁（买入）、日产（中性）、马自达（中性）、三菱汽车（卖出）
目标价（下调后）：丰田¥3,900 | 本田¥1,800 | 斯巴鲁¥3,800 | 日产¥390 | 马自达¥1,200 | 三菱¥330
核心结论：高盛下调日本汽车业盈利预测，反映三大逆风：(1)石脑油、铝及内存芯片价格上涨的原材料成本增加；(2)中东冲突宏观不确定性压制需求；(3)FY3/27实际税率上升。预计覆盖整车厂合计营业利润FY3/27同比下降16%，比IFIS一致预期低12%。FY3/28展望更乐观，OPM从4.8%恢复至6.9%。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- FY3/27营业利润修正：-16%；较IFIS一致预期低-12%
- 原材料成本逆风：拖累OPM约-3个百分点（石脑油/铝+15-20%/AI竞争DRAM产能致内存涨价）
- FY3/27E OPM：4.8%；FY3/28恢复至6.9%

▶ 【可操作结论】
维持丰田、本田、斯巴鲁买入，FY3/28 OPM恢复蕴含显著上行。回避三菱汽车（卖出）。FY3/27与一致预期仍有-12%差距，市场预期尚未充分调整。

---

## Apple (AAPL) F2Q26 Preview

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-20

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
评级：买入；目标价$330（12个月，隐含+22.1%）
核心结论：以服务业务增长、毛利率超预期及AI驱动需求催化剂（iPhone Fold）为依据。F2Q26E EPS $2.00（超一致预期$1.93），FY26E收入$471.3bn（+13.2%），EPS $8.70（+16.5%）。市值约$4.0万亿。iPhone Fold（2026秋发布）和WWDC AI Siri是重要催化剂。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- FY26E收入$471.3bn / EPS $8.70；FY27E EPS $9.41；FY28E EPS $10.19
- 服务收入增速+14% YoY，服务毛利率72-74% vs 硬件约40%
- FY26E自由现金流$140.4bn
- DRAM短缺：苹果凭规模锁定供应合同获得优先权

▶ 【详细分析】
WWDC 2026预计带来重大Siri AI升级，可能触发FY27显著换机潮。更大催化剂是2026秋iPhone Fold——高盛认为可能触发自iPhone X以来最大硬件升级周期，定价$1,500-2,000+。
- 乐观情景：Fold超预期+服务加速→FY27 EPS $10.5+→$370+
- 悲观情景：DRAM短缺扰乱供应→FY26 EPS $8.00-8.20→回调至$270

▶ 【可操作结论】
财报前买入，目标$330。iPhone Fold是未来12-18个月的期权价值，一致预期尚未充分反映。6月WWDC前买入。

---

## China Weekly Kickstart

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-18

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
评级：对中国股市持建设性态度；能源板块上调至标配，食品饮料下调至低配
核心结论：中国股市本周强劲（MXCN+2.4%，沪深300+2.0%），受Q1 GDP超预期、PPI转正、南下资金强劲流入（本周33亿美元）支撑。MXCN 11.3倍12个月远期市盈率仍具吸引力。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- MXCN 2026/27E EPS增速：+17%/+17%；沪深300：+23%/+13%
- 南下资金YTD净流入：310亿美元
- MXCN 11.3倍远期P/E vs 标普500的21倍，折扣46%

▶ 【可操作结论】
超配AI/科技，增加能源至标配，减配食品饮料。关注南下资金和5月中美峰会。MXCN 11.3倍P/E叠加+17%盈利增速，是全球范围内最佳风险回报选项之一。

---

## China Consumer Durables: Appliance Tracker Mar 2026

Publisher: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research | Date: 2026-04-20

▶ 【核心结论与投资建议】
评级：美的集团（A/H）买入；九号公司买入
核心结论：3月家电数据分化：国内空调出货+6% YoY（补库+4月1日涨价前备货），出口-10% YoY（春节错位+中东不确定性）。看好美的（股东回报+海外扩张）和九号公司（割草机器人需求接近+100% YoY、市场份额+5pp）。

▶ 【关键数据速览】
- 美的空调3月总量+7%（国内+18%，出口-3%）；格力-9%（出口-30%）
- 割草机器人需求（Sensor Tower）：3月接近+100% YoY

▶ 【可操作结论】
买入美的（下行保护+上行空间）；买入九号公司（结构性成长+估值近历史低位）；对格力谨慎（出口最差且海外多元化有限）。

---

## Taiwan CCL/PCB: 2H 进一步涨价可期

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-18

评级：买入 EMC、TUC、ZDT、GCE；目标价全线上调约15%（EMC NT$4,020 | TUC NT$1,165 | ZDT NT$338 | GCE NT$1,380）
核心结论：供应链调研确认 CCL/PCB 定价 2026年4月环比 +10-40%+，2H26 及 2027 还有量级相当的新一轮涨价。CSP 愿意接受涨价换产能保障。AI PCB/CCL 占前五大 CSP capex 从 0.1-1.2% → 2027E 3.3%/2.2%。EPS 预测上调 17-29%。
- 规格升级：3+N+3 HDI（26+层）→ 6+N+6/9+N+9 HDI（30+层）于 2H27-2028 实施，带来另一轮单价溢价
- TUC 2028E EPS 上调幅度最大（+25%），CCL 涨价杠杆最强
可操作结论：多年期结构性故事，2027 年是最有说服力的盈利拐点年；重点关注提前投资 HDI 产能的公司。

---

## China Property Weekly Wrap: Week 16

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-21

评级：对优质国有开发商持建设性立场；金茂（0817.HK，买入）为本周领涨标的
核心结论：第16周新房周环比+16%、同比+5%；二手房周环比+19%、同比+11%，双双同比正增长。价格稳定（成交价周环比+1%），新增供应同比-23%。4月百强开发商合同销售预计同比-11%（3月-19%，降幅明显收窄）。市场持续企稳但尚未进入自我维持复苏。
- 库存月数29.3；港股/A股平均NAV折让28%/18%
- 政策：财政部/住建部城市更新单城8-12亿元；地方公积金改革+人才购房补贴
可操作结论：精选优质国有开发商；二手房同比+11%是一手复苏时机的最佳领先指标；等待4月底销售数据确认改善趋势。

---

## Global Markets Comment: Beyond Relief — 跨资产视角

Publisher: Goldman Sachs | Date: 2026-04-19

核心结论：伊朗停火后市场已正确定价"宽松情景"（复苏与高盛情景相关性>80%），但油价仍比战前高30%+、债券收益率仍高于战前。快速宽松行情后下行尾部风险再度被低估，建议维持甚至增加对冲。
- 战后结构性背景：增长更低、通胀更高、长期油价更高、政策利率小幅偏高——对科技相对友好（AI支出与油价相关性低）
